title.zh: 卷五十六 列傳第五十 侯景
title.raw: 卷五十六 列傳第五十 侯景 Volume 56: Hou Jing

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第五十六 列傳第五十

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 56, Biography 50
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 56, Biography 50

sentences.zh: 臣聞股肱體合，則四海和平；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when the limbs and trunk function as one, the four seas are at peace;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when the body and its limbs move as one, the realm is at peace;

sentences.zh: 上下猜貳，則封疆幅裂。

translations.literal: when superiors and subordinates harbor mutual suspicion and divided loyalty, the borders are torn asunder.
translations.idiomatic: when those above and below doubt one another, the frontiers split apart.

sentences.zh: 故周、邵同德，越常之貢來臻；

translations.literal: Thus when the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao shared one virtue, the tribute of Yuechang arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao stood together in virtue, distant Yuechang sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 飛、惡離心，諸侯所以背叛。

translations.literal: When Fei and E turned their hearts away from each other, the feudal lords rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Fei and E fell out, the lords turned against their king.

sentences.zh: 此蓋成敗之所由，古今如畫一者也。

translations.literal: This is surely the cause of success or failure—true in ancient times as in our own, as if traced with one brushstroke.
translations.idiomatic: This is what decides triumph and ruin—the same in every age, as though drawn with a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 臣昔與魏丞相高王並肩戮力，共平災釁，扶危戴主，匡弼社稷。

translations.literal: Long ago I stood shoulder to shoulder with Grand Chancellor Prince Gao of Wei, exerting our strength together to quell disasters and calamities, supporting the endangered sovereign and bearing him aloft, bolstering the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Once I fought side by side with Wei's Grand Chancellor Prince Gao to put down rebellion, save the throne, and uphold the realm.

sentences.zh: 中興以後，無役不從；

translations.literal: After the restoration, there was no campaign from which I was absent;
translations.idiomatic: Since the restoration I have joined every campaign;

sentences.zh: 天平及此，有事先出。

translations.literal: and from the Tianping era until now, whenever action was needed I went out first.
translations.idiomatic: and from the Tianping era onward I have always been first into the field.

sentences.zh: 攻城每陷，野戰必殄；

translations.literal: In sieges I always took the cities; in field battles I always annihilated the foe.
translations.idiomatic: Every siege fell; every battle ended in the enemy's destruction.

sentences.zh: 筋力消於鞍甲，忠貞竭於寸心。

translations.literal: My sinews and strength were consumed upon saddle and armor; loyalty and constancy were drained to the last inch of my heart.
translations.idiomatic: I wore out my body in saddle and mail and spent every ounce of loyalty I had.

sentences.zh: 乘藉機運，位階鼎輔；

translations.literal: Riding the tide of opportunity, I rose to the rank of chief minister beside the tripod;
translations.idiomatic: Fortune raised me to stand beside the throne as chief minister;

sentences.zh: 宜應誓死罄節，仰報時恩，隕首流腸，溘焉罔貳。

translations.literal: I ought by rights to have sworn to die and exhaust my integrity, repaying in full the grace of my times—head smashed, entrails spilled, passing without a second thought.
translations.idiomatic: I should have sworn to die where honor required, repaying every debt with my life and never wavering.

sentences.zh: 何言翰墨，一旦論此？

translations.literal: How then to speak of ink and brush, and in a single day set forth such things?
translations.idiomatic: Why must I put this to writing, all at once, on a day like this?

sentences.zh: 臣所恨義非死所，壯士弗爲。

translations.literal: What I regret is that righteousness finds no place for my death—a thing no true warrior would undertake.
translations.idiomatic: What grieves me is that there is no honorable place left for me to die—the sort of death no true man would choose.

sentences.zh: 臣不愛命，但恐死之無益耳。

translations.literal: I do not cherish my life, but I fear dying to no purpose.
translations.idiomatic: I do not cling to life; I only fear that death would accomplish nothing.

sentences.zh: 而丞相旣遭疾患，政出子澄。

translations.literal: Yet the Grand Chancellor has fallen ill, and government passes to his son Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: But the Grand Chancellor is ill, and power has passed to his son Cheng.

sentences.zh: 澄天性險忌，觸類猜嫉，諂諛迭進，共相構毀。

translations.literal: Cheng is by nature devious and jealous; at every turn he suspects and envies. Fawners and flatterers advance in succession, joining to fabricate slanders.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng is suspicious and cruel by nature. Flatterers crowd in one after another and together weave false accusations.

sentences.zh: 而部分未周，累信賜召；

translations.literal: Though my preparations were not yet complete, repeated letters summoned me—
translations.idiomatic: Before my plans were fully laid, letter after letter summoned me—

sentences.zh: 不顧社稷之安危，惟恐私門之不植。

translations.literal: heedless of the altars' safety or peril, concerned only that his private faction not take root.
translations.idiomatic: indifferent to the realm's safety, caring only to secure his own house.

sentences.zh: 甘言厚幣，規滅忠梗。

translations.literal: With sweet words and rich gifts he plotted to destroy the loyal and upright.
translations.idiomatic: With honeyed speech and heavy bribes he sought to destroy every loyal man.

sentences.zh: 其父若殞，將何賜容。

translations.literal: If his father should die, how would he still grant me a place?
translations.idiomatic: If his father dies, what place will he leave for me?

sentences.zh: 懼讒畏戮，拒而不返，遂觀兵汝、潁，擁斾周、韓。

translations.literal: Fearing slander and dreading execution, I refused to return. Thereupon I reviewed troops at the Ru and Ying rivers and raised banners across Zhou and Han territory.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid of false charges and of being killed, I would not go back. I gathered my army on the Ru and Ying and marched under my banners through Zhou and Han.

sentences.zh: 乃與豫州刺史高成、廣州刺史郎椿、襄州刺史李密、兗州刺史邢子才、南兗州刺史石長宣、齊州刺史許季良、東豫州刺史丘元征、洛州刺史朱渾願、揚州刺史樂恂、北荊州刺史梅季昌、北揚州刺史元神和等，皆河南牧伯，大州帥長，各陰結私圖，剋相影會，秣馬潛戈，待時卽發。

translations.literal: In league with Inspector of Yuzhou Gao Cheng, Inspector of Guangzhou Lang Chun, Inspector of Xiangzhou Li Mi, Inspector of Yanzhou Xing Zicai, Inspector of South Yanzhou Shi Changxuan, Inspector of Qizhou Xu Jiliang, Inspector of East Yuzhou Qiu Yuanzheng, Inspector of Luozhou Zhu Hunyuan, Inspector of Yangzhou Le Xun, Inspector of North Jingzhou Mei Jichang, Inspector of North Yangzhou Yuan Yuanhe, and others—all governors of Henan, chiefs of great provinces—each secretly forming private designs, meeting like shadows at an appointed hour, feeding horses and hiding weapons, awaiting the moment to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the inspectors Gao Cheng of Yuzhou, Lang Chun of Guangzhou, Li Mi of Xiangzhou, Xing Zicai of Yanzhou, Shi Changxuan of South Yanzhou, Xu Jiliang of Qizhou, Qiu Yuanzheng of East Yuzhou, Zhu Hunyuan of Luozhou, Le Xun of Yangzhou, Mei Jichang of North Jingzhou, Yuan Yuanhe of North Yangzhou, and other great lords of Henan, each has made secret plans, matched his timing to the rest, readied horses and hidden arms, and waits only for the signal to rise.

sentences.zh: 函谷以東，瑕丘以西，咸願歸誠聖朝，息肩有道，戮力同心，死無二志。

translations.literal: East of Hangu Pass, west of Xiaqiu—all wish to submit in sincerity to the sacred court, rest their shoulders under righteous rule, join strength with one heart, dying without a second loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: From east of Hangu to west of Xiaqiu, all long to return to the imperial court, find rest under a righteous sovereign, and fight as one to the death.

sentences.zh: 惟有青、徐數州，僅須折簡，一驛走來，不勞經略。

translations.literal: Only Qing and Xu provinces need a folded letter—one post station's ride and they come, without need of grand strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Only Qing and Xu need a brief summons; one courier ride will bring them in, with no great campaign required.

sentences.zh: 且臣與高氏釁隙已成，臨患賜徵，前已不赴，縱其平復，終無合理。

translations.literal: Moreover my rift with the Gao clan is already fixed; when amid trouble they summoned me, I did not go before, and even if relations were mended, reconciliation would never be reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: My breach with the Gao house is already complete. They summoned me once in crisis and I refused; even if peace were restored, there would be no lasting trust.

sentences.zh: 黃河以南，臣之所職，易同反掌，附化不難。

translations.literal: South of the Yellow River is my command—turning it over is as easy as turning one's palm; winning them over is not difficult.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yellow River lies the territory under my command. To turn it over would be as easy as turning my hand; winning the people would not be hard.

sentences.zh: 羣臣顒仰，聽臣而唱。

translations.literal: The ministers look up with longing, waiting for me to lead the chorus.
translations.idiomatic: The officials look to me and wait for my signal.

sentences.zh: 若齊、宋一平，徐事燕、趙。

translations.literal: If Qi and Song are pacified in one stroke, Yan and Zhao can be handled afterwards.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qi and Song are settled, Yan and Zhao can be dealt with in turn.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下天網宏開，方同書軌，聞茲寸款，惟應霈然。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's heavenly net opens wide; the realm is becoming one script and one track. Hearing this brief sincerity, you should respond with outpouring grace.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's net of Heaven is broad, and the realm is moving toward unity. I beg you to receive this small pledge with overflowing mercy.

sentences.zh: 丁和旣至，高祖召羣臣廷議。

translations.literal: When Ding He arrived, Gaozu convened the ministers for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding He arrived, Gaozu called the ministers into court to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射謝舉及百辟等議，皆云納侯景非宜，高祖不從是議而納景。

translations.literal: Deputy Director of the Masters of Writing Xie Ju and the hundred officials deliberated—all said accepting Hou Jing was inadvisable; Gaozu did not follow that counsel and accepted Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Xie Ju and the whole court argued that taking Hou Jing in would be unwise. Gaozu rejected their advice and received him.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武卒，其子澄嗣，是爲文襄帝。

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu died, his son Cheng succeeded—this is Emperor Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan of Northern Qi died, his son Cheng succeeded him as Emperor Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃下詔封景河南王、大將軍、使持節、董督河南南北諸軍事、大行臺，承制輒行，如鄧禹故事，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Gaozu then issued an edict enfeoffing Jing as Prince of Henan, Great General, Bearer of the Staff with discretionary powers, Director Supervisor of military affairs north and south of Henan, Grand Commandery Platform, empowered to act on imperial mandate as in the precedent of Deng Yu, granted one suite of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then enfeoffed Jing as Prince of Henan and Great General, gave him the staff with full discretion, made him director of all military affairs north and south of the Yellow River, and set up a Grand Commandery Platform with authority to act on imperial mandate after the model of Deng Yu, along with one suite of martial music.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄遣大將軍慕容紹宗圍景於長社，景請西魏爲援，西魏遣其五城王元慶等率兵救之，紹宗乃退。

translations.literal: Qi Wenxiang sent Great General Murong Shaozong to besiege Jing at Changshe; Jing requested Western Wei aid; Western Wei sent its Prince of Wucheng Yuan Qing with troops to rescue; Shaozong then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxiang sent Great General Murong Shaozong to besiege Jing at Changshe. Jing asked Western Wei for help, and Western Wei sent Prince Yuan Qing of Wucheng with an army to relieve him. Shaozong then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 景復請兵於司州刺史羊鴉仁，鴉仁遣長史鄧鴻率兵至汝水，元慶軍又夜遁。

translations.literal: Jing again requested troops from Inspector of Sizhou Yang Yaren; Yaren sent Senior Clerk Deng Hong with troops to the Ru River; Yuan Qing's army fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Jing asked Inspector Yang Yaren of Sizhou for troops as well. Yaren sent Senior Clerk Deng Hong to the Ru River, and Yuan Qing's army fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 於是據懸瓠、項城，求遣刺史以鎮之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he held Xuanyong and Xiangcheng, requesting dispatch of governors to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: He then held Xuanyong and Xiangcheng and asked that inspectors be sent to garrison them.

sentences.zh: 詔以羊鴉仁爲豫、司二州刺史，移鎮懸瓠；

translations.literal: An edict made Yang Yaren Inspector of Yu and Si provinces, transferred to garrison Xuanyong;
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Yang Yaren inspector of Yu and Si and moved him to garrison Xuanyong;

sentences.zh: 西陽太守羊思建爲殷州刺史，鎮項城。

translations.literal: Administrator of Xiyang Yang Sijian made Inspector of Yin province, garrisoning Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: and made Yang Sijian, administrator of Xiyang, inspector of Yin with his seat at Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 魏旣新喪元帥，景又舉河南內附，齊文襄慮景與西、南合從，方爲己患，乃以書喻景曰：

translations.literal: Wei having just lost its commander, and Jing having offered Henan in submission, Qi Wenxiang feared Jing would ally with west and south, becoming his trouble, and sent a letter admonishing Jing:
translations.idiomatic: Wei had just lost its commander, and Jing had surrendered Henan to the Liang. Wenxiang feared that Jing would join forces with Western Wei and the Liang, and so he sent a letter to reason with him:

sentences.zh: 蓋聞位爲大寶，守之未易；

translations.literal: I have heard that position is the great treasure, and holding it is not easy;
translations.idiomatic: It is said that high rank is a great treasure, and to keep it is no easy thing;

sentences.zh: 仁誠重任，終之實難。

translations.literal: benevolence and sincerity are heavy burdens, and seeing them through is truly hard.
translations.idiomatic: and that duty and good faith are heavy charges, hard to carry to the end.

sentences.zh: 或殺身成名，或去食存信；

translations.literal: Some kill themselves to achieve fame, some forsake food to preserve faith;
translations.idiomatic: Some give their lives to preserve their name; some go hungry to keep their word;

sentences.zh: 比性命於鴻毛，等節義於熊掌。

translations.literal: they liken life to a goose feather and integrity to a bear's paw.
translations.idiomatic: they weigh life against a goose feather and honor against a bear's paw.

sentences.zh: 夫然者，舉不失德，動無過事；

translations.literal: When such is the case, every act loses no virtue, every move commits no fault;
translations.idiomatic: When men act thus, they keep their virtue intact and make no misstep;

sentences.zh: 進不見惡，退無謗言。

translations.literal: advancing, one meets no hatred; retreating, one bears no slander.
translations.idiomatic: going forward they earn no hatred; stepping back they leave no reproach.

sentences.zh: 先王與司徒契闊夷險，孤子相於，偏所眷屬，繾綣衿期，綢繆寤語，義貫終始，情存歲寒。

translations.literal: The former king and the Marshal shared hardship through distant perils; I treated you as a son, favoring you exclusively, binding our hearts in close affection, speaking in intimate counsel through the night—righteousness running from start to finish, affection enduring through the cold season.
translations.idiomatic: My father and you, Marshal, shared every danger together. I regarded you as one of my own and favored you above others, bound to you in close trust and long counsel. Our bond ran from beginning to end, and did not fade with the years.

sentences.zh: 司徒自少及長，從微至著，共相成生，非無恩德。

translations.literal: The Marshal from youth to age, from obscurity to prominence—we grew together; this was not without grace and merit.
translations.idiomatic: You, Marshal, rose from humble beginnings to great standing, and we grew up together. That history was not without kindness and reward.

sentences.zh: 旣爵冠通侯，位標上等，門容駟馬，室饗萬鐘，財利潤於鄉党，榮華被於親戚。

translations.literal: Already ennobled as Full Marquis, rank marked at the highest tier, gate worthy of four horses, hall feasting on ten thousand zhong—wealth enriching the village, glory covering kin.
translations.idiomatic: You were ennobled as a full marquis, given one of the highest ranks, a gate fit for four-horse carriages, and a household fed from ten thousand zhong. Wealth flowed to your kin, and honor spread through your clan.

sentences.zh: 意氣相傾，人倫所重，感於知己，義在忘軀。

translations.literal: Matching spirits, valued in human bonds, moved by one who knows you, righteousness lies in forgetting the self.
translations.idiomatic: Kindred souls are prized among men. When one finds a true patron, honor demands that he forget himself.

sentences.zh: 眷爲國士者，乃立漆身之節；

translations.literal: Those regarded as champions of the realm set the standard of lacquered body;
translations.idiomatic: A man honored as champion of the state will even lacquer his flesh for his lord;

sentences.zh: 饋以壺飱者，便致扶輪之效。

translations.literal: those given a basket of rice perform the service of supporting the wheel hub.
translations.idiomatic: and one who receives even a basket of food will repay it by bracing the chariot wheel.

sentences.zh: 若然尚不能已，況其重於此乎！

translations.literal: If even such things cannot be stopped, how much more weighty is this!
translations.idiomatic: If such obligations cannot be cast aside, how much heavier is the debt between us!

sentences.zh: 幸以故舊之義，欲持子孫相託，方爲秦晉之匹，共成劉范之親。

translations.literal: On the strength of old friendship, I wish to entrust my sons and grandsons to you, becoming match like Qin and Jin, forming kinship like Liu and Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Out of old friendship I would entrust my sons and grandsons to you, binding our houses like Qin and Jin, joining our fates like Liu and Fan.

sentences.zh: 假使日往月來，時移世易，門無強廕，家有幼孤，猶加璧不遺，分宅相濟，無忘先德，以恤後人。

translations.literal: Suppose days pass and months come, times shift and generations change; the gate lacks strong shade, the household has young orphans—still I would add jade bi without withholding, divide houses to aid, not forgetting former merit, to comfort those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: Even if time passed, fortunes turned, and my house were left with only weak protection and young orphans, I would still give jade without stint, share my home to help you, remember past kindness, and care for those who came after.

sentences.zh: 況聞負杖行歌，便已狼顧犬噬，於名無所成，於義無所取，不蹈忠臣之跡，自陷叛人之地。

translations.literal: Yet I hear you lean on your staff and walk singing, already glancing back like a wolf, biting like a dog—in name achieving nothing, in righteousness gaining nothing; not treading the path of loyal ministers, but casting yourself into the land of rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hear that you lean on your staff and sing as you walk, already looking back like a wolf and snapping like a dog. You win nothing in reputation and gain nothing in honor. You leave the path of loyal ministers and cast yourself among rebels.

sentences.zh: 力不足以自強，勢不足以自保；

translations.literal: Strength insufficient to strengthen yourself, momentum insufficient to protect yourself;
translations.idiomatic: You are not strong enough to stand alone, nor powerful enough to defend yourself;

sentences.zh: 率烏合之衆，爲累卵之危。

translations.literal: leading a motley crowd, placing yourself in danger like piled eggs.
translations.idiomatic: you lead a rabble and stand in peril as fragile as a tower of eggs.

sentences.zh: 西求救於黑泰，南請援於蕭氏，以狐疑之心，爲首鼠之事。

translations.literal: West you beg rescue from Heitai, south you ask aid from the Xiao clan—with a fox's suspicious heart, doing a first-and-last-mouse's deed.
translations.idiomatic: To the west you beg Yuwen Tai for help; to the south you ask the Xiao for rescue. With a wavering heart you play both sides at once.

sentences.zh: 入秦則秦人不容，歸吳則吳人不信。

translations.literal: Enter Qin and the Qin people will not hold you; return to Wu and the Wu people will not trust you.
translations.idiomatic: Go west and the westerners will not keep you; turn south and the southerners will not trust you.

sentences.zh: 當今相視，未見其可，不知終久，持此安歸。

translations.literal: Looking at the present together, none see it feasible; not knowing in the end how long you can hold this or where you will go.
translations.idiomatic: Seen clearly, none of this can succeed. In the end, how long can you hold on, and where will you go?

sentences.zh: 相推本心，必不應爾。

translations.literal: Pushing our hearts' true intent, you surely should not act thus.
translations.idiomatic: If you search your own heart, you cannot truly mean to go on like this.

sentences.zh: 當是不逞之人，曲爲口端之說，遂懷市虎之疑，乃致投杼之惑耳。

translations.literal: Surely this is one who cannot have his way, twisting words at the mouth, then harboring market-tiger suspicions, then falling into the delusion of casting away the pestle.
translations.idiomatic: Surely some schemer has twisted your ear, planted false rumors, and driven you into needless fear.

sentences.zh: 比來舉止，事已可見，人相疑誤，想自覺知，合門大小，並付司寇。

translations.literal: Recently your conduct has made things visible; people mutually suspect and err; I think you perceive this yourself. Your entire household, great and small, is handed over to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Your recent actions have already shown your intent, and everyone sees the mistake. I think you know it yourself. Your whole household, great and small, has been handed over to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 近者，聊命偏師，前驅致討，南兗、揚州，應時剋復。

translations.literal: Recently I merely ordered a detached division as vanguard to chastise; South Yan and Yangzhou were recovered as expected.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago I sent a vanguard force against you, and South Yan and Yangzhou fell back into our hands at once.

sentences.zh: 卽欲乘機，長驅懸瓠；

translations.literal: I intended to seize the moment and drive long-distance to Xuanyong;
translations.idiomatic: I meant to press on at once to Xuanyong;

sentences.zh: 屬以炎暑，欲爲後圖。

translations.literal: owing to the scorching heat, I plan for later.
translations.idiomatic: but the heat forced me to wait and plan for another day.

sentences.zh: 方憑國靈，龔行天罰，器械精新，士馬強盛。

translations.literal: Relying on the state's numinous power, I march Heaven's punishment; weapons refined and new, soldiers and horses strong and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Backed by the fortune of the state, I shall march under Heaven's judgment with fresh arms and strong horses.

sentences.zh: 內外感德，上下齊心，三令五申，可蹈湯火。

translations.literal: Inside and outside moved by virtue, above and below of one heart—three orders and five proclamations, one could tread boiling water and fire.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without answer to virtue, and high and low are of one mind. With repeated commands my men would walk through fire.

sentences.zh: 若使旗鼓相望，埃塵相接，勢如沃雪，事等注螢。

translations.literal: If banners and drums face each other, dust and ash connect, the momentum like pouring snow on boiling water, the affair like pouring water on fireflies.
translations.idiomatic: If our banners meet and our dust clouds join, your force will melt like snow on boiling water and fail like water poured on embers.

sentences.zh: 夫明者去危就安，智者轉禍爲福。

translations.literal: The clear-sighted leave danger for safety; the wise turn disaster into blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The clear-eyed leave danger for safety; the wise turn ruin into blessing.

sentences.zh: 寧使我負人，不使人負我。

translations.literal: Better that I wrong others than that others wrong me.
translations.idiomatic: Better that I wrong another than that another wrong me.

sentences.zh: 當開從善之門，決改先迷之路。

translations.literal: Open the gate of accepting good counsel; decisively change the path of former confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Open the door to good counsel and leave the road of your former error.

sentences.zh: 今刷心蕩意，除嫌去惡，想猶致疑，未便見信。

translations.literal: Now I wash my heart and clear my intent, removing suspicion and evil—I think you still harbor doubts and are not yet ready to believe.
translations.idiomatic: I speak now with a cleared heart and without malice. Yet I know you still doubt me and are not ready to believe.

sentences.zh: 若能卷甲來朝，垂櫜還闕者，當授豫州刺史。

translations.literal: If you can roll up your armor and come to court, hang your quiver and return to the palace, I will grant you Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: If you lay down your arms, come to court, and return in peace, I will make you inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 卽使終君之世，所部文武更不追攝。

translations.literal: Even for your whole lifetime, the civil and military under your command will not be pursued further.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest of your life none of the officers and soldiers once under you will be pursued.

sentences.zh: 進得保其祿位，退則不喪功名。

translations.literal: Advancing, you preserve rank and salary; retreating, you lose no fame and merit.
translations.idiomatic: Come forward and you keep your rank and pay; step back and you lose neither honor nor credit.

sentences.zh: 君門眷屬，可以無恙；

translations.literal: Your clan and kin at the gate can be unharmed;
translations.idiomatic: Your family at home may remain unharmed;

sentences.zh: 寵妻愛子，亦送相還。

translations.literal: cherished wife and beloved sons will also be sent back to you.
translations.idiomatic: your wife and children will be returned to you as well.

sentences.zh: 仍爲通家，卒成親好。

translations.literal: Still we become connected families, finally forming cordial friendship.
translations.idiomatic: We shall again be joined as one house and become close friends.

sentences.zh: 所不食言，有如皎日。

translations.literal: What I do not eat in word is as the bright sun.
translations.idiomatic: What I promise I do not break—my word is as clear as the sun.

sentences.zh: 君旣不能東封函谷，南向稱孤，受制於人，威名頓盡。

translations.literal: You could not seal Hangu eastward nor declare yourself sovereign southward; subject to others, your prestige and name are suddenly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: You could not hold Hangu in the east or rule in the south on your own. Now, dependent on others, your power and name are spent.

sentences.zh: 空使兄弟子侄，足首異門，垂發戴白，同之塗炭，聞者酸鼻，見者寒心，矧伊骨肉，能無愧也？

translations.literal: In vain your brothers, sons, and nephews—feet and heads in different gates, hair white before their time, sharing the same torment—hearers sour the nose, viewers chill the heart; how much more for blood kin—can there be no shame?
translations.idiomatic: Your brothers, sons, and nephews will be scattered to different fates, worn white before their time, and ruined alike. Those who hear of it will weep; those who see it will shudder. For your own flesh and blood, can there be no shame?

sentences.zh: 孤子今日不應方遣此書，但見蔡遵道云：司徒本無歸西之心，深有悔禍之意，聞西兵將至，遣遵道向崤中參其多少；

translations.literal: I should not today be sending this letter, but I saw Cai Zundao's report: the Marshal originally had no heart to go west, deeply regretted the calamity, heard Western troops were coming, sent Zunda to the Xiao Mountains to assess their numbers;
translations.idiomatic: I would not be writing this now, but Cai Zundao told me that you never truly meant to go west, that you deeply regretted what had happened, and that when you heard Western Wei was marching you sent Zundao into the Xiao Mountains to learn how many they were;

sentences.zh: 少則與其同力，多則更爲其備。

translations.literal: if few, join strength with them; if many, prepare further against them.
translations.idiomatic: if they were few, you would join them; if many, you would prepare against them.

sentences.zh: 又云：房長史在彼之日，司徒嘗欲遣書啓，將改過自新。

translations.literal: Also: when Senior Clerk Fang was there, the Marshal once wished to send a letter, intending to reform and renew himself.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that while Senior Clerk Fang was with you, you once meant to send a letter and turn back to the right path.

sentences.zh: 已差李龍仁，垂欲發遣，聞房已遠，遂復停發。

translations.literal: He had already dispatched Li Longren, about to send him off; hearing Fang was far away, he stopped the sending.
translations.idiomatic: You had already sent Li Longren and were about to dispatch him, but when you learned Fang was far away you halted the message.

sentences.zh: 未知遵道此言爲虛爲實，但旣有所聞，不容不相盡告。

translations.literal: I do not know whether Zundao's words are false or true, but having heard something, I cannot fail to tell you fully.
translations.idiomatic: I do not know whether Zundao spoke truth or falsehood, but since I have heard this I cannot keep it from you.

sentences.zh: 吉凶之理，想自圖之。

translations.literal: The logic of fortune and calamity—I think you should plot it yourself.
translations.idiomatic: The way fortune and ruin turn—surely you will judge that for yourself.

sentences.zh: 景報書曰：

translations.literal: Jing replied in a letter:
translations.idiomatic: Jing answered in a letter:

sentences.zh: 蓋聞立身揚名者，義也；

translations.literal: I have heard that establishing oneself and spreading one's name—that is righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: It is said that to stand with honor and leave a name behind is righteousness;

sentences.zh: 在躬所寶者，生也。

translations.literal: what one treasures in the person—that is life.
translations.idiomatic: and that what a man holds dear in his own body is life.

sentences.zh: 苟事當其義，則節士不愛其軀；

translations.literal: If the deed accords with righteousness, the man of integrity does not spare his body;
translations.idiomatic: When the cause is just, a man of honor does not spare himself;

sentences.zh: 刑罰斯舛，則君子實重其命。

translations.literal: when punishments are perverse, the gentleman truly cherishes his life.
translations.idiomatic: but when punishment is unjust, even a gentleman will guard his life.

sentences.zh: 昔微子發狂而去殷，陳平懷智而背楚者，良有以也。

translations.literal: In old times Weizi went mad and left Yin; Chen Ping harbored wisdom and betrayed Chu—there was good reason for this.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Weizi feigned madness and quit Yin; Chen Ping used his wit and turned from Chu. They had cause.

sentences.zh: 僕鄉曲布衣，本乖藝用。

translations.literal: I am a common cloth-clad man of the countryside, by nature unsuited to arts and utility.
translations.idiomatic: I am a plain countryman, ill suited by nature to polished arts.

sentences.zh: 初逢天柱，賜忝帷幄之謀；

translations.literal: At first meeting the Heavenly Pillar, I was graced with counsel in the command tent;
translations.idiomatic: When I first met the Heavenly Pillar, I was honored with a place in the command tent;

sentences.zh: 晚遇永熙，委以干戈之任。

translations.literal: late encountering Yongxi, I was entrusted with the charge of arms.
translations.idiomatic: and later, in the Yongxi era, I was entrusted with command of the army.

sentences.zh: 出身爲國，綿歷二紀，犯危履難，豈避風霜。

translations.literal: Born to serve the state, spanning two decades, braving danger and treading hardship—how would I avoid wind and frost?
translations.idiomatic: I entered service for the state more than twenty years ago, facing danger and hardship without shrinking from wind or frost.

sentences.zh: 遂得躬被袞衣，口飱玉食，富貴當年，光榮身世。

translations.literal: Thus I came to wear the imperial robe myself, eat food fit for jade, enjoy wealth and honor in my prime, and bring glory to my person and lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Thus I came to wear the imperial robe myself, dine on food fit for jade, enjoy wealth and honor in my prime, and bring glory to my person and lineage.

sentences.zh: 何爲一旦舉旌斾，援桴鼓，而北面相抗者，何哉？

translations.literal: Why then, all at once raising banners and standards, beating drums, and facing north in resistance—why?
translations.idiomatic: Why then did I suddenly raise banners, beat the drums, and turn north to resist you?

sentences.zh: 實以畏懼危亡，恐招禍害，捐軀非義，身名兩滅故耳。

translations.literal: Truly because I feared destruction and dreaded inviting disaster—sacrificing the body without righteousness means both body and name are destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Because I feared ruin and dreaded inviting disaster—dying for no righteous cause destroys both body and name.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 往年之暮，尊王遘疾，神不祐善，祈禱莫瘳。

translations.literal: In the twilight of last year my lord fell ill; the spirits did not bless the good, and prayers could not cure him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of last year my lord fell ill; heaven did not protect the good, and no prayer could cure him.

sentences.zh: 遂使嬖幸擅威權，閽寺肆詭惑，上下相猜，心腹離貳。

translations.literal: Thus favored minions seized power, eunuchs ran wild with deceit, above and below mutually suspected one another, and confidants split in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Favored minions seized power, eunuchs spun deceit, court and camp turned on each other, and trusted men divided their loyalties.

sentences.zh: 僕妻子在宅，無事見圍；

translations.literal: My wife and children were at home, yet without cause were besieged;
translations.idiomatic: My wife and children were at home, yet for no reason they were besieged;

sentences.zh: 段康之謀，莫知所以；

translations.literal: the plot of Duan Kang—I know not why;
translations.idiomatic: the plot involving Duan Kang—I do not know why;

sentences.zh: 盧潛入軍，未審何故。

translations.literal: Lu Qian entered the army—for what reason I could not tell.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qian entered the army—for what reason I could not tell.

sentences.zh: 翼翼小心，常懷戰慄，有靦面目，寧不自疑。

translations.literal: Treading cautiously, I constantly trembled with fear; with shame upon my face, how could I not doubt myself?
translations.idiomatic: I walked on eggshells and lived in dread; with shame burning on my face, how could I not doubt myself?

sentences.zh: 及廻師長社，希自陳狀，簡書未達，斧鉞已臨。

translations.literal: When I returned to the army at Changshe, hoping to explain myself, my letter had not arrived before the axe and yue were already at hand.
translations.idiomatic: When I returned to the army at Changshe hoping to explain myself, my letter had not even arrived before the executioner's axe was at my throat.

sentences.zh: 旣旌旗相對，咫尺不遠，飛書每奏，兼申鄙情；

translations.literal: With banners already facing each other, barely a stone's throw apart, I sent letters again and again, also stating my humble feelings;
translations.idiomatic: Our banners already faced each other, barely a spear's length apart; I sent letter after letter, pleading my case as best I could;

sentences.zh: 而羣率恃雄，眇然不顧，運戟推鋒，專欲屠滅。

translations.literal: yet your host relied on its strength, disdained me utterly, wheeled halberds and thrust with blades, intent solely on slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: yet your army trusted its numbers, ignored me completely, wheeled halberds and drove the blades, bent on nothing but annihilation.

sentences.zh: 築圍堰水，三板僅存，舉目相看，命懸晷刻，不忍死亡，出戰城下。

translations.literal: They built siege works and dammed water; only three planks of the wall remained; we looked at each other—life hung by a moment; unable to bear death, I went out to fight below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: They built earthworks and dammed the water; only three layers of wall remained; we stared at one another with our lives on the clock; unable to wait for death, I went out to fight beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 禽獸惡死，人倫好生，送地拘秦，非樂爲也。

translations.literal: Beasts hate death; human nature loves life—yielding territory and submitting to Qin was no joy.
translations.idiomatic: Beasts hate death and men love life—surrendering land and submitting to Qin was no pleasure of mine.

sentences.zh: 但尊王平昔見與，比肩共獎帝室，雖形勢參差，寒暑小異，丞相司徒，雁行而已。

translations.literal: Yet my lord in times past treated me as an equal, shoulder to shoulder in praising the imperial house—though circumstances differed and seasons varied slightly, Chancellor and Minister of Works were merely geese flying in formation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the past my lord treated me as an equal, shoulder to shoulder in serving the imperial house—though our stations differed and seasons changed, Chancellor and Minister of Works were only geese in a single flight.

sentences.zh: 福祿官榮，自是天爵，勞而後受，理不相干，欲求吞炭，何其謬也！

translations.literal: Fortune, salary, rank, and glory are Heaven's grants, earned after labor—the matter is unrelated; to seek to swallow charcoal—how absurd!
translations.idiomatic: Fortune, salary, rank, and glory are gifts of Heaven, earned only after toil—the cases have nothing to do with each other; to demand I swallow charcoal—how absurd!

sentences.zh: 然竊人之財，猶謂爲盜，祿去公室，相爲不取。

translations.literal: Yet stealing another's wealth is still called theft; when salary left the public office, we considered it something not to take.
translations.idiomatic: Stealing another man's wealth is still called theft; when salary left the public treasury, we both refused to take what was not ours.

sentences.zh: 今魏德雖衰，天命未改，祈恩私第，何足關言。

translations.literal: Now Wei's virtue may be in decline, but Heaven's mandate has not changed—pleading for favor in a private residence is hardly worth mention.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's virtue may be fading, but Heaven's mandate has not changed—begging for grace in a private house is hardly worth discussing.

sentences.zh: 賜示「不能東封函谷，受制於人」，當似教僕賢祭仲而襃季氏。

translations.literal: You showed me "unable to seal off Hangu eastward, subject to others' control"—as if teaching me to praise Ji Zhong while honoring the Ji clan.
translations.idiomatic: You wrote that I was "unable to seal Hangu in the east and subject to others' control"—as if instructing me to praise Ji Zhong while exalting the Ji clan.

sentences.zh: 無主之國，在禮未聞，動而不法，何以取訓？

translations.literal: A lordless state—in ritual never heard of; acting without law, how can one take instruction?
translations.idiomatic: A state without a lord is nowhere mentioned in ritual; to act without law—how can one learn from that?

sentences.zh: 竊以分財養幼，事歸令終，捨宅存孤，誰云隙末？

translations.literal: I hold that sharing wealth to raise the young brings a fitting end; giving up a house to preserve orphans—who calls that a petty rupture?
translations.idiomatic: I believe that sharing wealth to raise the young is a proper ending, and giving up a house to save orphans—who would call that a petty break?

sentences.zh: 復言僕「衆不足以自強，危如累卵」。

translations.literal: You also say I "lack the numbers to strengthen myself, danger like piled eggs."
translations.idiomatic: You also say my forces "are too few to stand alone, perilous as piled eggs."

sentences.zh: 然紂有億兆夷人，卒降十亂；

translations.literal: Yet Zhou had billions of barbarian subjects and in the end was reduced by the Ten Disorders;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhou had billions of subjects and in the end fell to the Ten Disorders;

sentences.zh: 桀之百剋，終自無後。

translations.literal: Jie's hundred victories—in the end he had no successor.
translations.idiomatic: Jie won a hundred battles and in the end left no heir.

sentences.zh: 潁川之戰，卽是殷監。

translations.literal: The battle at Yingchuan is the mirror of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The battle at Yingchuan is the warning mirror of the Shang.

sentences.zh: 輕重由人，非鼎在德。

translations.literal: Weight and lightness depend on men, not the tripod on virtue alone.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a state stands or falls depends on its men, not on the tripod alone.

sentences.zh: 苟能忠信，雖弱必強。

translations.literal: If one can be loyal and faithful, though weak one must become strong.
translations.idiomatic: If one can be loyal and faithful, even the weak must grow strong.

sentences.zh: 殷憂啓聖，處危何苦。

translations.literal: Deep worry gives birth to sagacity—what hardship in standing in peril?
translations.idiomatic: Deep worry breeds wisdom—what hardship is there in standing in danger?

sentences.zh: 況今梁道邕熙，招攜以禮，被我獸文，縻之好爵。

translations.literal: Moreover now the Liang Way is harmonious and bright; it gathers the distant by ritual, cloaks us in tiger-pattern robes, and ties us with noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Liang Way is now broad and bright; it gathers the distant by ritual, robes us in tiger-pattern insignia, and binds us with noble ranks.

sentences.zh: 方欲苑五岳而池四海，掃夷穢以拯黎元，東羈甌越，西通汧、隴。

translations.literal: It intends to take the Five Peaks as parks and the Four Seas as ponds, sweep barbarian filth to rescue the people, tie down Ou and Yue in the east, and open Qian and Long in the west.
translations.idiomatic: It means to make the Five Peaks its park and the Four Seas its pond, sweep away barbarian filth to save the people, bind Ou and Yue in the east, and open Qian and Long in the west.

sentences.zh: 吳、楚剽勁，帶甲千羣；

translations.literal: Wu and Chu are fierce and sharp, with a thousand groups in armor;
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Chu are fierce and sharp, with a thousand armored hosts;

sentences.zh: 吳兵冀馬，控弦十萬。

translations.literal: Wu soldiers and Ji horses, a hundred thousand with bowstrings drawn.
translations.idiomatic: Wu troops and Ji horses, a hundred thousand bowstrings drawn.

sentences.zh: 兼僕所部義勇如林，奮義取威，不期而發，大風一振，枯幹必摧，凝霜暫落，秋蒂自殞。

translations.literal: Together with the righteous warriors under my command thick as a forest, rousing righteousness to seize glory, erupting without warning—a great wind one blast and dry trunks must fall; frost briefly drops and autumn fruit falls of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Add the righteous warriors under my command, thick as a forest, rousing righteousness to win glory and striking without warning—a great wind one gust and dry trunks snap; frost falls for a moment and autumn fruit drops by itself.

sentences.zh: 此而爲弱，誰足稱強！

translations.literal: If this is called weak, who dare call himself strong!
translations.idiomatic: If this is weak, who has the right to call himself strong!

sentences.zh: 又見誣兩端，受疑二國。

translations.literal: Again I am slandered from both sides, suspected by two states.
translations.idiomatic: Again I am slandered from both sides and suspected by two states.

sentences.zh: 斟酌物情，一何至此！

translations.literal: Weighing human sentiment—how could it come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Weighing how men feel—how could it come to this!

sentences.zh: 昔陳平背楚，歸漢則王；

translations.literal: In the past Chen Ping turned from Chu; returning to Han he was made king;
translations.idiomatic: In the past Chen Ping abandoned Chu; when he returned to Han he was made king;

sentences.zh: 百里出虞，入秦斯霸。

translations.literal: Baili left Yu; entering Qin he became hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: Baili left Yu; entering Qin he became hegemon.

sentences.zh: 蓋昏明由主，用捨在時，奉禮而行，神其庇也。

translations.literal: Brightness and darkness depend on the ruler; use and discard depend on the times—follow ritual and act, and the spirits will shelter you.
translations.idiomatic: Clarity and obscurity depend on the ruler; use and discard depend on the times—follow ritual and act, and the spirits will protect you.

sentences.zh: 書稱士馬精新，剋日齊舉，誇張形勝，指期蕩滅。

translations.literal: Your letter says troops and horses are fresh and new, on a set day all will advance together, boasting of strategic advantage, pointing to a date for total destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Your letter says troops and horses are fresh, that on a fixed day all will march together, boasting of strategic advantage and promising total destruction by a set date.

sentences.zh: 竊以寒飂白露，節候乃同；

translations.literal: I note that cold wind and white dew—the seasons are the same;
translations.idiomatic: I note that cold wind and white dew—the seasons are the same;

sentences.zh: 秋風揚塵，馬首何異。

translations.literal: autumn wind raises dust—the horse's head—what difference?
translations.idiomatic: autumn wind raises dust from the horses' hooves—what difference does that make?

sentences.zh: 徒知北方之力爭，未識西、南之合從，苟欲徇意於前途，不覺坑穽在其側。

translations.literal: You only know the struggle for power in the north, not the alliance of west and south; if you wish to indulge your will on the road ahead, you do not notice the pitfall at your side.
translations.idiomatic: You see only the power struggle in the north, not the alliance of west and south; if you indulge your will on the road ahead, you will not notice the pitfall beside you.

sentences.zh: 若云去危令歸正朔，轉禍以脫網羅，彼旣嗤僕之愚迷，此亦笑君之晦昧。

translations.literal: If you say to leave danger and return to the true calendar, turn calamity to escape the net—there they already mock my folly and blindness, here too they laugh at your obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: If you say to leave danger, return to the true calendar, and turn calamity into escape from the net—there they already mock my folly, and here they laugh at your blindness.

sentences.zh: 今已引二邦，揚旌北討，熊虎齊奮，剋復中原，荊、襄、廣、潁已屬關右，項城、懸瓠亦奉南朝，幸自取之，何勞恩賜。

translations.literal: Now I have already drawn in two states, raised banners for a northern campaign, bear and tiger together rousing, to recover the Central Plain—Jing, Xiang, Guang, and Ying already belong to the west; Xiangcheng and Xuan'gu also obey the Southern Court; take them yourself if you please—why trouble yourself with gracious bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: I have already drawn in two states, raised banners for a northern campaign, and roused bear and tiger together to recover the Central Plain—Jing, Xiang, Guang, and Ying already belong to the west; Xiangcheng and Xuan'gu already serve the Southern Court; take them yourself if you wish—why need your gracious grant?

sentences.zh: 然權變不一，理有萬途。

translations.literal: Yet expedients vary endlessly; reason has ten thousand paths.
translations.idiomatic: Yet expedients vary endlessly; reason has ten thousand paths.

sentences.zh: 爲君計者，莫若割地兩和，三分鼎峙，燕、衛、晉、趙足相奉祿，齊、曹、宋、魯悉歸大梁，使僕得輸力南朝，北敦姻好，束帛交行，戎車不動。

translations.literal: For your planning, nothing better than dividing territory and making peace in two, three parts standing like tripods—Yan, Wei, Jin, and Zhao enough to supply each other's salaries; Qi, Cao, Song, and Lu all returning to Great Liang—let me contribute strength to the Southern Court, cement affinity ties with the north, silks going back and forth, war chariots unmoving.
translations.idiomatic: For your planning, nothing beats dividing the land and making peace in two—three kingdoms standing like tripods—Yan, Wei, Jin, and Zhao supplying one another's salaries; Qi, Cao, Song, and Lu all returning to Great Liang—let me serve the Southern Court, bind ties with the north, exchange silks, and keep war chariots still.

sentences.zh: 僕立當世之功，君卒祖禰之業，各保疆界，躬享歲時，百姓乂寧，四民安堵。

translations.literal: I would establish merit for the age; you would complete the work of ancestors and fathers—each guarding our borders, personally enjoying the seasons, the people peaceful, the four classes settled.
translations.idiomatic: I would win merit for the age; you would finish the work of ancestors and fathers—each keeping his borders, enjoying the seasons in peace, the people tranquil, the four classes settled.

sentences.zh: 孰若驅農夫於隴畝，抗勍敵於三方，避干戈於首尾，當鋒鏑於心腹。

translations.literal: Compared with driving farmers from the fields, resisting fierce enemies on three sides, avoiding weapons at head and tail, meeting blades and arrowheads at the heart—
translations.idiomatic: How much better that than driving farmers from the fields, facing fierce enemies on three sides, dodging weapons at both ends, and taking blades and arrows in the heart—

sentences.zh: 縱太公爲將，不能獲存，歸之高明，何以剋濟。

translations.literal: even with the Grand Duke as general, one cannot survive; entrusted to your lofty wisdom—how can you overcome and succeed?
translations.idiomatic: even with the Grand Duke as general one could not survive; given to your lofty wisdom—how could you overcome and succeed?

sentences.zh: 復尋來書云，僕妻子悉拘司寇。

translations.literal: Again searching your letter, it says my wife and children are all detained by the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Reading your letter again, it says my wife and children are all held by the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 以之見要，庶其可及。

translations.literal: Using them to threaten me—perhaps it could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Using them to threaten me—perhaps that could work.

sentences.zh: 當是見疑褊心，未識大趣。

translations.literal: This must be narrow-minded suspicion, not understanding the larger design.
translations.idiomatic: That must be narrow suspicion, not understanding the larger design.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 昔王陵附漢，母在不歸；

translations.literal: In the past Wang Ling adhered to Han—his mother alive, he did not return;
translations.idiomatic: In the past Wang Ling sided with Han—though his mother lived, he did not return;

sentences.zh: 太上囚楚，乞羹自若。

translations.literal: the Supreme One was prisoner of Chu—begged for broth as if normal.
translations.idiomatic: the Supreme One was prisoner of Chu—he begged for broth as if nothing were wrong.

sentences.zh: 矧伊妻子，而可介意。

translations.literal: How much more so—mere wife and children—could one care?
translations.idiomatic: How much less, then, should mere wife and children matter?

sentences.zh: 脫謂誅之有益，欲止不能；

translations.literal: If killing them were said to help, wanting to stop but unable;
translations.idiomatic: If killing them were said to help, you might want to stop but could not;

sentences.zh: 殺之無損，徒復坑戮。

translations.literal: killing them without loss—only further massacre in vain.
translations.idiomatic: killing them without loss would only add pointless slaughter.

sentences.zh: 家累在君，何關僕也？

translations.literal: My family's lives are in your hands—what has that to do with me?
translations.idiomatic: My family's lives are in your hands—what has that to do with me?

sentences.zh: 而遵道所傳，頗亦非謬，但在縲紲，恐不備盡，故重陳辭，更論款曲。

translations.literal: What Zun Dao transmitted is also not without reason, but while in bonds I fear I cannot be complete—therefore I restate my case and again discuss sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: What Zun Dao reported is not entirely wrong, but while in chains I fear I cannot say everything—so I restate my case and speak again of sincerity.

sentences.zh: 所望良圖，時惠報旨。

translations.literal: What I hope for is a good plan; please timely grant a reply.
translations.idiomatic: What I hope for is a wise plan; please reply in good time.

sentences.zh: 然昔與盟主，事等琴瑟，讒人間之，翻爲讎敵。

translations.literal: Yet in the past with our covenant lord, our affairs were like lute and zither—slanderers came between us and we turned into enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the past with our covenant lord our bond was like lute and zither—slanderers came between us and we became enemies.

sentences.zh: 撫弦搦矢，不覺傷懷，裂帛還書，知何能述。

translations.literal: Touching the strings and grasping the arrow, I unknowingly wound my heart; tearing silk to reply—how can words suffice?
translations.idiomatic: Touching the strings and grasping the arrow, I wound my own heart without noticing; tearing silk to write back—how can words say enough?

sentences.zh: 十二月，景率軍圍譙城不下，退攻城父，拔之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Jing led troops to besiege Qiao city but could not take it; withdrew to attack Chengfucheng and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Jing led troops to besiege Qiao but failed to take it; he withdrew to attack Chengfucheng and captured it.

sentences.zh: 又遣其行臺左丞王偉、左民郎中王則詣闕獻策，求諸元子弟立爲魏主，輔以北伐，許之。

translations.literal: He also sent his Mobile Headquarters Left Director Wang Wei and Left Civil Affairs Attendant Wang Ze to the palace with a plan, asking that a member of the Yuan clan be installed as Wei ruler to assist in a northern campaign—they assented.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his Mobile Headquarters Left Director Wang Wei and Left Civil Affairs Attendant Wang Ze to court with a plan, asking that a Yuan prince be installed as Wei ruler to assist a northern campaign—the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔遣太子舍人元貞爲咸陽王，須渡江，許卽偽位，乘輿副御以資給之。

translations.literal: An edict sent the Crown Prince's Aide Yuan Zhen as Prince of Xianyang; once he crossed the river he was granted the false throne, with imperial carriage attendants to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Crown Prince's Aide Yuan Zhen as Prince of Xianyang; once he crossed the river he would take the false throne, with imperial carriage attendants provided for him.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄又遣慕容紹宗追景，景退入渦陽，馬尚有數千匹，甲卒數萬人，車萬餘輛，相持於渦北。

translations.literal: Qi Wenxiang again sent Murong Shaozong to pursue Jing; Jing withdrew into Woyang, still had several thousand horses, tens of thousands of armored soldiers, more than ten thousand carts—a standoff north of the Wo River.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wenxiang again sent Murong Shaozong to pursue Jing; Jing withdrew into Woyang with several thousand horses, tens of thousands of armored men, and more than ten thousand carts—a standoff north of the Wo River.

sentences.zh: 景軍食盡，士卒並北人，不樂南渡，其將暴顯等各率所部降於紹宗。

translations.literal: Jing's army ran out of food; the soldiers were all northerners, unwilling to cross south; his generals Bao Xian and others each led their units to surrender to Shaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's army ran out of food; his soldiers were all northerners and unwilling to cross south; generals such as Bao Xian each led their units to surrender to Shaozong.

sentences.zh: 景軍潰散，乃與腹心數騎自峽石濟淮，稍收散卒，得馬步八百人，奔壽春，監州韋黯納之。

translations.literal: Jing's army collapsed and scattered; then with a few trusted horsemen he himself crossed the Huai at Xiashi, gradually gathered scattered troops, got eight hundred foot and horse, fled to Shouyang; Acting Prefect Wei An received him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's army broke and scattered; with a few trusted horsemen he crossed the Huai at Xiashi himself, slowly gathered scattered troops until he had eight hundred foot and horse, fled to Shouyang, and Acting Prefect Wei An took him in.

sentences.zh: 景啓求貶削，優詔不許，仍以爲豫州牧，本官如故。

translations.literal: Jing memorialized asking to be demoted and stripped; a gracious edict refused; he was still made Inspector of Yuzhou, original posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Jing memorialized asking to be demoted and stripped; a gracious edict refused; he remained Inspector of Yuzhou with his original posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 景旣據壽春，遂懷反叛，屬城居民，悉召募爲軍士，輒停責市估及田租，百姓子女悉以配將卒。

translations.literal: Once Jing held Shouchun, he harbored rebellion; residents of subordinate cities were all conscripted as soldiers; market dues and land tax were halted; commoners' sons and daughters were all assigned to officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jing held Shouchun he turned rebellious; residents of subordinate cities were all conscripted as soldiers; market dues and land tax were stopped; commoners' sons and daughters were all assigned to officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 又啓求錦萬匹，爲軍人袍，領軍朱异議，以御府錦署止充頒賞遠近，不容以供邊城戎服，請送青布以給之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting ten thousand bolts of brocade for soldiers' robes; Supreme Commander Zhu Yi argued the imperial brocade office only supplied rewards near and far—it could not furnish border garrison military dress; request to send blue cloth instead.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized requesting ten thousand bolts of brocade for soldiers' robes; Supreme Commander Zhu Yi argued the imperial brocade office only supplied rewards near and far and could not clothe border garrisons—blue cloth should be sent instead.

sentences.zh: 景得布，悉用爲袍衫，因尚青色。

translations.literal: Jing got the cloth, used it all for robes and jackets, and hence favored azure.
translations.idiomatic: Jing got the cloth, used it all for robes and jackets, and from then on favored azure.

sentences.zh: 又以臺所給仗，多不能精，啓請東冶鍛工，欲更營造，敕並給之。

translations.literal: Also because the weapons supplied by the court were mostly not fine, he memorialized requesting Eastern Workshop smiths to rebuild—an edict granted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Because the weapons supplied by the court were mostly poor, he memorialized requesting Eastern Workshop smiths to rebuild them—an edict granted all he asked.

sentences.zh: 景自渦陽敗後，多所徵求，朝廷含弘，未嘗拒絕。

translations.literal: After Jing's defeat at Woyang, he made many demands; the court was tolerant and never refused.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing's defeat at Woyang he made many demands; the court was tolerant and never refused.

sentences.zh: 先是，豫州刺史貞陽侯淵明督衆軍圍彭城，兵敗沒于魏。

translations.literal: Earlier, Inspector of Yuzhou Marquis Yuanming of Zhenyang had supervised the host besieging Pengcheng; the army was defeated and he perished in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuzhou Inspector Marquis Yuanming of Zhenyang had commanded the armies besieging Pengcheng; the army was defeated and he perished in Wei.

sentences.zh: 至是，遣使還述魏人請追前好。

translations.literal: At this time he sent envoys back reporting the Wei people asked to renew the former friendship.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he sent envoys back saying the Wei people asked to renew the former friendship.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，高祖又與魏連和。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, Gaozu again made alliance with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year Gaozu again made alliance with Wei.

sentences.zh: 景聞之懼，馳啓固諫，高祖不從。

translations.literal: Jing heard and feared; sent urgent memorials firmly remonstrating—Gaozu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jing heard and was afraid; he sent urgent memorials firmly remonstrating, but Gaozu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 爾後表疏跋扈，言辭不遜。

translations.literal: Thereafter his memorials were arrogant, his words irreverent.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter his memorials grew arrogant and his words irreverent.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽王範鎮合肥，及司州刺史羊鴉仁俱累啓稱景有異志，領軍朱异曰：「侯景數百叛虜，何能爲役？

translations.literal: Prince Fan of Poyang was garrisoned at Hefei, and Inspector of Si Province Yang Yaren both repeatedly memorialized that Jing had rebellious intent; Zhu Yi said: "Hou Jing—a few hundred rebel captives—how can he be of service?
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fan of Poyang held Hefei, and Si Province Inspector Yang Yaren both repeatedly memorialized that Jing had rebellious intent; Zhu Yi said, "Hou Jing—a few hundred rebel captives—how can he be of any use?

sentences.zh: 」並抑不奏聞，而逾加賞賜，所以姦謀益果。

translations.literal: " All were suppressed without being reported upward, yet rewards only increased—thus his treacherous plot grew bolder.
translations.idiomatic: " All were suppressed without being reported upward, yet rewards only increased—so his treacherous plot grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 又知臨賀王正德怨望朝廷，密令要結，正德許爲內啓。

translations.literal: He also knew Prince Zhengde of Linhe resented the court; secretly sent to win him over—Zhengde promised to open from within.
translations.idiomatic: He also knew Prince Zhengde of Linhe resented the court; he secretly sent to win him over, and Zhengde promised to open the gates from within.

sentences.zh: 八月，景遂發兵反，攻馬頭、木柵，執太守劉神茂、戍主曹璆等。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Jing then raised troops in rebellion, attacked Matou and Mu Fort, seized Administrator Liu Shenmao, garrison commander Cao Qiu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Jing raised troops in rebellion, attacked Matou and Mu Fort, and seized Administrator Liu Shenmao, garrison commander Cao Qiu, and others.

sentences.zh: 於是詔郢州刺史鄱陽王範爲南道都督，北徐州刺史封山侯正表爲北道都督，司州刺史柳仲禮爲西道都督，通直散騎常侍裴之高爲東道都督，同討景，濟自歷陽；

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict made Inspector of Yingzhou Prince Fan of Poyang southern-route Commander, Inspector of North Xuzhou Marquis Zhengbiao of Fengshan northern-route Commander, Inspector of Si Province Liu Zhongli western-route Commander, General-of-Regular-Gateway Attendant Pei Zhigao eastern-route Commander, all to attack Jing together, crossing from Liyang;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict made Yingzhou Inspector Prince Fan of Poyang southern-route commander, North Xuzhou Inspector Marquis Zhengbiao of Fengshan northern-route commander, Si Province Inspector Liu Zhongli western-route commander, and General-of-Regular-Gateway Attendant Pei Zhigao eastern-route commander, all to attack Jing together, crossing from Liyang;

sentences.zh: 又令開府儀同三司、丹陽尹、邵陵王綸持節，董督衆軍。

translations.literal: also ordered General with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, Danyang Governor, Prince Lun of Shaoling to bear the staff and supervise the host.
translations.idiomatic: It also ordered General with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, Danyang governor, Prince Lun of Shaoling to bear the staff and supervise the armies.

sentences.zh: 十月，景留其中軍王顯貴守壽春城，出軍偽向合肥，遂襲譙州，助防董紹先開城降之，執刺史豊城侯泰。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Jing left his Central Army Wang Xiankui to hold Shouchun city, marched out feigning toward Hefei, then suddenly attacked Qiaozhou; Assistant Defender Dong Shaoxian opened the gates and surrendered; seized Inspector Marquis Tai of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Jing left Central Army Wang Xiankui to hold Shouchun, marched out feigning toward Hefei, then suddenly attacked Qiaozhou; Assistant Defender Dong Shaoxian opened the gates and surrendered; Inspector Marquis Tai of Fengcheng was seized.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，遣太子家令王質率兵三千巡江遏防。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard and sent Crown Prince House Steward Wang Zhi with three thousand troops to patrol the river and block.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu heard and sent Crown Prince House Steward Wang Zhi with three thousand troops to patrol the river and block the crossing.

sentences.zh: 景進攻歷陽，歷陽太守莊鐵遣弟均率數百人夜斫景營，不克，均戰沒，鐵又降之。

translations.literal: Jing advanced to attack Liyang; Liyang Administrator Zhuang Tie sent his younger brother Jun with several hundred men to raid Jing's camp by night—failed; Jun died in battle; Tie again surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing advanced to attack Liyang; Liyang Administrator Zhuang Tie sent his younger brother Jun with several hundred men to raid Jing's camp by night but failed; Jun died in battle, and Tie surrendered to him again.

sentences.zh: 蕭正德先遣大船數十艘，偽稱載荻，實裝濟景。

translations.literal: Xiao Zhengde first sent several dozen large ships, falsely claiming to carry reeds—in reality equipped to ferry Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhengde first sent several dozen large ships, falsely claiming to carry reeds but in reality ready to ferry Jing.

sentences.zh: 景至京口，將渡，慮王質爲梗。

translations.literal: Jing reached Jingkou, about to cross, fearing Wang Zhi would obstruct.
translations.idiomatic: Jing reached Jingkou and was about to cross, fearing Wang Zhi would block him.

sentences.zh: 俄而質無故退，景聞之尚未信也，乃密遣覘之。

translations.literal: Suddenly Zhi withdrew for no apparent reason; Jing heard but did not yet believe; he secretly sent scouts.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly Zhi withdrew for no apparent reason; Jing heard but did not yet believe it, and secretly sent scouts.

sentences.zh: 謂使者曰：「質若審退，可折江東樹枝爲驗。

translations.literal: He told the messenger: "If Zhi has truly withdrawn, break branches from east-of-river trees as proof.
translations.idiomatic: He told the messenger, "If Zhi has truly withdrawn, break branches from east-of-river trees as proof.

sentences.zh: 」覘人如言而返，景大喜曰：「吾事辦矣。

translations.literal: " The scout returned as instructed; Jing rejoiced greatly: "My business is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: " The scout returned as instructed; Jing rejoiced greatly and said, "My business is accomplished.

sentences.zh: 」乃自採石濟，馬數百匹，兵千人，京師不之覺。

translations.literal: " Then he himself crossed from Caishi—several hundred horses, a thousand soldiers—the capital did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he crossed from Caishi himself—several hundred horses, a thousand soldiers—and the capital did not notice.

sentences.zh: 景卽分襲姑孰，執淮南太守文成侯寧，遂至慈湖。

translations.literal: Jing then divided forces to strike Gudu, seized Huainan Administrator Marquis Ning of Wencheng, and reached Cihu.
translations.idiomatic: Jing then divided his forces to strike Gudu, seized Huainan Administrator Marquis Ning of Wencheng, and reached Cihu.

sentences.zh: 於是詔以揚州刺史宣城王大器爲都督城內諸軍事，都官尚書羊侃爲軍師將軍以副焉；

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict made Inspector of Yangzhou Prince Daqi of Xuancheng commander of all forces within the walls, Minister of Justice Yang Kan as Army Advisor General to assist;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict made Yangzhou Inspector Prince Daqi of Xuancheng commander of all forces within the walls, and Minister of Justice Yang Kan Army Advisor General to assist him;

sentences.zh: 南浦侯推守東府城，西豊公大春守石頭城，輕車長史謝禧守白下。

translations.literal: Marquis Tui of Nanpu held the Eastern Palace city, Duke Dachun of Xifeng held Stone City, Light Chariot Chief Clerk Xie Xi held Baixia.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Tui of Nanpu held the Eastern Palace city, Duke Dachun of Xifeng held Stone City, and Light Chariot Chief Clerk Xie Xi held Baixia.

sentences.zh: 旣而景至朱雀航，蕭正德先屯丹陽郡，至是，率所部與景合。

translations.literal: Soon Jing reached the Zhuque floating bridge; Xiao Zhengde had earlier garrisoned Danyang commandery—now he led his troops to join Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jing reached the Zhuque Bridge. Xiao Zhengde had been garrisoned at Danyang; now he marched out with his men to join him.

sentences.zh: 建康令庾信率兵千餘人屯航北，見景至航，命徹航，始除一舶，遂棄軍走南塘，遊軍復閉航渡景。

translations.literal: Jiankang magistrate Yu Xin led over a thousand troops to garrison north of the bridge; when he saw Jing reach the bridge he ordered it dismantled; after removing only one vessel he abandoned his army and fled to Nantang; roaming patrol units again closed the bridge and let Jing cross.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang magistrate Yu Xin held the north bank with a thousand-odd troops. Seeing Jing at the bridge, he ordered it broken—but only one boat was cleared before he fled to Nantang with his force abandoned. Patrol units then reclosed the bridge and let Jing cross.

sentences.zh: 皇太子以所乘馬授王質，配精兵三千，使援庾信。

translations.literal: The crown prince gave his own mount to Wang Zhi and assigned three thousand elite troops to aid Yu Xin.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince gave Wang Zhi his own horse and three thousand picked troops to relieve Yu Xin.

sentences.zh: 質至領軍府，與賊遇，未陣便奔走，景乘勝至闕下。

translations.literal: Zhi reached the Commandant-in-Chief's office, met the rebels, and fled before forming ranks; Jing pressed his victory to the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi reached the commandant's headquarters, met the rebels, and broke before he could form ranks. Jing rode the momentum to the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 西豊公大春棄石頭城走，景遣其儀同于子悅據之。

translations.literal: Western Feng duke Dachun abandoned Stone Fort city and fled; Jing sent his Yitong Yu Ziyue to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Western Feng duke Dachun abandoned Stone Fort and fled. Jing sent his Yitong Yu Ziyue to occupy it.

sentences.zh: 謝禧亦棄白下城走。

translations.literal: Xie Xi also abandoned Baixia city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xi likewise abandoned Baixia and fled.

sentences.zh: 景於是百道攻城，持火炬燒大司馬、東西華諸門。

translations.literal: Jing then assaulted the city from a hundred directions, bearing torches to burn the Grand Marshal Gate and the East and West Flower gates.
translations.idiomatic: Jing assaulted from every direction, torches in hand, setting fire to the Grand Marshal Gate and the East and West Flower gates.

sentences.zh: 城中倉卒，未有其備，乃鑿門樓，下水沃火，久之方滅。

translations.literal: Inside the city, caught unprepared, they hacked through the gate tower, poured water to douse the fire—it was long before it went out.
translations.idiomatic: The city was caught flat-footed. They hacked through the gate tower and poured water on the flames; only after a long while did the fire die.

sentences.zh: 賊又斫東掖門將開，羊侃鑿門扇，刺殺數人，賊乃退。

translations.literal: The rebels again hacked at the East Side Gate about to open; Yang Kan hacked through the gate panels and killed several men—the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hacked at the East Side Gate as it was about to open. Yang Kan smashed the gate panels and killed several men, and the rebels fell back.

sentences.zh: 又登東宮牆，射城內，至夜，太宗募人出燒東宮，東宮臺殿遂盡。

translations.literal: They also climbed the Eastern Palace wall and shot into the city; at night Taizong recruited men to go out and burn the Eastern Palace—the Eastern Palace halls and pavilions were utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: They scaled the Eastern Palace wall and shot into the city. That night Taizong raised volunteers to burn the Eastern Palace; its halls and towers were consumed entirely.

sentences.zh: 景又燒城西馬廄、士林館、太府寺。

translations.literal: Jing also burned the west city's horse stables, Scholars Grove Hall, and the Grand Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Jing also burned the western horse stables, Scholars Grove Hall, and the Grand Treasury.

sentences.zh: 明日，景又作木驢數百攻城，城上飛石擲之，所值皆碎破。

translations.literal: The next day Jing built several hundred wooden siege tortoises to attack the city; from the walls catapult stones were hurled—whatever they struck was shattered.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jing built hundreds of wooden siege tortoises. Stones flew from the walls; whatever they hit shattered.

sentences.zh: 景苦攻不剋，傷損甚多，乃止攻，築長圍以絕內外，啓求誅中領軍朱异、太子右衛率陸驗、兼少府卿徐驎、制局監周石珍等。

translations.literal: Jing, unable to take the city despite bitter assault and heavy casualties, halted the attack and built a long encirclement to cut off inside from out; he petitioned for the execution of Central Commandant Zhu Yi, Crown Prince's Right Guard leader Lu Yan, concurrent Minister of the Palace Treasury Xu Lin, Office of Manufacture Supervisor Zhou Shizhen, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to break the city despite heavy losses, Jing stopped the assault and built a long encirclement to seal inside from out. He petitioned for the heads of Central Commandant Zhu Yi, Crown Prince Right Guard leader Lu Yan, concurrent Palace Treasury minister Xu Lin, Manufacture Supervisor Zhou Shizhen, and others.

sentences.zh: 城內亦射賞格出外：「有能斬景首，授以景位，幷錢一億萬，布絹各萬匹，女樂二部。」

translations.literal: Inside the city they also shot out reward placards: "Whoever can cut off Jing's head shall receive Jing's rank, plus a hundred million cash, ten thousand bolts each of cloth and silk, and two ensembles of female musicians."
translations.idiomatic: The city shot out reward placards: "Whoever brings Jing's head gets his rank, a hundred million cash, ten thousand bolts of cloth and silk each, and two troupes of female musicians."

sentences.zh: 十一月，景立蕭正德爲帝，卽偽位於儀賢堂，改年曰正平。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Jing installed Xiao Zhengde as emperor, who immediately took the false throne at the Hall of Virtuous Worthies and changed the era name to Zhengping.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Jing set up Xiao Zhengde as emperor. Zhengde took the false throne at the Hall of Virtuous Worthies and changed the era to Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 初，童謠有「正平」之言，故立號以應之。

translations.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme had spoken of "Zhengping"—so he took that era name to match it.
translations.idiomatic: A children's rhyme had already spoken of "Zhengping," so he chose that name to answer the omen.

sentences.zh: 景自爲相國、天柱將軍，正德以女妻之。

translations.literal: Jing made himself Chancellor of State and Pillar of Heaven General; Zhengde gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Jing made himself chancellor and Pillar of Heaven General. Zhengde gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 景又攻東府城，設百尺樓車，鉤城堞盡落，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Jing again attacked the Eastern Palace city, setting up hundred-foot tower wagons; hooks pulled down all the battlements—the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Jing attacked the Eastern Palace city again with hundred-foot tower wagons. Hooks tore down the battlements, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 景使其儀同盧暉略率數千人，持長刀夾城門，悉驅城內文武裸身而出，賊交兵殺之，死者二千餘人。

translations.literal: Jing had his Yitong Lu Huilue lead several thousand men, long knives at the city gates on both sides, driving all civil and military officials inside the city out naked; the rebels crossed weapons and killed them—over two thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent Yitong Lu Huilue with several thousand men, long knives flanking the gates, driving every official inside out stripped bare. The rebels cut them down—more than two thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 南浦侯推是日遇害。

translations.literal: Marquis Tui of Nanpu was killed that day.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Tui of Nanpu died that day.

sentences.zh: 景使正德子見理、儀同盧暉略守東府城。

translations.literal: Jing had Zhengde's son Jianli and Yitong Lu Huilue guard the Eastern Palace city.
translations.idiomatic: Jing put Zhengde's son Jianli and Yitong Lu Huilue in charge of the Eastern Palace city.

sentences.zh: 景又於城東西各起一土山以臨城內，城內亦作兩山以應之，王公以下皆負土。

translations.literal: Jing also raised an earthen mound on east and west of the city to overlook the interior; inside the city two mounds were built in response—princes and officials down all carried earth.
translations.idiomatic: Jing raised earthen mounds east and west to overlook the city. Inside, two counter-mounds went up; princes and officials down to the lowest ranks all carried earth.

sentences.zh: 初，景至，便望克定京師，號令甚明，不犯百姓。

translations.literal: At first when Jing arrived he expected swiftly to pacify the capital; his orders were very clear and he did not harm the common people.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing first arrived he expected a quick capture of the capital. His orders were strict, and he did not molest the people.

sentences.zh: 旣攻城不下，人心離阻，又恐援軍總集，衆必潰散，乃縱兵殺掠，交屍塞路，富室豪家，恣意裒剝，子女妻妾，悉入軍營。

translations.literal: Once the city could not be taken, hearts turned away and resistance grew; fearing relief armies would gather and his force would scatter, he unleashed his troops to kill and plunder—corpses blocked the roads; wealthy and powerful households were stripped at will; sons and daughters, wives and concubines—all entered the military camps.
translations.idiomatic: When the city would not fall, morale cracked and fear spread. Afraid relief armies would mass and his host dissolve, he let his troops kill and loot. Corpses choked the roads; rich houses were stripped bare; sons, daughters, wives, and concubines—all were taken into camp.

sentences.zh: 及築土山，不限貴賤，晝夜不息，亂加毆棰，疲羸者因殺之以填山，號哭之聲，響動天地。

translations.literal: When building the earthen mounds, without distinction of noble or base, day and night without cease, they beat people at random; the weak and exhausted were killed to fill the mounds—the sound of wailing shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: To build the mounds, noble and common alike were driven day and night without rest, beaten at random. The weak were killed to fill the earthworks. Wailing shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 百姓不敢藏隱，並出從之，旬日之間，衆至數萬。

translations.literal: The common people dared not hide; all came out to follow him; within ten days or so his force reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The people dared not hide and turned out to serve him. Within ten days his numbers swelled to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 景儀同範桃棒密遣使送款乞降，會事泄見殺。

translations.literal: Jing's Yitong Fan Taobang secretly sent envoys offering surrender and begging to defect—when the matter leaked out he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's Yitong Fan Taobang secretly sent envoys to offer surrender. The plot leaked, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 至是，邵陵王綸率西豊公大春、新塗將軍永安侯確、超武將軍南安鄉侯駿、前譙州刺史趙伯超、武州刺史蕭弄璋、步兵校尉尹思合等，馬步三萬發自京口，直據鐘山。

translations.literal: At this time Prince of Shaoling Lun led Western Feng duke Dachun, New Tu general Marquis Que of Yong'an, Super-Martial general Marquis Jun of Nanxiang, former Qiao province inspector Zhao Bochao, Wu province inspector Xiao Nongzhang, Colonel of Footsoldiers Yin Sihe, and others—thirty thousand horse and foot setting out from Jingkou, directly taking Zhong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Then Prince of Shaoling Lun led Western Feng duke Dachun, New Tu general Marquis Que of Yong'an, Super-Martial general Marquis Jun of Nanxiang, former Qiao inspector Zhao Bochao, Wu inspector Xiao Nongzhang, Colonel of Footsoldiers Yin Sihe, and others—thirty thousand horse and foot from Jingkou, seizing Zhong Mountain outright.

sentences.zh: 景黨大駭，具船舟咸欲逃散，分遣萬餘人距綸，綸擊大破之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: Jing's faction was greatly terrified; all who had boats wanted to flee and scatter; he dispatched over ten thousand men to block Lun; Lun struck and routed them, cutting off over a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's men were terrified. Everyone with a boat wanted to flee. He sent ten thousand-odd men to stop Lun, but Lun routed them and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 旦日，景復陳兵覆舟山北，綸亦列陣以待之。

translations.literal: At dawn Jing again deployed troops north of Fuzhou Mountain; Lun also drew up ranks to await him.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Jing formed ranks north of Fuzhou Mountain. Lun lined up to meet him.

sentences.zh: 景不進，相持。

translations.literal: Jing did not advance—they faced off.
translations.idiomatic: Jing did not advance. The two armies stood facing each other.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，景引軍還，南安侯駿率數十騎挑之，景迴軍與戰，駿退。

translations.literal: At dusk Jing withdrew his army; Marquis Jun of Nan'an led several dozen horsemen to provoke him; Jing turned his army to fight—Jun retreated.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Jing pulled back. Marquis Jun of Nan'an rode out with several dozen men to taunt him. Jing turned and fought; Jun withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時趙伯超陳於玄武湖北，見駿急，不赴，乃率軍前走，衆軍因亂，遂敗績。

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Bochao was deployed north of Xuanwu Lake; seeing Jun in distress he did not go to help but instead led his army forward in flight—the army fell into disorder and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bochao was posted north of Xuanwu Lake. Seeing Jun in trouble, he did not go to his aid but fled forward with his own force. The army broke ranks and was routed.

sentences.zh: 綸奔京口。

translations.literal: Lun fled to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Lun fled back to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 賊盡獲輜重器甲，斬首數百級，生俘千餘人，獲西豊公大春、綸司馬莊丘惠達、直閣將軍胡子約、廣陵令霍儁等，來送城下徇之，逼云「已擒邵陵王」，儁獨云「王小小失利，已全軍還京口，城中但堅守，援軍尋至」。

translations.literal: The rebels captured all baggage, armor, and weapons, cut off several hundred heads, took over a thousand alive; they seized Western Feng duke Dachun, Lun's staff officer Zhuangqiu Huida, Direct Gate general Hu Ziyue, Guangling magistrate Huo Jun, and others; they were brought to the city wall and paraded; forced to say "The Prince of Shaoling has been captured," Jun alone said "My lord suffered a small setback and has returned with his full army to Jingkou—hold firm inside the city, relief will soon arrive."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took all baggage, armor, and arms, killed several hundred, and captured more than a thousand alive—including Western Feng duke Dachun, Lun's staff officer Zhuangqiu Huida, Direct Gate general Hu Ziyue, and Guangling magistrate Huo Jun. They were paraded beneath the wall and forced to cry that the Prince of Shaoling had been taken. Only Huo Jun said, "My lord met a small reverse and has returned whole to Jingkou. Hold the city—relief is near."

sentences.zh: 賊以刀毆之，儁言辭顏色如舊，景義而釋之。

translations.literal: The rebels beat him with swords; Jun's words and countenance remained as before; Jing admired his integrity and released him.
translations.idiomatic: They beat him with blades, but Jun's words and face never changed. Jing admired his courage and let him go.

sentences.zh: 是日，鄱陽世子嗣、裴之高至後渚，結營于蔡洲。

translations.literal: That day the Prince of Poyang's heir Si and Pei Zhigao reached Later Islet and encamped at Cai Isle.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Prince of Poyang's heir Si and Pei Zhigao reached Later Islet and camped on Cai Isle.

sentences.zh: 景分軍屯南岸。

translations.literal: Jing divided his army to garrison the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: Jing split his force to hold the south bank.

sentences.zh: 十二月，景造諸攻具及飛樓、橦車、登城車、登堞車、階道車、火車，並高數丈，一車至二十輪，陳於闕前，百道攻城並用焉。
