translations.literal: In the twelfth month Jing built all manner of siege engines—flying towers, ram wagons, scaling wagons, battlement-scaling wagons, ramp wagons, fire wagons—all several zhang high, some wagons with twenty wheels; arrayed before the palace gates, they were all used together in the hundred-direction assault.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Jing built every sort of siege engine—flying towers, rams, scaling wagons, battlement climbers, ramp carts, fire carts—each several zhang tall, some with twenty wheels. They stood before the palace gates and were all deployed in the hundred-direction assault.

sentences.zh: 以火車焚城東南隅大樓，賊因火勢以攻城，城上縱火，悉焚其攻具，賊乃退。

translations.literal: Using fire wagons they burned the great tower at the southeast corner of the city; the rebels used the blaze to press the assault; from the walls fire was released and all their siege engines were burned—the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fire wagons burned the great tower at the southeast corner. The rebels used the blaze to press the attack, but the defenders set counter-fires from the wall and burned every engine. The rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又築土山以逼城，城內作地道以引其土山，賊又不能立，焚其攻具，還入于柵。

translations.literal: They again built earthen mounds to press the city; inside the city they dug tunnels to undermine the mounds; the rebels could not hold—they burned their siege engines and retreated to their stockade.
translations.idiomatic: They raised earthworks again to press the city. Defenders dug tunnels to undercut the mounds. Unable to hold, the rebels burned their engines and fell back to their stockade.

sentences.zh: 材官將軍宋嶷降賊，因爲立計，引玄武湖水灌臺城，城外水起數尺，闕前御街並爲洪波矣。

translations.literal: Materials-and-works general Song Ni surrendered to the rebels and devised a plan: divert Xuanwu Lake water to flood Terrace City; outside the walls water rose several feet—the imperial avenue before the palace became a vast flood.
translations.idiomatic: Materials-and-works general Song Ni defected and advised diverting Xuanwu Lake to flood Terrace City. Water rose several feet outside the walls, and the imperial avenue before the palace became a surging flood.

sentences.zh: 又燒南岸民居營寺，莫不咸盡。

translations.literal: They also burned the south bank's dwellings and temples—none were spared.
translations.idiomatic: They burned the dwellings and temples on the south bank until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 司州刺史柳仲禮、衡州刺史韋粲、南陵太守陳文徹、宣猛將軍李孝欽等，皆來赴援。

translations.literal: Si province inspector Liu Zhongli, Heng province inspector Wei Can, Nanling administrator Chen Wenche, Proclamation-Fierce general Li Xiaoqin, and others all came to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: Si inspector Liu Zhongli, Heng inspector Wei Can, Nanling administrator Chen Wenche, Proclamation-Fierce general Li Xiaoqin, and others all marched to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽世子嗣、裴之高又濟江。

translations.literal: The Prince of Poyang's heir Si and Pei Zhigao also crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Poyang's heir Si and Pei Zhigao crossed the river as well.

sentences.zh: 仲禮營朱雀航南，裴之高營南苑，韋粲營青塘，陳文徹、李孝欽屯丹陽郡，鄱陽世子嗣營小航南，並緣淮造柵。

translations.literal: Zhongli encamped south of Zhuque Bridge; Pei Zhigao at South Park; Wei Can at Qingtang; Chen Wenche and Li Xiaoqin garrisoned Danyang commandery; the Prince of Poyang's heir Si south of Little Bridge—all built stockades along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli camped south of Zhuque Bridge; Pei Zhigao at South Park; Wei Can at Qingtang; Chen Wenche and Li Xiaoqin at Danyang; the Prince of Poyang's heir Si south of Little Bridge—all building stockades along the river.

sentences.zh: 及曉，景方覺，乃登禪靈寺門樓望之，見韋粲營壘未合，先渡兵擊之。

translations.literal: At dawn Jing finally noticed; he ascended the gate tower of Zen Spirit Temple to survey; seeing Wei Can's encampment not yet closed, he first sent troops across to strike.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Jing finally saw them. From the gate tower of Zen Spirit Temple he looked out, saw Wei Can's camp still open, and sent troops across first to strike.

sentences.zh: 粲拒戰敗績，景斬粲首徇於城下。

translations.literal: Can resisted but was defeated; Jing cut off Can's head and displayed it beneath the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: Can fought but was routed. Jing cut off his head and displayed it below the wall.

sentences.zh: 柳仲禮聞粲敗，不遑貫甲，與數十騎馳赴之，遇賊交戰，斬首數百，投水死者千餘人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhongli hearing of Can's defeat, without time to don full armor, galloped with several dozen horsemen to the rescue; he met the rebels in battle, cut off several hundred heads; over a thousand drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Can had fallen, Liu Zhongli galloped out with several dozen men before he could arm fully. He met the rebels, took several hundred heads, and more than a thousand drowned.

sentences.zh: 仲禮深入，馬陷泥，亦被重創。

translations.literal: Zhongli pressed deep in; his horse sank in mud and he too was badly wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli pressed too far in. His horse sank in mud, and he was badly wounded himself.

sentences.zh: 自是賊不敢濟岸。

translations.literal: From then the rebels dared not cross to the shore.
translations.idiomatic: After that the rebels dared not cross to the bank.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王綸與臨成公大連等自東道集于南岸，荊州刺史湘東王繹遣世子方等、兼司馬吳曄、天門太守樊文皎下赴京師，營于於湘子岸前，高州刺史李遷仕、前司州刺史羊鴉仁又率兵繼至。

translations.literal: Prince of Shaoling Lun and Duke of Lincheng Dalian and others gathered on the south bank from the eastern route; Jing province inspector Prince of Xiangdong Yi sent his heir Fangde, concurrent staff officer Wu Ye, and Tianmen administrator Fan Wenjiao down to the capital, encamping before Xiangzi Shore; Gaozhou inspector Li Qianshi and former Si province inspector Yang Yaren also led troops arriving in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shaoling Lun and Duke of Lincheng Dalian gathered on the south bank from the east. Jing inspector Prince of Xiangdong Yi sent his heir Fangde, staff officer Wu Ye, and Tianmen administrator Fan Wenjiao toward the capital, camping before Xiangzi Shore. Gaozhou inspector Li Qianshi and former Si inspector Yang Yaren followed with more troops.

sentences.zh: 旣而鄱陽世子嗣、永安侯確、羊鴉仁、李遷仕、樊文皎率衆渡淮，攻賊東府城前柵，破之，遂結營于青溪水東。

translations.literal: Soon the Prince of Poyang's heir Si, Marquis Que of Yong'an, Yang Yaren, Li Qianshi, and Fan Wenjiao led their forces across the Huai, attacked the rebels' stockade before the Eastern Palace city, broke it, and encamped east of Qingxi River.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Prince of Poyang's heir Si, Marquis Que of Yong'an, Yang Yaren, Li Qianshi, and Fan Wenjiao crossed the river, stormed the stockade before the Eastern Palace city, broke it, and camped east of Qingxi River.

sentences.zh: 景遣其儀同宋子仙頓南平王第，緣水西立柵相拒。

translations.literal: Jing sent his Yitong Song Zixian to station at the Prince of Nanping's residence and built stockades west along the water to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Jing posted Yitong Song Zixian at the Prince of Nanping's mansion and built stockades west along the water to block them.

sentences.zh: 景食稍盡，至是米斛數十萬人相食者十五六。

translations.literal: Jing's food gradually ran out; by then a hu of rice cost several hundred thousand—one or two in ten resorted to cannibalism.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's provisions dwindled. A hu of rice now cost several hundred thousand cash, and one or two people in ten turned to eating human flesh.

sentences.zh: 初，援兵至北岸，百姓扶老攜幼以候王師，才得過淮，便競剝掠，賊黨有欲自拔者，聞之咸止。

translations.literal: At first when relief troops reached the north bank, the people, supporting the old and leading the young, waited for the royal army; once they had just crossed the Huai they competed in plunder; rebels who wished to desert themselves, hearing this, all stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When relief first reached the north bank, people old and young waited for the royal army. But the moment troops crossed the river they looted one another. Rebels who meant to defect heard this and held back.

sentences.zh: 賊之始至，城中才得固守，平蕩之事，期望援軍。

translations.literal: When the rebels first arrived the city had barely managed to hold; for the task of pacification they looked to relief armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels first came, the city barely held. Everyone looked to the relief armies to finish the work.

sentences.zh: 旣而四方雲合，衆號百萬，連營相持，已月餘日，城中疾疫，死者太半。

translations.literal: Soon forces gathered from four directions, numbering in the millions by report, camps linked in stalemate for over a month; inside the city plague spread—more than half the people died.
translations.idiomatic: Forces gathered from every quarter, said to number a million. Camps faced one another for more than a month. Inside the city plague raged, and more than half the people died.

sentences.zh: 景自歲首以來乞和，朝廷未之許，至是事急乃聽焉。

translations.literal: Since the year's beginning Jing had begged for peace; the court did not grant it; now with matters urgent they agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the year's start Jing had asked for peace, and the court had refused. Now, with crisis pressing, they agreed.

sentences.zh: 請割江右四州之地，幷求宣城王大器出送，然後解圍濟江；

translations.literal: He requested ceding the four provinces of Jiangyou and also demanded Prince of Xuancheng Daqi be sent out as hostage, then he would lift the siege and cross the river;
translations.idiomatic: He asked to keep the four Jiangyou provinces and demanded that Prince of Xuancheng Daqi be sent out as hostage; then he would lift the siege and cross the river.

sentences.zh: 仍許遣其儀同于子悅、左丞王偉入城爲質。

translations.literal: he also permitted sending his Yitong Yu Ziyue and Left Director Wang Wei into the city as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: He also agreed to send his Yitong Yu Ziyue and Left Director Wang Wei into the city as hostages.

sentences.zh: 中領軍傅岐議以宣城王嫡嗣之重，不容許之。

translations.literal: Central Commandant Fu Qi argued that the Prince of Xuancheng as legitimate heir was too weighty to grant.
translations.idiomatic: Central Commandant Fu Qi argued that the Prince of Xuancheng, as legitimate heir, was too important to hand over.

sentences.zh: 乃請石城公大款出送，詔許焉。

translations.literal: They then requested Duke of Stone Fort Dakuan be sent out instead, and an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: They asked instead for Duke of Stone Fort Dakuan, and an edict approved.

sentences.zh: 遂於西華門外設壇，遣尚書僕射王克、兼侍中上甲鄉侯韶、兼散騎常侍蕭瑳與于子悅、王偉等，登壇共盟。

translations.literal: Thereupon outside the West Flower Gate an altar was set; Palace Secretary Wang Ke, concurrent Palace Attendant Marquis Shao of Shangjia township, and concurrent Palace Cadet Xiao Chuo with Yu Ziyue, Wang Wei, and others ascended the altar to swear the oath together.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the West Flower Gate they raised an altar. Palace Secretary Wang Ke, concurrent Palace Attendant Marquis Shao of Shangjia, and concurrent Palace Cadet Xiao Chuo joined Yu Ziyue, Wang Wei, and others on the altar to swear the pact.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍柳津出西華門下，景出其柵門，與津遙相對，刑牲歃血。

translations.literal: Left Guard general Liu Jin went out below the West Flower Gate; Jing came out his stockade gate—they faced each other from afar and swore by slaughtering victims and tasting blood.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard general Liu Jin went out below the West Flower Gate. Jing came out his stockade gate. They faced each other from afar and swore over slaughtered victims and blood.

sentences.zh: 南兗州刺史南康嗣王會理、前青、冀二州刺史湘潭侯退、西昌侯世子彧率衆三萬，至于馬邛州。

translations.literal: South Yanzhou inspector Prince of Nankang heir Huili, former Qing and Ji province inspector Marquis Tui of Xiangtan, and Heir of Marquis of Xichang Yu led thirty thousand men, reaching Magongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: South Yanzhou inspector Prince of Nankang heir Huili, former Qing and Ji inspector Marquis Tui of Xiangtan, and the Heir of Marquis of Xichang Yu led thirty thousand men to Magongzhou.

sentences.zh: 景慮北軍自白下而上，斷其江路，請悉勒聚南岸，敕乃遣北軍進江潭苑。

translations.literal: Jing feared northern forces ascending from Baixia would cut his river route; he requested all armies be mustered on the south bank; an edict then sent the northern army to advance into Jiangtan Park.
translations.idiomatic: Jing feared northern troops coming up from Baixia would cut his river line. He asked that all armies mass on the south bank. An edict then sent the northern force into Jiangtan Park.

sentences.zh: 景啓稱：「永安侯、趙威方頻隔柵見詬臣，云『天子自與汝盟，我終當逐汝』。

translations.literal: Jing petitioned: "Marquis Que of Yong'an and Zhao Wei frequently shout across the stockade at me, saying 'The Son of Heaven made peace with you himself—I will still drive you out.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing petitioned: "Marquis Que of Yong'an and Zhao Wei keep shouting across the stockade at me, 'The Son of Heaven made peace with you himself—I will still drive you out.'

sentences.zh: 乞召入城，卽當進發。

translations.literal: I beg they be summoned into the city—then I will advance.
translations.idiomatic: Summon them into the city, and I will advance at once.

sentences.zh: 」敕並召之。

translations.literal: " An edict summoned both.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict summoned them both.

sentences.zh: 景又啓云：「西岸信至，高澄已得壽春、鐘離，便無處安足。

translations.literal: Jing again petitioned: "Word has come from the west bank that Gao Cheng has taken Shouyang and Zhongli—there is nowhere left to stand.
translations.idiomatic: Jing petitioned again: "Word from the west bank says Gao Cheng has taken Shouyang and Zhongli. I have nowhere left to stand.

sentences.zh: 權借廣陵、譙州，須征得壽春、鐘離，卽以奉還朝廷。」

translations.literal: I beg to borrow Guangling and Qiao province temporarily; once I recover Shouyang and Zhongli I will return them to the court."
translations.idiomatic: Let me hold Guangling and Qiao for now. Once I recover Shouyang and Zhongli I will return them to the court."

sentences.zh: 初，彭城劉邈說景曰：「大將軍頓兵已久，攻城不拔，今援衆雲集，未易而破；

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Miao of Pengcheng said to Jing: "Great General, your army has halted long; the city cannot be taken; now relief forces gather like clouds—not easy to break;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Miao of Pengcheng told Jing: "Great General, you have stalled too long and still cannot take the city. Relief armies are massing like clouds—not easy to break now.

sentences.zh: 如聞軍糧不支一月，運漕路絕，野無所掠，嬰兒掌上，信在於今。

translations.literal: I hear army provisions won't last a month, transport routes are cut, nothing to plunder in the fields—a child in the palm, the truth lies in this day.
translations.idiomatic: I hear your grain will not last a month, your supply lines are cut, and the countryside is bare. The matter is like a child in the palm—the truth is plain today.

sentences.zh: 未若乞和，全師而返，此計之上者。

translations.literal: Better to beg peace, return with your army intact—this is the best plan."
translations.idiomatic: Better to sue for peace and withdraw whole. That is the best course."

sentences.zh: 」景然其言，故請和。

translations.literal: Jing agreed with his words and therefore sought peace.
translations.idiomatic: Jing accepted this and therefore asked for peace.

sentences.zh: 後知援軍號令不一，終無勤王之效；

translations.literal: Later learning that relief armies' orders were not unified and there would be no effect of loyal kings coming to the rescue;
translations.idiomatic: Later he learned the relief armies gave conflicting orders and would never truly save the throne.

sentences.zh: 又聞城中死疾轉多，必當有應之者。

translations.literal: and hearing that inside the city deaths and sickness grew ever more—there would surely be those who responded.
translations.idiomatic: He also heard that deaths and sickness inside the city kept mounting—surely someone would answer.

sentences.zh: 景謀臣王偉又說曰：「王以人臣舉兵背叛，圍守宮闕，已盈十旬，逼辱妃主，淩穢宗廟，今日持此，何處容身？

translations.literal: Jing's strategist Wang Wei also said: "My lord, as a subject you raised troops in rebellion, besieged and held the palace gates for over a hundred days, humiliated consorts and princesses, defiled the ancestral temple—with this on your hands today, where can you find shelter?
translations.idiomatic: Jing's counselor Wang Wei also said: "My lord, you rose in rebellion as a subject, besieged the palace for more than a hundred days, humiliated consorts and princesses, and defiled the ancestral temple. With that on your hands, where can you go?

sentences.zh: 願王且觀其變。

translations.literal: I wish my lord would watch for changes.
translations.idiomatic: Watch for what changes, my lord.

sentences.zh: 」景然之，乃抗表曰：

translations.literal: " Jing agreed and submitted a defiant memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: " Jing agreed and submitted a defiant memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞「書不盡言，言不盡意」。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard "writing cannot exhaust words, words cannot exhaust meaning."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that writing cannot exhaust words, and words cannot exhaust meaning.

sentences.zh: 然則意非言不宣，言非筆不盡，臣所以含憤蓄積，不能默已者也。

translations.literal: Yet meaning cannot be declared without words, words cannot be fully written without the brush—that is why your servant harbors indignation and cannot keep silent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet meaning needs words, and words need the brush. That is why your servant stores up anger and cannot stay silent.

sentences.zh: 竊惟陛下睿智在躬，多才多藝。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that Your Majesty possesses wisdom in person, many talents and many arts.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant considers that Your Majesty carries wisdom in your person and mastery in many arts.

sentences.zh: 昔因世季，龍翔漢、沔，夷凶剪亂，克雪家怨，然後踵武前王，光宅江表，憲章文、武，祖述堯、舜。

translations.literal: In past days amid a declining age you soared like a dragon over Han and Mian, quelled evil and cut disorder, avenged the house's grievance—then followed the former kings' footsteps, illuminated the lands south of the river, took Wen and Wu as models, claimed Yao and Shun as forebears.
translations.idiomatic: In a fallen age you rose like a dragon over Han and Mian, cut down the wicked and stilled chaos, and avenged your house. Then you followed the former kings, lit the lands south of the river, took Wen and Wu as your model, and claimed Yao and Shun as your line.

sentences.zh: 兼屬魏國淩遲，外無勍敵，故能西取華陵，北封淮、泗，結好高氏，輶軒相屬，疆埸無虞，十有餘載。

translations.literal: Moreover as Wei declined with no formidable foe abroad, you could take Hualing in the west, seal Huai and Si in the north, ally with the Gao clan—envoys' chariots unbroken, borders untroubled for over ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Wei declined abroad and you had no strong enemy, so you took Hualing in the west, sealed Huai and Si in the north, and allied with the Gao clan. Envoys came and went without cease, and the borders were quiet for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 躬覽萬機，劬勞治道。

translations.literal: You personally oversee all affairs, toiling at governance.
translations.idiomatic: You personally handle every affair and toil at governance.

sentences.zh: 刊正周、孔之遺文，訓釋真如之秘奧。

translations.literal: You revised the surviving texts of Zhou and Confucius, explicated the secret depths of True Suchness.
translations.idiomatic: You corrected the surviving texts of Zhou and Confucius and explained the hidden depths of True Suchness.

sentences.zh: 享年長久，本枝磐石。

translations.literal: Long-lived years, the root branch firm as bedrock.
translations.idiomatic: Long life, and the root branch firm as bedrock.

sentences.zh: 人君藝業，莫之與京。

translations.literal: No sovereign's accomplishments match yours.
translations.idiomatic: No ruler's achievements can match yours.

sentences.zh: 臣所以踴躍一隅，望南風而歎息也，豈圖名與實爽，聞見不同？

translations.literal: That is why your servant leapt with joy in my corner, sighed facing the south wind—who thought name and reality would diverge, that what I heard and what I see differ?
translations.idiomatic: That is why your servant rejoiced in my corner and sighed toward the south wind. Who thought name and reality would part, that what I heard and what I see would differ?

sentences.zh: 臣自委質策名，前後事蹟，從來表奏，已具之矣。

translations.literal: From the day I pledged loyalty and entered your rolls, my deeds before and after, memorials submitted—all have been set forth.
translations.idiomatic: From the day I pledged myself and entered your service, my deeds and memorials have already been laid out in full.

sentences.zh: 不勝憤懣，復爲陛下陳之：

translations.literal: Unable to contain my indignation, I again lay before Your Majesty:
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bear my anger, I lay this again before Your Majesty:

sentences.zh: 陛下與高氏通和，歲踰一紀，舟車往復，相望道路，必將分災卹患，同休等戚；

translations.literal: Your Majesty made peace with the Gao clan for over twelve years; boats and carts went back and forth, visible on every road—you were sure to share disaster and relieve suffering, share joy and grief alike;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty was at peace with the Gao clan for more than twelve years. Boats and carts traveled back and forth on every road—you were bound to share disaster and ease suffering, to share joy and grief alike.

sentences.zh: 寧可納臣一介之服，貪臣汝、潁之地，便絕好河北，檄詈高澄，聘使未歸，陷之虎口，揚兵擊鼓，侵逼彭、宋。

translations.literal: how could you receive one thread-worn servant, covet my lands of Ru and Ying, then sever friendship with Hebei, send indictments cursing Gao Cheng—envoys not yet returned, trap him in the tiger's maw, raise drums and troops pressing Peng and Song?
translations.idiomatic: How could you take in one worn servant, covet my lands of Ru and Ying, then break with Hebei, send indictments cursing Gao Cheng, trap his envoys in a tiger's maw before they returned, and march drums and troops against Peng and Song?

sentences.zh: 夫敵國相伐，聞喪則止，匹夫之交，托孤寄命。

translations.literal: When enemy states attack each other, they halt on hearing of mourning; even a common man's friendship trusts orphans and entrusts lives.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy states fight, they stop at news of mourning. Even a common man's bond can hold orphans and entrust lives.

sentences.zh: 豈有萬乘之主，見利忘義若此者哉！

translations.literal: Can there be a lord of ten thousand chariots who forgets righteousness at sight of profit like this!
translations.idiomatic: Can a lord of ten thousand chariots forget righteousness for profit like this!

sentences.zh: 其失一也。

translations.literal: This is your first fault.
translations.idiomatic: That is your first fault.

sentences.zh: 臣與高澄，旣有仇憾，義不同國，歸身有道。

translations.literal: Your servant and Gao Cheng have old hatred; righteousness bars sharing a state—I turned to the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant and Gao Cheng bear old hatred. Righteousness forbids sharing one state, so I turned to the Way.

sentences.zh: 陛下授以上將，任以專征，歌鐘女樂，車服弓矢。

translations.literal: Your Majesty granted me the title of Grand General, entrusted me with sole command, song bells, female musicians, chariots, robes, bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty made me grand general, gave me sole command, song bells, female musicians, chariots, robes, bows, and arrows.

sentences.zh: 臣受命不辭，實思報效。

translations.literal: I accepted the commission without demur, truly intending to repay it with service.
translations.idiomatic: I took the commission without hesitation, meaning to repay it in full.

sentences.zh: 方欲掛旆嵩、華，懸旌冀、趙，劉夷蕩滌，一匡宇內；

translations.literal: I meant to plant my banners on Song and Hua, raise my standards in Ji and Zhao, sweep away and cleanse Liu Yi, and restore order under Heaven—
translations.idiomatic: I meant to plant banners on Song and Hua, raise standards in Ji and Zhao, sweep the land clean, and set the realm right—

sentences.zh: 陛下朝服濟江，告成東岳，使大梁與軒黃等盛，臣與伊、呂比功，垂裕後昆，流名竹帛，此實生平之志也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty would cross the river in court robes, announce completion at the Eastern Peak, make Great Liang equal in splendor to Xuanyuan and Huangdi, and I would rank with Yi Yin and Lü Shang in merit, grace the generations after, and leave my name in the annals—this was truly my life's ambition.
translations.idiomatic: You would cross the river in court robes, proclaim victory at the Eastern Peak, lift Great Liang to the glory of Xuanyuan and Huangdi, and I would stand beside Yi Yin and Lü Shang in fame—blessing posterity, my name in the histories. That was my life's wish.

sentences.zh: 而陛下欲分其功，不能賜任，使臣擊河北，欲自舉徐方，遣庸懦之貞陽，任驕貪之胡、趙，裁見旗鼓，鳥散魚潰，慕容紹宗乘勝席捲，渦陽諸鎮靡不棄甲。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty wanted to share the credit, would not grant me free command, had me strike Hebei while intending to raise Xu Province yourself, sent the weak and timid Zhenyáng, put arrogant and greedy Hu and Zhao in charge—and at the first sight of banners and drums they scattered like birds and broke like fish. Murong Shaozong rode the victory in a sweeping tide, and every fortress at Woyang cast off its armor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you wanted to share the glory, withheld full command, sent me against Hebei while you meant to raise Xu yourself, put timid Zhenyáng in the field and arrogant, greedy Hu and Zhao in charge—and at the first drum they broke like fish in a net. Murong Shaozong swept the victory onward, and every Woyang garrison threw down its arms.

sentences.zh: 疾雷不及掩耳，散地不可固全，使臣狼狽失據，妻子爲戮，斯實陛下負臣之深。

translations.literal: Thunder comes too fast to cover the ears; scattered ground cannot be held firm. You left me disheveled, stripped of position, my wife and children slaughtered—this is how deeply Your Majesty has wronged me.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder strikes before you can cover your ears; scattered ground cannot be held. You left me ruined and bereft, my wife and children killed—this is how deeply you have wronged me.

sentences.zh: 其失二也。

translations.literal: This was fault two.
translations.idiomatic: That was the second fault.

sentences.zh: 韋黯之守壽陽，衆無一旅，慕容凶銳，欲飲馬長江，非臣退保淮南，其勢未之可測。

translations.literal: Wei An held Shouyang with fewer than a regiment; Murong's army was savage and sharp, intending to water their horses in the Yangtze. Had I not withdrawn to hold the Huai south, their momentum could not have been gauged.
translations.idiomatic: Wei An held Shouyang with less than a brigade while Murong's fierce troops meant to water their horses in the Yangtze. Had I not fallen back to the south Huai, no one could have guessed what would follow.

sentences.zh: 旣而逃遁，邊境獲寧，令臣作牧此州，以爲蕃捍。

translations.literal: Once he fled, the borderlands found peace, and Your Majesty made me governor of this province as a barrier defense.
translations.idiomatic: Once he fled the border quieted, and you made me governor here as a frontier shield.

sentences.zh: 方欲收合餘燼，勞來安集，勵兵秣馬，剋申後戰，封韓山之屍，雪渦陽之恥。

translations.literal: I was just gathering the embers, comforting and settling the survivors, sharpening troops and feeding horses, to renew the fight, bury the dead of Hanshan, and wash away the shame of Woyang.
translations.idiomatic: I was gathering the survivors, settling the people, sharpening arms and feeding horses, to fight again—bury Hanshan's dead and wipe away Woyang's shame.

sentences.zh: 陛下喪其精魄，無復守氣，便信貞陽謬啓，復請通和。

translations.literal: Your Majesty lost your spirit and could no longer hold resolve; you believed Zhenyáng's false reports and again sought peace.
translations.idiomatic: You lost heart entirely, believed Zhenyáng's lying dispatches, and again sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 臣頻陳執，疑閉不聽。

translations.literal: I repeatedly stated my firm view, yet you shut your ears in suspicion and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: I argued again and again, yet you closed your ears in suspicion and refused to hear me.

sentences.zh: 翻覆若此，童子猶且羞之；

translations.literal: To turn about like this—even a child would be ashamed;
translations.idiomatic: To flip back and forth like this—even a child would blush;

sentences.zh: 況在人君，二三其德。

translations.literal: how much more a sovereign, whose virtue should not waver.
translations.idiomatic: how much more a ruler whose word should stand firm.

sentences.zh: 其失三也。

translations.literal: This was fault three.
translations.idiomatic: That was the third fault.

sentences.zh: 夫畏懦逗留，軍有常法。

translations.literal: Cowardice and delay in the field have fixed military law.
translations.idiomatic: Cowardice and delay on campaign are punished by fixed military law.

sentences.zh: 子玉小敗，見誅於楚；

translations.literal: Ziyu suffered a small defeat and was put to death by Chu;
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu lost a minor battle and Chu put him to death;

sentences.zh: 王恢失律，受戮於漢。

translations.literal: Wang Hui broke discipline and was executed by Han.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui violated command and Han executed him.

sentences.zh: 貞陽精甲數萬，器械山積，慕容輕兵，衆無百乘，不能拒抗，身受囚執。

translations.literal: Zhenyáng had tens of thousands in fine armor, weapons piled like hills; Murong's light troops numbered fewer than a hundred chariots—and yet Zhenyáng could not resist and was taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyáng had tens of thousands in fine armor and weapons heaped like hills; Murong's light force was less than a hundred chariots wide—yet Zhenyáng could not hold and was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 以帝之猶子，而面縛敵庭，實宜絕其屬籍，以釁征鼓。

translations.literal: As the Emperor's own nephew, bound face-forward in the enemy camp, he should have been struck from the clan rolls and offered as blood on the war drums.
translations.idiomatic: As the Emperor's own nephew, bound before the enemy, he should have been cut from the clan register and offered to the war drums.

sentences.zh: 陛下曾無追責，憐其苟存，欲以微臣，規相貿易。

translations.literal: Your Majesty never pursued blame; pitying his bare survival, you meant to trade me for him.
translations.idiomatic: You never held him to account; pitying his survival, you meant to trade me away for him.

sentences.zh: 人君之法，當如是哉？

translations.literal: Is this how a sovereign's law should run?
translations.idiomatic: Is this how a ruler's law should work?

sentences.zh: 其失四也。

translations.literal: This was fault four.
translations.idiomatic: That was the fourth fault.

sentences.zh: 懸瓠大籓，古稱汝、潁。

translations.literal: Xuanchuo was a great frontier prefecture, anciently called Ru and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanchuo was a great frontier command, anciently known as Ru and Ying.

sentences.zh: 臣舉州內附，羊鴉仁固不肯入；

translations.literal: I brought the whole province over in submission, yet Yang Yaren stubbornly refused to enter;
translations.idiomatic: I brought the whole province over to you, yet Yang Yaren would not enter it;

sentences.zh: 旣入之後，無故棄之，陛下曾無嫌責，使還居北司。

translations.literal: and once he entered, he abandoned it for no cause. Your Majesty never reproached him and had him return to North Si.
translations.idiomatic: and once he did enter, he abandoned it for no reason. You never blamed him and sent him back to North Si.

sentences.zh: 鴉仁棄之，旣不爲罪，臣得之不以爲功。

translations.literal: Yaren abandoned it without penalty; I gained it without credit.
translations.idiomatic: Yaren lost it without punishment; I took it without reward.

sentences.zh: 其失五也。

translations.literal: This was fault five.
translations.idiomatic: That was the fifth fault.

sentences.zh: 臣渦陽退衂，非戰之罪，實由陛下君臣相與見誤。

translations.literal: My withdrawal from Woyang was no fault of battle—it came from Your Majesty and your ministers jointly misleading one another.
translations.idiomatic: My retreat from Woyang was no defeat in the field—it came from you and your ministers misleading one another.

sentences.zh: 乃還壽春，曾無悔色，祗奉朝廷，掩惡揚善。

translations.literal: Yet he returned to Shouyang without a trace of shame, reverently serving the court, hiding evil and proclaiming good.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he returned to Shouyang unashamed, dutiful toward the court, hiding faults and praising virtues.

sentences.zh: 鴉仁自知棄州，切齒歎恨，內懷慚懼，遂啓臣欲反。

translations.literal: Yaren knew he had abandoned the province; grinding his teeth in regret, ashamed and afraid within, he then reported that I meant to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Yaren knew he had abandoned the province; gnashing his teeth in shame and fear, he then reported that I meant to rebel.

sentences.zh: 欲反當有形迹，何所徵驗？

translations.literal: Rebellion should leave traces—what proof was there?
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion ought to leave signs—what evidence was there?

sentences.zh: 誣陷頓爾，陛下曾無辯究，默而信納。

translations.literal: The slander came so abruptly, yet Your Majesty never examined it and silently believed.
translations.idiomatic: The accusation came out of nowhere, yet you never investigated and silently believed it.

sentences.zh: 豈有誣人莫大之罪，而可並肩事主者乎？

translations.literal: How can one who bears the greatest crime of false accusation still serve the lord shoulder to shoulder?
translations.idiomatic: How can a man guilty of the gravest slander still stand beside his lord in service?

sentences.zh: 其失六也。

translations.literal: This was fault six.
translations.idiomatic: That was the sixth fault.

sentences.zh: 趙伯超拔自無能，任居方伯，惟漁獵百姓，多蓄士馬，非欲爲國立功，直是自爲富貴，行貨權幸，徼買聲名。

translations.literal: Zhao Bochao was promoted though utterly without talent; as a frontier governor he only plundered the people and amassed troops and horses—not to serve the state but to enrich himself, bribing the powerful for fame bought at a price.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bochao was raised from nothing though he had no ability; as a frontier governor he preyed on the people and hoarded troops and horses—not to serve the state but to make himself rich, bribing the powerful and buying a name.

sentences.zh: 朱异之徒，積受金貝，遂使咸稱胡、趙，比昔關、張，誣掩天聽，謂爲真實。

translations.literal: Zhu Yi and his kind, having amassed gold and shells, made all call Hu and Zhao the equals of Guan and Zhang of old, deceiving Heaven's ear into taking it for truth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi and his circle, fat with gold and treasure, made everyone call Hu and Zhao the equals of Guan and Zhang, deceiving the throne into believing it.

sentences.zh: 韓山之役，女妓自隨，裁聞敵鼓，與妾俱逝，不待貞陽，故只輪莫返。

translations.literal: At Hanshan he brought courtesans in his train; at the first enemy drum he fled with his concubines, not waiting for Zhenyáng—so not a single wheel returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanshan he brought singing girls with him; at the first enemy drum he fled with his concubines, never waiting for Zhenyáng—not one chariot wheel came back.

sentences.zh: 論其此罪，應誅九族；

translations.literal: For this crime he deserved execution to the ninth degree;
translations.idiomatic: For that crime he deserved death to the ninth degree of kin;

sentences.zh: 而納賄中人，還處州任。

translations.literal: yet after bribing the palace eunuchs he returned to his provincial post.
translations.idiomatic: yet after bribing the inner court he returned to his provincial post.

sentences.zh: 伯超無罪，臣功何論？

translations.literal: Bochao went unpunished—what reckoning did my merit receive?
translations.idiomatic: Bochao went free—what credit did my service receive?

sentences.zh: 賞罰無章，何以爲國？

translations.literal: When reward and punishment have no rule, how can there be a state?
translations.idiomatic: When reward and punishment have no order, how can a state endure?

sentences.zh: 其失七也。

translations.literal: This was fault seven.
translations.idiomatic: That was the seventh fault.

sentences.zh: 臣禦下素嚴，無所侵物，關市征稅，咸悉停原，壽陽之民，頗懷優復。

translations.literal: I have always governed strictly without seizing property; market tolls were all remitted, and the people of Shouyang enjoyed real relief.
translations.idiomatic: I have always ruled strictly and taken nothing from the people; market taxes were all waived, and the folk of Shouyang knew real relief.

sentences.zh: 裴之悌等助戍在彼，憚臣檢制，遂無故遁歸；

translations.literal: Pei Zhidi and others who garrisoned there feared my oversight and fled home without cause;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhidi and others who helped garrison there feared my discipline and fled home without cause;

sentences.zh: 又啓臣欲反。

translations.literal: and again reported that I meant to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: and again reported that I meant to rebel.

sentences.zh: 陛下不責違命離局，方受其浸潤之譖。

translations.literal: Your Majesty did not punish their dereliction but instead swallowed their soaked-in slander.
translations.idiomatic: You did not punish their desertion but swallowed their dripping slander instead.

sentences.zh: 處臣如此，使何地自安？

translations.literal: Treat me thus—where could I find peace?
translations.idiomatic: Treat me like this—where could I rest secure?

sentences.zh: 其失八也。

translations.literal: This was fault eight.
translations.idiomatic: That was the eighth fault.

sentences.zh: 臣雖才謝古人，實頗更事，撫民率衆，自幼至長，少來運動，多無遺策。

translations.literal: Though my talent falls short of the ancients, I have seen much service; from youth to age, leading people and troops, I have seldom moved without a plan left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am no match for the ancients in talent, I have seen much of war; from youth to age, leading people and armies, I have rarely acted without a plan that held.

sentences.zh: 及歸身有道，罄竭忠規，每有陳奏，恒被抑遏。

translations.literal: Since I submitted to the Way, I have poured out loyal counsel—yet every memorial was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Since I submitted to your court I have poured out loyal counsel—yet every memorial was stifled.

sentences.zh: 朱异專斷軍旅，周石珍總尸兵杖，陸驗、徐驎典司穀帛，皆明言求貨，非令不行。

translations.literal: Zhu Yi monopolized military decisions; Zhou Shizhen controlled arms; Lu Yan and Xu Lin managed grain and cloth—all openly demanding bribes, without which no order would pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi ruled the armies alone; Zhou Shizhen held all weapons; Lu Yan and Xu Lin controlled grain and cloth—all openly asking for bribes, and nothing moved without payment.

sentences.zh: 境外虛實，定計於舍人之省；

translations.literal: The truth beyond the borders was decided in the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: The enemy's strength beyond the border was decided in the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 舉將出師，責奏於主者之命。

translations.literal: generals were chosen and campaigns launched only after reports reached the chief clerk's desk.
translations.idiomatic: generals were chosen and armies sent out only after reports reached the chief clerk's desk.

sentences.zh: 臣無賄於中，故恒被抑折。

translations.literal: I bribed no one at court, and so was constantly overruled.
translations.idiomatic: I paid no one in the inner court, and so was constantly overruled.

sentences.zh: 其失九也。

translations.literal: This was fault nine.
translations.idiomatic: That was the ninth fault.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽之鎮合肥，與臣鄰接。

translations.literal: Poyang garrisoned Hefei, bordering my territory.
translations.idiomatic: Poyang held Hefei on my border.

sentences.zh: 臣推以皇枝，每相祗敬；

translations.literal: I honored him as imperial kin and always showed respect;
translations.idiomatic: I treated him as imperial kin and always showed respect;

sentences.zh: 而嗣王庸怯，虛見備御，臣有使命，必加彈射，或聲言臣反，或啓臣纖介。

translations.literal: yet the heir prince was timid and cowardly, shamming defense; whenever I had business he attacked—sometimes crying that I rebelled, sometimes reporting petty faults.
translations.idiomatic: yet the heir prince was timid and cowardly, pretending to guard the frontier; whenever I had business he attacked—sometimes crying rebellion, sometimes reporting petty faults.

sentences.zh: 招攜當須以禮，忠烈何以堪於此哉！

translations.literal: Winning loyalty requires courtesy—how can the loyal and fierce endure such treatment!
translations.idiomatic: Winning men requires courtesy—how can the loyal and fierce bear such treatment!

sentences.zh: 其失十也。

translations.literal: This was fault ten.
translations.idiomatic: That was the tenth fault.

sentences.zh: 其餘條目，不可具陳。

translations.literal: The remaining counts cannot all be listed.
translations.idiomatic: The rest cannot all be set down here.

sentences.zh: 進退惟谷，頻有表疏。

translations.literal: Advancing or retreating I walked a narrow gorge, memorial after memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Whether I advanced or withdrew I stood in peril, memorial after memorial.

sentences.zh: 言直辭強，有忤龍鱗，遂發嚴詔，便見討襲。

translations.literal: My words were blunt and my tone hard, touching the dragon's scales—so a stern edict was issued and I was marked for attack.
translations.idiomatic: My words were blunt and my tone fierce, touching the dragon's scales—so a stern edict came down and I was marked for attack.

sentences.zh: 重華純孝，猶逃凶父之杖；

translations.literal: Even Shun in pure filial piety fled his brutal father's staff;
translations.idiomatic: Even Shun, filial to the core, fled his brutal father's beating;

sentences.zh: 趙盾忠賢，不討殺君之賊。

translations.literal: Zhao Dun the loyal worthy did not pursue the regicide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dun the loyal minister did not hunt the king-killer.

sentences.zh: 臣何親何罪，而能坐受殲夷？

translations.literal: What kinship or crime do I have, that I should sit and accept annihilation?
translations.idiomatic: What kinship or crime do I have, that I should sit still and be destroyed?

sentences.zh: 韓信雄桀，亡項霸漢，末爲女子所烹，方悔蒯通之說。

translations.literal: Han Xin was a towering hero who destroyed Xiang Yu and helped Han rule—yet in the end a woman boiled him alive, and only then did he regret ignoring Kuai Tong's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin was a towering hero who overthrew Xiang Yu and helped Han rule—yet in the end a woman boiled him alive, and only then did he regret ignoring Kuai Tong.

sentences.zh: 臣每覽書傳，心常笑之。

translations.literal: Whenever I read that in the histories, I laugh in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read that in the histories I laugh to myself.

sentences.zh: 豈容遵彼覆車，而快陛下佞臣之手？

translations.literal: How could I follow that overturned cart and please Your Majesty's flatterers?
translations.idiomatic: How could I follow that overturned cart and please your sycophants?

sentences.zh: 是以興晉陽之甲，亂長江而直濟，願得升赤墀，踐文石，口陳枉直，指畫臧否，誅君側之惡臣，清國朝之粃政，然後還守籓翰，以保忠節，實臣之至願也。

translations.literal: Therefore I have raised the armor of Jinyang, crossed the Yangtze in disorder, hoping to ascend the red steps, tread the court stones, speak wrong and right with my mouth, mark good and ill with my hand, execute the evil ministers at the sovereign's side, cleanse the state's chaff from government, then return to guard the frontier and keep my loyalty—this is my deepest wish.
translations.idiomatic: So I have raised the armies of Jinyang, crossed the Yangtze in force, hoping to climb the red steps, stand on the court stones, speak wrong and right aloud, mark good and ill with my hand, kill the evil ministers at your side, purge the state's rotten policy, then return to guard the frontier and keep my loyalty—that is my deepest wish.

sentences.zh: 三月朔旦，城內以景違盟，舉烽鼓噪，於是羊鴉仁、柳敬禮、鄱陽世子嗣進軍於東府城北。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month, inside the city flames and drums rose because Jing had broken the treaty; then Yang Yaren, Liu Jingli, and the Poyang heir Si marched against the East Palace quarter's north wall.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month the city raised beacon fires and drums because Jing had broken the treaty; then Yang Yaren, Liu Jingli, and the Poyang heir Si advanced on the north wall of the East Palace quarter.

sentences.zh: 柵壘未立，爲景將宋子仙所襲，敗績，赴淮死者數千人。

translations.literal: Their ramparts were not yet finished when Jing's general Song Zixian struck them; they were routed, and thousands died drowning in the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Their palisades were not yet up when Jing's general Song Zixian struck them; they were routed, and thousands drowned in the Huai.

sentences.zh: 賊送首級於于闕下。

translations.literal: The rebels sent the severed heads to the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent the heads to the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 景又遣于子悅至，更請和。

translations.literal: Jing again sent Yu Ziyue to renew the plea for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Jing again sent Yu Ziyue to ask for peace once more.

sentences.zh: 遣御史中丞沈浚至景所，景無去意，浚固責之。

translations.literal: The court sent Censor-in-Chief Shen Jun to Jing's camp; Jing had no intent to leave, and Jun pressed him hard.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Censor-in-Chief Shen Jun to Jing's camp; Jing had no thought of leaving, and Jun pressed him hard.

sentences.zh: 景大怒，卽決石闕前水，百道攻城，晝夜不息，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Jing flew into rage, dammed the water before the Stone Gate, assaulted from a hundred directions day and night without rest, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Jing flew into rage, broke the water before the Stone Gate, and assaulted from a hundred directions day and night without pause until the city fell.

sentences.zh: 於是悉鹵掠乘輿服玩、後宮嬪妾，收王侯朝士送永福省，撤二宮侍衛。

translations.literal: Then he plundered the imperial regalia and palace women, gathered princes and court officials into Yongfu Province, and stripped both palaces of their guards.
translations.idiomatic: Then he looted the imperial carriage and regalia and the palace women, gathered princes and court officials into Yongfu Province, and stripped both palaces of their guards.

sentences.zh: 使王偉守武德殿，于子悅屯太極東堂，矯詔大赦天下，自爲大都督、督中外諸軍事、錄尚書，其侍中、使持節、大丞相、王如故。

translations.literal: He put Wang Wei in Wude Hall, garrisoned Yu Ziyue in the Eastern Hall of Taiji, forged an edict of general amnesty, and made himself Grand Commander of all armies at home and abroad, Recorder of the Masters of Writing—with his prior posts as Palace Attendant, Commissioner Bearing the Staff, Grand Chancellor, and Prince unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He put Wang Wei in Wude Hall, garrisoned Yu Ziyue in the Eastern Hall of Taiji, forged a general amnesty, and made himself Grand Commander of all armies at home and abroad and Recorder of the Masters of Writing—keeping his posts as Palace Attendant, Commissioner Bearing the Staff, Grand Chancellor, and Prince.

sentences.zh: 初，城中積屍不暇埋瘞，又有已死而未斂，或將死而未絕，景悉聚而燒之，臭氣聞十餘里。

translations.literal: At first corpses piled in the city too fast to bury; some dead unshrouded, some not yet dead—Jing gathered them all and burned them, and the stench carried ten li.
translations.idiomatic: At first corpses piled in the city faster than they could be buried; some dead and unshrouded, some not yet dead—Jing gathered them all and burned them, and the stench carried more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 尚書外兵郎鮑正疾篤，賊曳出焚之，宛轉火中，久而方絕。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant for External Armies Bao Zheng lay gravely ill; rebels dragged him out and burned him, twisting in the flames a long while before he died.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant for External Armies Bao Zheng lay gravely ill; rebels dragged him out and burned him alive, writhing in the fire a long while before he died.

sentences.zh: 於是援兵並散。

translations.literal: The relief armies then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The relief armies then broke apart.

sentences.zh: 景矯詔曰：「日者，姦臣擅命，幾危社稷，賴丞相英發，入輔朕躬，征鎮牧守可各復本任。

translations.literal: Jing forged an edict: "Recently wicked ministers seized command and nearly destroyed the state; thanks to the Chancellor's timely rise to assist Us in person, frontier generals and provincial governors may each resume their original posts.
translations.idiomatic: Jing forged an edict: "Recently wicked ministers seized command and nearly destroyed the state; thanks to the Chancellor's timely rise to assist Us in person, frontier generals and provincial governors may each resume their original posts.

sentences.zh: 」降蕭正德爲侍中、大司馬，百官皆復其職。

translations.literal: " He demoted Xiao Zhengde to Palace Attendant and Grand Marshal; all officials resumed their posts.
translations.idiomatic: " He demoted Xiao Zhengde to Palace Attendant and Grand Marshal, and all officials resumed their posts.

sentences.zh: 景遣董紹先率兵襲廣陵，南兗州刺史南康嗣王會理以城降之。

translations.literal: Jing sent Dong Shaoxian to storm Guangling; Inspector of South Yanzhou, Prince Huili of Nankang, surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent Dong Shaoxian to strike Guangling; Prince Huili of Nankang, inspector of South Yanzhou, surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 景以紹先爲南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Jing made Shaoxian Inspector of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing made Shaoxian inspector of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，北兗州刺史定襄侯祗與湘潭侯退，及前潼州刺史郭鳳同起兵，將赴援。

translations.literal: Earlier, Inspector of North Yanzhou Marquis Zhi of Dingxiang, Marquis Tui of Xiangtan, and former Inspector of Tongzhou Guo Feng had raised troops together to march to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Marquis Zhi of Dingxiang, inspector of North Yanzhou, Marquis Tui of Xiangtan, and former Tongzhou inspector Guo Feng had raised troops together to march to the relief.

sentences.zh: 至是，鳳謀以淮陰應景，祗等力不能制，並奔于魏。

translations.literal: Now Feng plotted to hand Huaiyin to Jing; Zhi and the others could not stop him and all fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Now Feng plotted to hand Huaiyin to Jing; Zhi and the others could not restrain him and all fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 景以蕭弄璋爲北兗州刺史，州民發兵拒之，景遣廂公丘子英、直閣將軍羊海率衆赴援，海斬子英，率其軍降于魏，魏遂據其淮陰。

translations.literal: Jing made Xiao Nongzhang Inspector of North Yanzhou; the province's people raised troops to resist. Jing sent Colonel Qiu Ziying and Direct Gate General Yang Hai to aid him; Hai killed Ziying and led his army to surrender to Wei, and Wei then held Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Jing made Xiao Nongzhang inspector of North Yanzhou; the province's people raised troops to resist. Jing sent Colonel Qiu Ziying and Direct Gate General Yang Hai to aid him; Hai killed Ziying, led his army to surrender to Wei, and Wei then held Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 景又遣儀同于子悅、張大黑率兵入吳，吳郡太守袁君正迎降。

translations.literal: Jing again sent Commandants Yu Ziyue and Zhang Dahei into Wu; Administrator of Wu Commandery Yuan Junzheng welcomed them and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jing again sent Commandants Yu Ziyue and Zhang Dahei into Wu; Wu commandery administrator Yuan Junzheng welcomed them and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 子悅等旣至，破掠吳中，多自調發，逼掠子女，毒虐百姓，吳人莫不怨憤，於是各立城柵拒守。

translations.literal: When Ziyue and the others arrived they ravaged Wu, requisitioning wildly, seizing sons and daughters, brutalizing the people—every man in Wu nursed rage, and each district raised palisades to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyue and the others arrived they ravaged Wu, requisitioning at will, seizing sons and daughters, brutalizing the people—every man in Wu nursed rage, and each district raised palisades to resist.

sentences.zh: 是月，景移屯西州，遣儀同任約爲南道行臺，鎮姑孰。

translations.literal: That month Jing shifted camp to West Province and sent Commandant Ren Yue as Southern Route Mobile Headquarters, garrisoning Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: That month Jing moved camp to West Province and sent Commandant Ren Yue as Southern Route Mobile Headquarters to garrison Gushu.

sentences.zh: 五月，高祖崩于文德殿。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Gaozu died in Wende Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Gaozu died in Wende Hall.

sentences.zh: 初，臺城旣陷，景先遣王偉、陳慶入謁高祖，高祖曰：「景今安在？

translations.literal: When the Terrace City fell, Jing first sent Wang Wei and Chen Qing to call on Gaozu. Gaozu asked, "Where is Jing now?
translations.idiomatic: When the Terrace City fell, Jing first sent Wang Wei and Chen Qing to call on Gaozu. Gaozu asked, "Where is Jing now?

sentences.zh: 卿可召來。

translations.literal: Summon him here."
translations.idiomatic: Summon him here."

sentences.zh: 」時高祖坐文德殿，景乃入朝，以甲士五百人自衛，帶劍升殿。

translations.literal: Gaozu sat in Wende Hall; Jing then came to court with five hundred armored men as escort, wearing his sword as he ascended the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sat in Wende Hall; Jing then came to court with five hundred armored men as escort, sword at his side as he climbed the steps.

sentences.zh: 拜訖，高祖問曰：「卿在戎日久，無乃爲勞？

translations.literal: After the bow Gaozu asked, "You have been long in the field—is it not weary work?"
translations.idiomatic: After the bow Gaozu asked, "You have been long in the field—is the work not wearying?"

sentences.zh: 」景默然。

translations.literal: Jing was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said nothing.

sentences.zh: 又問：「卿何州人，而敢至此乎？

translations.literal: Again he asked, "What province are you from, that you dare come here?"
translations.idiomatic: Again he asked, "What province are you from, that you dare come here?"

sentences.zh: 」景又不能對，從者代對。

translations.literal: Jing could not answer; a follower replied for him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing could not answer; a follower answered for him.

sentences.zh: 及出，謂廂公王僧貴曰：「吾常據鞍對敵，矢刃交下，而意氣安緩，了無怖心。

translations.literal: On leaving, he said to Colonel Wang Senggui: "I have often sat my saddle facing the enemy, arrows and blades falling together, yet my spirit stayed easy—I had no fear at all.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving, he said to Colonel Wang Senggui: "I have often sat my saddle facing the enemy, arrows and blades falling together, yet my spirit stayed easy—I had no fear at all.

sentences.zh: 今日見蕭公，使人自懾，豈非天威難犯？

translations.literal: Today meeting Lord Xiao makes one quail of oneself—is this not an inviolable heavenly majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Today, meeting Lord Xiao, I felt myself shrink with awe. Is that not majesty Heaven itself makes untouchable?

sentences.zh: 吾不可再見之。

translations.literal: I cannot meet him again.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot face him again.

sentences.zh: 」高祖雖外跡已屈，而意猶忿憤，時有事奏聞，多所譴卻。

translations.literal: " Gaozu, though outwardly he had submitted, still harbored wrath within; whenever matters were reported he often sent them back with reprimands.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu had bowed in appearance, but rage still burned in him. Memorial after memorial came up; he rejected most with sharp rebuke.

sentences.zh: 景深敬憚，亦不敢逼。

translations.literal: Jing deeply respected and feared him, and also did not dare press hard.
translations.idiomatic: Jing held him in deep awe and did not dare push further.

sentences.zh: 景遣軍人直殿省內，高祖問制局監周石珍曰：「是何物人？

translations.literal: Jing sent soldiers straight into the Palace Secretariat; Gaozu asked Director of the Bureau of Manufactures Zhou Shizhen: "What sort of people are these?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing posted soldiers inside the Palace Secretariat. Gaozu asked Zhou Shizhen, director of the bureau of manufactures, "What sort of men are these?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「丞相。

translations.literal: He answered: "The Chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The chancellor."

sentences.zh: 」高祖乃謬曰：「何物丞相？

translations.literal: Gaozu then pretended confusion: "What sort of chancellor?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu feigned ignorance. "What chancellor?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「是侯丞相。

translations.literal: He answered: "It is Chancellor Hou."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Chancellor Hou."

sentences.zh: 」高祖怒曰：「是名景，何謂丞相！

translations.literal: Gaozu angrily said: "His name is Jing—why call him chancellor!"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu flared. "His name is Jing. Why call him chancellor!"

sentences.zh: 」是後，每所徵求，多不稱旨，至於御膳亦被裁抑，遂憂憤感疾而崩。

translations.literal: " After that, every request mostly failed to please; even the imperial meals were cut back, and he finally fell ill from grief and anger and died.
translations.idiomatic: " After that Jing's every demand missed the mark. Even the imperial table was pared back. Gaozu sickened from grief and rage, and died.

sentences.zh: 景乃密不發喪，權殯于昭陽殿，自外文武咸莫知之。

translations.literal: Jing then secretly withheld announcement of death; the coffin was provisionally placed in Zhaoyang Hall, and outside the palace none of civil or military officers knew.
translations.idiomatic: Jing kept the death secret. The coffin lay provisionally in Zhaoyang Hall, and outside the palace no civil or military officer knew.

sentences.zh: 二十餘日，升梓宮於太極前殿，迎皇太子卽皇帝位。

translations.literal: After more than twenty days, the imperial coffin was raised to the front hall of Taiji and the crown prince was welcomed to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty days the imperial coffin was moved to the front hall of Taiji, and the crown prince was brought forward to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 於是矯詔赦北人爲奴婢者，冀收其力用焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon a forged edict pardoned northerners held as slave servants, hoping to gather their strength for use.
translations.idiomatic: A forged edict then freed northerners held as slaves and servants, hoping to win their labor and arms.

sentences.zh: 又遣儀同來亮率兵攻宣城，宣城內史楊華誘亮斬之；

translations.literal: He also sent Yitong Lai Liang to lead troops attacking Xuancheng; Xuancheng Administrator Yang Hua lured Liang and had him beheaded;
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Yitong Lai Liang against Xuancheng. Xuancheng administrator Yang Hua lured Liang in and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 景復遣其將李賢明討華，華以郡降。

translations.literal: Jing again sent his general Li Xianming to attack Hua; Hua surrendered the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent his general Li Xianming against Hua, and Hua surrendered the commandery.

sentences.zh: 景遣儀同宋子仙等率衆東次錢塘，新城戍主戴僧易據縣拒之。

translations.literal: Jing sent Yitong Song Zixian and others leading troops east to camp at Qiantang; Xincheng garrison commander Dai Shengyi held the county and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent Yitong Song Zixian and others east to Qiantang. Xincheng garrison commander Dai Shengyi held the county and blocked them.

sentences.zh: 是月，景遣中軍侯子鑒入吳軍，收于子悅、張大黑，還京誅之。

translations.literal: That month Jing sent Central Army Hou Zijian into the Wu armies, captured Yu Ziyue and Zhang Dahei, returned to the capital and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: That month Jing sent Central Army Hou Zijian into the Wu forces, seized Yu Ziyue and Zhang Dahei, returned to the capital, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 時東揚州刺史臨成公大連據州，吳興太守張嵊據郡，自南陵以上，皆各據守。

translations.literal: At the time East Yangzhou Inspector Prince of Lincheng Dalian held the province, Wuxing Administrator Zhang Song held the commandery; from Nanling upstream all held and defended separately.
translations.idiomatic: East Yangzhou inspector Prince of Lincheng Dalian held the province. Wuxing administrator Zhang Song held the commandery. From Nanling upstream each stronghold held its own ground.

sentences.zh: 景制命所行，惟吳郡以西、南陵以北而已。

translations.literal: Jing's orders could reach only west of Wu commandery and north of Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's commands ran only west of Wu commandery and north of Nanling.

sentences.zh: 六月，景以儀同郭元建爲尚書僕射、北道行臺、總江北諸軍事，鎮新秦。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Jing made Yitong Guo Yuanjian Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Northern Route Mobile Headquarters, overall command of Jiangbei military affairs, garrisoning at Xinqin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Jing made Yitong Guo Yuanjian vice director of the Masters of Writing, northern route mobile headquarters, and commander of all Jiangbei forces, garrisoning Xinqin.

sentences.zh: 郡人陸緝、戴文舉等起兵萬餘人，殺景太守蘇單于，推前淮南太守文成侯寧爲主，以拒景。

translations.literal: Commandery men Lu Ji, Dai Wenju and others raised troops of over ten thousand, killed Jing's administrator Su Chanyu, and pushed former Huainan Administrator Wen-cheng Marquis Ning as leader to resist Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji, Dai Wenju, and others in the commandery raised more than ten thousand men, killed Jing's administrator Su Chanyu, and set up former Huainan administrator Wen-cheng Marquis Ning to resist Jing.

sentences.zh: 宋子仙聞而擊之，緝等棄城走。

translations.literal: Song Zixian heard and attacked; Ji and the others abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zixian heard and struck. Ji and the rest abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 景乃分吳郡海鹽、胥浦二縣爲武原郡。

translations.literal: Jing then separated Wu commandery's Haiyan and Xupu two counties into Wuyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jing then split Haiyan and Xupu of Wu commandery into Wuyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 至是，景殺蕭正德於永福省。

translations.literal: By then Jing killed Xiao Zhengde at Yongfu Office.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jing killed Xiao Zhengde in Yongfu Office.

sentences.zh: 封元羅爲西秦王，元景龍爲陳留王，諸元子弟封王者十餘人。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Yuan Luo as Prince of Western Qin, Yuan Jinglong as Prince of Chenliu; over ten Yuan clan youths were enfeoffed as princes.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Yuan Luo as Prince of Western Qin and Yuan Jinglong as Prince of Chenliu; more than ten Yuan clansmen received princely titles.

sentences.zh: 以柳敬禮爲使持節、大都督，隸大丞相，參戎事。

translations.literal: He made Liu Jingli Bearer of the Staff and Grand Commander, subordinate to the Grand Chancellor, participating in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He made Liu Jingli bearer of the staff and grand commander under the Grand Chancellor, to share in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 景遣其中軍侯子鑒監行臺劉神茂等軍東討，破吳興，執太守張嵊父子送京師，景並殺之。

translations.literal: Jing sent his Central Army Hou Zijian to supervise Mobile Headquarters Liu Shenmao's army on eastern campaign; they broke Wuxing, seized Administrator Zhang Song father and son and sent them to the capital; Jing had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent Central Army Hou Zijian to oversee mobile headquarters Liu Shenmao's eastern campaign. They broke Wuxing, seized administrator Zhang Song and his son, sent them to the capital, and Jing had them all killed.

sentences.zh: 景以宋子仙爲司徒，任約爲領軍將軍，尒朱季伯、叱羅子通、彭儁、董紹先、張化仁、于慶、魯伯和、紇奚斤、史安和、時靈護、劉歸義，並爲開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Jing made Song Zixian Minister of Works, Ren Yue General of the Garrison Army; Erzhu Jibo, Chiluo Zitong, Peng Jun, Dong Shaoxian, Zhang Huaren, Yu Qing, Lu Bohe, Hexi Jin, Shi Anhe, Shi Linghu, and Liu Guiyi—all made Opened-Office Yitong of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Jing made Song Zixian minister of works and Ren Yue general of the garrison army. Erzhu Jibo, Chiluo Zitong, Peng Jun, Dong Shaoxian, Zhang Huaren, Yu Qing, Lu Bohe, Hexi Jin, Shi Anhe, Shi Linghu, and Liu Guiyi were all made opened-office yitong of the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 是月，鄱陽嗣王範率兵次柵口，江州刺史尋陽王大心要之西上。

translations.literal: That month Prince of Poyang successor Fan led troops to Zankou; Jiangzhou Inspector Prince of Xunyang Daxin invited him westward.
translations.idiomatic: That month Prince of Poyang successor Fan led troops to Zankou, and Jiangzhou inspector Prince of Xunyang Daxin asked him to come west.

sentences.zh: 景出頓姑孰，範將裴之悌、夏侯威生以衆降景。

translations.literal: Jing moved out and encamped at Gushu; Fan's generals Pei Zhi and Xiahou Weisheng surrendered their forces to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Jing moved out and encamped at Gushu. Fan's generals Pei Zhi and Xiahou Weisheng surrendered with their troops to Jing.

sentences.zh: 十一月，宋子仙攻錢塘，戴僧易降。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Song Zixian attacked Qiantang; Dai Shengyi surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Song Zixian attacked Qiantang, and Dai Shengyi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 景以錢塘爲臨江郡，富陽爲富春郡。

translations.literal: Jing made Qiantang Linjiang commandery and Fuyang Fuchun commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jing made Qiantang into Linjiang commandery and Fuyang into Fuchun commandery.

sentences.zh: 又王偉、元羅並爲儀同三司。

translations.literal: Wang Wei and Yuan Luo were also made Opened-Office Yitong of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei and Yuan Luo were also made opened-office yitong of the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 十二月，宋子仙、趙伯超、劉神茂進攻會稽，東揚州刺史臨成公大連棄城走，遣劉神茂追擒之。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Song Zixian, Zhao Bochao, and Liu Shenmao advanced to attack Kuaiji; East Yangzhou Inspector Prince of Lincheng Dalian abandoned the city and fled; Liu Shenmao was sent to pursue and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Song Zixian, Zhao Bochao, and Liu Shenmao attacked Kuaiji. East Yangzhou inspector Prince of Lincheng Dalian abandoned the city and fled; Liu Shenmao was sent in pursuit and captured him.

sentences.zh: 景以裴之悌爲使持節、平西將軍、合州刺史，以夏侯威生爲使持節、平北將軍、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Jing made Pei Zhi Bearer of the Staff, Pacification West General, and Hefei Inspector; Xiahou Weisheng Bearer of the Staff, Pacification North General, and South Yuzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Jing made Pei Zhi bearer of the staff, Pacification West General, and Hefei inspector, and Xiahou Weisheng bearer of the staff, Pacification North General, and South Yuzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 是月，百濟使至，見城邑丘墟，於端門外號泣，行路見者莫不灑淚。

translations.literal: That month Baekje envoys arrived; seeing the cities in ruins they wept outside the Main Gate, and passersby all wept.
translations.idiomatic: That month Baekje envoys arrived. Seeing the cities in ruins, they wailed outside the Main Gate, and every passerby wept.

sentences.zh: 景聞之大怒，送小莊嚴寺禁止，不聽出入。

translations.literal: Jing heard and was greatly enraged; he sent them to Minor Zhuangyan Temple under house arrest, forbidden to go in or out.
translations.idiomatic: Jing heard and was furious. He sent them to Minor Zhuangyan Temple under confinement, forbidden to enter or leave.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年正月，景矯詔自加班劍四十人，給前後部羽葆鼓吹，置左右長史、從事中郎四人。

translations.literal: First month of first year of Dabao: Jing forged an edict adding forty sword-bearers to his entourage, granting front and rear guard feather-canopies and martial music, and appointing four Left and Right Chief Clerks and Attending Cadres.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Dabao year one Jing forged an edict adding forty sword-bearers, granting front and rear guard feather-canopies and martial music, and appointing four left and right chief clerks and attending cadres.

sentences.zh: 前江都令祖皓起兵於廣陵，斬景刺史董紹先，推前太子舍人蕭勔爲刺史；

translations.literal: Former Jiangdu Magistrate Zu Hao raised troops at Guangling, beheaded Jing's inspector Dong Shaoxian, and pushed former Crown Prince House Steward Xiao Min as inspector;
translations.idiomatic: Former Jiangdu magistrate Zu Hao raised troops at Guangling, killed Jing's inspector Dong Shaoxian, and set up former crown prince house steward Xiao Min as inspector.

sentences.zh: 又結魏人爲援，馳檄遠近，將以討景。

translations.literal: He also allied with Wei people as allies, sent proclamations far and near, intending to attack Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He also sought Wei allies, sent proclamations far and wide, and prepared to march against Jing.

sentences.zh: 景聞之大懼，卽日率侯子鑒等出自京口，水陸並集。

translations.literal: Jing heard and was greatly afraid; that same day he led Hou Zijian and others out from Jingkou, land and water forces gathering together.
translations.idiomatic: Jing heard and was terrified. That same day he led Hou Zijian and others out from Jingkou, land and river forces massing together.

sentences.zh: 皓嬰城拒守，景攻城，陷之。

translations.literal: Hao closed the city and resisted; Jing attacked the city and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Hao shut the city and held out. Jing stormed it and took it.

sentences.zh: 景車裂皓以徇，城中無少長皆斬之。

translations.literal: Jing had Hao torn apart by chariots as a warning; everyone young and old in the city was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had Hao torn apart by chariots as a warning, then beheaded every soul in the city, young and old alike.

sentences.zh: 以侯子鑒監南兗州事。

translations.literal: He made Hou Zijian overseer of South Yanzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He put Hou Zijian in charge of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 是月，景召宋子仙還京口。

translations.literal: That month Jing summoned Song Zixian back to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: That month Jing recalled Song Zixian to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 四月，景以元思虔爲東道行臺，鎮錢塘。

translations.literal: Fourth month: Jing made Yuan Siqian Eastern Route Mobile Headquarters, garrisoning Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Jing made Yuan Siqian eastern route mobile headquarters and garrisoned him at Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 以侯子鑒爲南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He made Hou Zijian South Yanzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He made Hou Zijian South Yanzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 文成侯寧於吳西鄉起兵，旬日之間，衆至一萬，率以西上。

translations.literal: Wen-cheng Marquis Ning raised troops in the western townships of Wu; within ten days forces reached ten thousand, and he led them westward.
translations.idiomatic: Wen-cheng Marquis Ning raised troops in Wu's western townships. Within ten days his force reached ten thousand, and he led them west.

sentences.zh: 景廂公孟振、侯子榮擊破之，斬寧，傳首于景。

translations.literal: Jing's colonels Meng Zhen and Hou Zirong defeated them, beheaded Ning, and sent his head to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's colonels Meng Zhen and Hou Zirong broke them, beheaded Ning, and sent his head to Jing.

sentences.zh: 七月，景以秦郡爲西兗州，陽平郡爲北兗州。

translations.literal: Seventh month: Jing made Qin commandery Western Yanzhou, and Yangping commandery Northern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Jing made Qin commandery into Western Yanzhou and Yangping commandery into Northern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 任約、盧暉略攻晉熙郡，殺鄱陽世子嗣。

translations.literal: Ren Yue and Lu Huilue attacked Jinxi commandery and killed the Poyang heir prince Si.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yue and Lu Huilue attacked Jinxi commandery and killed Poyang heir prince Si.

sentences.zh: 景以王偉爲中書監。

translations.literal: Jing made Wang Wei Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jing made Wang Wei director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 任約進軍襲江州，江州刺史尋陽王大心降之。

translations.literal: Ren Yue advanced the army in a raid on Jiangzhou; Jiangzhou Inspector Prince of Xunyang Daxin surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yue marched against Jiangzhou. Jiangzhou inspector Prince of Xunyang Daxin surrendered to him.

sentences.zh: 世祖時聞江州失守，遣衛軍將軍徐文盛率衆軍下武昌，拒約。

translations.literal: When Shizu heard Jiangzhou had fallen, he sent Guard General Xu Wensheng leading the massed armies down to Wuchang to resist Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu heard Jiangzhou had fallen, he sent Guard General Xu Wensheng with the main armies down to Wuchang to block Yue.

sentences.zh: 景又矯詔自進位爲相國，封泰山等二十郡爲漢王，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，劍履上殿，如蕭何故事。

translations.literal: Jing again forged an edict advancing himself to Chancellor of State, enfeoffing twenty commanderies including Taishan as Prince of Han, exempt from hurrying at court, exempt from having his name spoken at salutation, permitted sword and shoes in the hall—following the precedent of Xiao He.
translations.idiomatic: Jing forged another edict promoting himself to chancellor of state and enfeoffing him as Prince of Han over twenty commanderies including Taishan, with privilege to enter court without haste, to be saluted without naming, and to wear sword and shoes in the hall—after the precedent of Xiao He.

sentences.zh: 景以柳敬禮爲護軍將軍，姜詢義爲相國左長史，徐洪爲左司馬，陸約爲右長史，沈衆爲右司馬。

translations.literal: Jing made Liu Jingli Protector General; Jiang Xunyi Chancellor of State Left Chief Clerk; Xu Hong Left Marshal; Lu Yue Right Chief Clerk; Shen Zhong Right Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Jing made Liu Jingli protector general, Jiang Xunyi left chief clerk to the chancellor of state, Xu Hong left marshal, Lu Yue right chief clerk, and Shen Zhong right marshal.

sentences.zh: 是月，景率舟師上皖口。

translations.literal: That month Jing led his fleet up to Wankou.
translations.idiomatic: That month Jing led his fleet up the river to Wankou.

sentences.zh: 十月，盜殺武林侯諮于廣莫門。

translations.literal: Tenth month: robbers killed Marquis of Wulin Zi at Guangmo Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month robbers killed Marquis of Wulin Zi at Guangmo Gate.

sentences.zh: 諮常出入太宗臥內，景党不能平，故害之。

translations.literal: Zi often went in and out of Taizong's bedchamber; Jing's faction could not stomach it, and so killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zi often entered and left Taizong's bedchamber. Jing's men could not abide it, and so they killed him.

sentences.zh: 景又矯詔曰：「蓋懸象在天，四時取則於辰斗；

translations.literal: Jing again forged an edict: "For the suspended images are in Heaven; the four seasons take their rule from Chen and Dou;
translations.idiomatic: Jing forged another edict: "Heaven hangs its signs on high; the four seasons take their measure from the stars of Chen and Dou.

sentences.zh: 羣生育地，萬物仰照於大明。

translations.literal: the myriad creatures are born on Earth; all things look to the Bright Illuminator for light.
translations.idiomatic: All living things are born on earth and turn to the great brightness for light.

sentences.zh: 是以垂拱當扆，則八枿共輳；

translations.literal: Thus in yielding governance at the throne, the eight pillars gather together;
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler sits in yielding governance, the eight pillars of the realm draw close as one wheel;

sentences.zh: 負圖正位，則九域同歸。

translations.literal: bearing the chart in correct position, the nine regions return as one.
translations.idiomatic: when he bears the chart in rightful place, the nine provinces return to a single allegiance.

sentences.zh: 故乃雲名水號之君，龍官人爵之後，莫不啓符河、洛，封禪岱宗，奔走四夷，來朝萬國。

translations.literal: Therefore from lords named for clouds and waters, dragon officials and human nobles—all opened their tally at the River and Luo, performed feng and shan at Mount Dai, rushed the four barbarians, and came to court from ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: So from lords named for clouds and rivers, from dragon officers and noble heirs of men—none failed to open their tally at the River and Luo, to perform feng and shan on Mount Tai, to drive the four quarters, and to come in homage from ten thousand states.

sentences.zh: 逖聽虞、夏，厥道彌新。

translations.literal: Listening afar to Yu and Xia, their Way grew ever new.
translations.idiomatic: Listening back to Yu and Xia, their Way grew ever fresh.

sentences.zh: 爰及商、周，未之或改。

translations.literal: Down to Shang and Zhou, none altered it.
translations.idiomatic: Down through Shang and Zhou, none changed it.

sentences.zh: 逮幽、厲不競，戎馬生郊；

translations.literal: Until You and Li lost vigor, war-horses were born in the suburbs;
translations.idiomatic: Then You and Li lost their strength, and war-horses foaled in the capital outskirts;

sentences.zh: 惠、懷失御，胡塵犯蹕。

translations.literal: Hui and Huai lost the reins, barbarian dust violated the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and Huai lost the reins, and barbarian dust fouled the imperial road.

sentences.zh: 遂使豺狼肆毒，侵穴伊、瀍；

translations.literal: So wolves and dogs ran rampant, burrowing into Yi and Luo;
translations.idiomatic: Wolves and dogs ran wild, gnawing at the heartlands of Yi and Luo;

sentences.zh: 獫狁孔熾，巢棲咸、洛。

translations.literal: the Xianyun blazed hot, nesting in Xian and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: the Xianyun burned bright and nested in Xian and Luo.

sentences.zh: 自晉鼎東遷，多歷年代，周原不復，歲實永久。

translations.literal: Since the Jin tripod moved east, many years have passed; the Zhou plains never restored—for ages unending.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin cauldron moved east, years piled into ages, and the plains of Zhou were never restored.

sentences.zh: 雖宋祖經略，中息遠圖，齊號和親，空勞冠蓋。

translations.literal: Though Emperor Wu of Song undertook strategy and briefly stilled distant plans, and Qi styled itself harmony in marriage, it toiled in vain with crowns and canopies.
translations.idiomatic: Though Emperor Wu of Song took up strategy and for a time checked distant ambition, and Qi spoke of harmony through marriage, crown and canopy achieved nothing but empty toil.

sentences.zh: 我大梁膺符作帝，出震登皇。

translations.literal: Our Great Liang received the tally and became emperor, emerged from the thunder and ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Our Great Liang received Heaven's mandate and took the throne, rising out of thunder to ascend the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 浹㝢歸仁，綿區飲化。

translations.literal: Within the four seas all returned in benevolence; across the realm all drank transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Within the four seas all returned in benevolence; across the realm all drank in royal transformation.

sentences.zh: 開疆辟土，跨瀚海以揚鑣；

translations.literal: Opening borders and spreading soil, spanning the Han Sea to whip the steeds;
translations.idiomatic: It opened borders and spread its soil, spanning the Han Sea to drive its steeds;

sentences.zh: 來庭入覲，等塗山而比轍。

translations.literal: coming to court and entering audience, equal to Tushan and matching wheels.
translations.idiomatic: it received envoys at court and in audience, matching the rites of Tushan, wheel following wheel.

sentences.zh: 玄龜出洛，白雉歸豊。

translations.literal: The black tortoise emerged from the Luo; the white pheasant returned to abundance.
translations.idiomatic: The black tortoise came forth from the Luo; the white pheasant returned to the capital of abundance.

sentences.zh: 鳥塞同文，胡天共軌。

translations.literal: Bird passes shared script; northern skies shared track.
translations.idiomatic: Bird barriers shared one script; northern heavens one wheel-track.

sentences.zh: 不謂高澄跋扈，虔劉魏邦，扇動華夷，不供王職，遂乃狼顧北侵，馬首南向。

translations.literal: Who expected Gao Cheng's overbearing wildness, slaughtering and ravaging Wei, stirring Huaxia, refusing royal service—then wolf-glanced north to invade, horse-head turned south.
translations.idiomatic: Who thought Gao Cheng would grow so overbearing—slaughtering and ravaging Wei, stirring all Huaxia, refusing the king's command—then turning wolf-eyed north to invade and horse-head south?

sentences.zh: 值天厭昏偽，醜徒數盡，龍豹應期，風雲會節。

translations.literal: When Heaven grew weary of dark falsehood and ugly minions' numbers were spent, dragon and leopard answered the season, wind and cloud met the conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven grew weary of dark falsehood; the ugly faction's days ran out. Dragon and leopard answered the season; wind and cloud met at the turning.

sentences.zh: 相國漢王，上德英姿，蓋惟天授；

translations.literal: Chancellor of State Prince of Han, supreme virtue and heroic countenance—surely Heaven's gift;
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor of State, Prince of Han, bears supreme virtue and a heroic mien—surely Heaven's gift;

sentences.zh: 雄謨勇略，出自懷抱。

translations.literal: bold stratagems and brave designs, born from the heart.
translations.idiomatic: bold stratagems and brave designs born straight from the heart.

sentences.zh: 珠魚表應，辰昴葉暉；

translations.literal: Pearl-fish marked the omen, Chen and Mao leaves shone;
translations.idiomatic: Pearl-fish marked the omen; Chen and Mao leaves caught the light;

sentences.zh: 剖析六韜，錙銖四履。

translations.literal: he parsed the Six Secret Treatises, weighed the Four Realms to a hair.
translations.idiomatic: he parsed the Six Secret Treatises and weighed the four quarters to a hair.

sentences.zh: 騰文豹變，鳳集虬翔；

translations.literal: Leaping patterns of the spotted leopard, phoenix gathered and dragonflies soared;
translations.idiomatic: Spotted leopard leapt in new patterns; phoenix gathered and horned dragon soared;

sentences.zh: 奮翼來儀，負圖而降。

translations.literal: spreading wings he came as an omen, bearing the chart he descended.
translations.idiomatic: spreading wings he came as an omen; bearing the chart he descended.

sentences.zh: 爰初秉律，實先啓行；

translations.literal: At first wielding law, he truly led the van;
translations.idiomatic: At first, wielding law, he truly led the van;

sentences.zh: 奉茲廟算，克除獯醜。

translations.literal: holding to the temple's calculations, he cut down the savage uglies.
translations.idiomatic: holding to the temple's calculations, he cut down the savage foe.

sentences.zh: 直以鼎湖上征，六龍晏駕；

translations.literal: Only because at Dinghu the Emperor ascended, the six dragons rested in stillness;
translations.idiomatic: Only because at Dinghu the Emperor ascended and the six dragons rested in stillness;

sentences.zh: 干戈暫止，九伐未申。

translations.literal: blades briefly halted, the nine punitive expeditions unproclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: blades halted for a time, and the nine punitive expeditions went unproclaimed.

sentences.zh: 而惡稔貫盈，元凶殞斃；

translations.literal: Yet evil ripened to fullness, the chief villain perished;
translations.idiomatic: Yet evil ripened to fullness, and the chief villain perished;

sentences.zh: 弟洋繼逆，續長亂階。

translations.literal: younger brother Yang continued the rebellion, prolonging chaos step by step.
translations.idiomatic: younger brother Yang carried on the rebellion, prolonging chaos step by step.
