sentences.zh: 異彼洋音，同茲荐食；

translations.literal: Unlike that Yang tone, same as this feasting on the people;
translations.idiomatic: Unlike that Yang in name alone, alike in devouring the people;

sentences.zh: 偷竊偽號，心希舉斧。

translations.literal: stealing a false title, in heart aspiring to the uplifted axe.
translations.idiomatic: stealing a false title, in heart reaching for the uplifted axe.

sentences.zh: 豊水君臣，奉圖乞援；

translations.literal: Feng River's lord and ministers, offered the chart begging aid;
translations.idiomatic: The lords and ministers by the Feng offered the chart and begged for aid;

sentences.zh: 關河百姓，泣血請師。

translations.literal: Guan and Yellow River's common people, wept blood begging troops.
translations.idiomatic: the people of the passes and rivers wept blood and begged for armies.

sentences.zh: 咸願承奉國靈，思睹王化。

translations.literal: All wished to receive the nation's numen, longing to behold royal transformation.
translations.idiomatic: All wished to receive the nation's numen and behold royal transformation.

sentences.zh: 朕以寡昧，纂戎下武，庶拯堯黎，冀康禹跡。

translations.literal: I, though dull and obscure, inherited the military mantle of Wu the Martial, hoping to rescue Yao's multitudes, hoping to restore Yu's traces.
translations.idiomatic: I, though dull and obscure, inherited the martial mantle of King Wu, hoping to rescue Yao's people and restore Yu's traces.

sentences.zh: 且夫車服以庸，名因事著。

translations.literal: Moreover, carriage and raiment reward merit; name follows achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, carriage and raiment reward merit, and name follows the deed.

sentences.zh: 周師克殷，鷹揚創自尚父；

translations.literal: When Zhou's army conquered Yin, the hawk-flourish began with Lord Shang;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou's army conquered Yin, the hawk-flourish began with Lord Shang;

sentences.zh: 漢征戎狄，明友實始度遼。

translations.literal: When Han campaigned against the Rong and Di, Ming You was the first to cross the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: When Han fought the northern tribes, Ming You was first to cross the Liao.

sentences.zh: 況乃神規叡算，眇乎難測，大功懋績，事絕言象，安可以習彼常名，保茲守固。

translations.literal: Moreover his divine strategy and keen calculations are beyond measure; his great deeds and splendid achievements exceed words and images—how could one hold to ordinary titles and keep to this narrow rank?
translations.idiomatic: His divine strategy and keen wit are beyond gauging; merit so great it outruns language—how could ordinary titles suffice for such a man?

sentences.zh: 相國可加宇宙大將軍、都督六合諸軍事，餘悉如故。

translations.literal: The Chancellor may be advanced to Grand General of the Universe and Director-in-Chief of all armies under Heaven; all else shall remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor shall be made Grand General of the Universe and supreme commander of all armies under Heaven; all else stays as before.

sentences.zh: 」以詔文呈太宗，太宗驚曰：「將軍乃有宇宙之號乎！」

translations.literal: " The edict text was presented to Taizong; Taizong said in shock, "The General truly bears the title of Universe!"
translations.idiomatic: " The edict was shown to Taizong, who cried in alarm, "The General has taken the title Universe!"

sentences.zh: 齊遣其將辛術圍陽平，景行臺郭元建率兵赴援，術退。

translations.literal: Qi sent its general Xin Shu to besiege Yangping; Jing's Mobile Headquarters Guo Yuanjian led troops to the relief, and Shu withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent general Xin Shu to besiege Yangping; Jing's mobile headquarters Guo Yuanjian marched to relieve it, and Shu withdrew.

sentences.zh: 徐文盛入資磯，任約率水軍逆戰，文盛大破之，仍進軍大舉口。

translations.literal: Xu Wensheng entered Ziji; Ren Yue led the river fleet to meet him in battle. Wensheng inflicted a great defeat and pressed on to Dajukou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wensheng took Ziji; Ren Yue led the river fleet against him. Wensheng routed him and advanced to Dajukou.

sentences.zh: 時景屯於皖口，京師虛弱，南康王會理及北兗州司馬成欽等將襲之。

translations.literal: At the time Jing was encamped at Wankou and the capital was weak; Prince Kuili of Nankang and North Yanzhou aide Cheng Qin and others were about to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was encamped at Wankou while the capital lay weakened; Prince Kuili of Nankang and North Yanzhou aide Cheng Qin plotted to strike him.

sentences.zh: 建安侯賁知其謀，以告景，景遣收會理與其弟祈陽侯通理、柳敬禮、成欽等，並害之。

translations.literal: Marquis Ben of Jian'an learned of the plot and told Jing. Jing sent men to seize Kuili, his brother Marquis Tongli of Qiyang, Liu Jingli, Cheng Qin, and others—and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Ben of Jian'an discovered the plot and warned Jing. Jing had Kuili, his brother Marquis Tongli of Qiyang, Liu Jingli, and Cheng Qin seized and killed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，景矯詔封賁爲竟陵王，賞發南康之謀也。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Jing forged an edict enfeoffing Ben as Prince of Jingling commandery, rewarding him for exposing the Nankang plot.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Jing forged an edict making Ben Prince of Jingling, a reward for revealing the Nankang conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 是月，張彪起義於會稽，攻破上虞，景太守蔡臺樂討之，不能禁。

translations.literal: That month Zhang Biao raised a righteous army in Kuaiji and stormed Shangyu; Jing's administrator Cai Taile tried to suppress him and could not.
translations.idiomatic: That month Zhang Biao rebelled in Kuaiji and took Shangyu; Jing's administrator Cai Taile could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 至是，彪又破諸暨、永興等諸縣，景遣儀同田遷、趙伯超、謝答仁等東伐彪。

translations.literal: By then Biao had also taken Zhuji, Yongxing, and other counties. Jing sent Yitong Tian Qian, Zhao Bochao, Xie Daren, and others east against Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had also overrun Zhuji, Yongxing, and other counties. Jing sent Yitong Tian Qian, Zhao Bochao, Xie Daren, and others east to crush him.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，彪遣別將寇錢塘、富春，田遷進軍與戰，破之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year Biao sent a detached general to raid Qiantang and Fuchun; Tian Qian advanced and routed him in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year two Biao sent a detachment against Qiantang and Fuchun; Tian Qian advanced and broke them.

sentences.zh: 景以王克爲太師，宋子仙爲太保，元羅爲太傅，郭元建爲太尉，張化仁爲司徒，任約爲司空，于慶爲太子太師，時靈護爲太子太保，紇奚斤爲太子太傅，王偉爲尚書左僕射，索超世爲尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Jing made Wang Ke Grand Preceptor, Song Zixian Grand Guardian, Yuan Luo Grand Tutor, Guo Yuanjian Grand Commandant, Zhang Huaren Minister of Education, Ren Yue Minister of Works, Yu Qing Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince, Shi Linghu Grand Guardian to the Crown Prince, Hexi Jin Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, Wang Wei Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Suo Chaoshi Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Jing made Wang Ke Grand Preceptor, Song Zixian Grand Guardian, Yuan Luo Grand Tutor, Guo Yuanjian Grand Commandant, Zhang Huaren Minister of Education, Ren Yue Minister of Works, Yu Qing Grand Preceptor to the Crown Prince, Shi Linghu Grand Guardian to the Crown Prince, Hexi Jin Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, Wang Wei Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Suo Chaoshi Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 北兗州刺史蕭邕謀降魏，事泄，景誅之。

translations.literal: Inspector of North Yanzhou Xiao Yong plotted surrender to Wei; the plot leaked and Jing executed him.
translations.idiomatic: North Yanzhou inspector Xiao Yong plotted to surrender to Wei; when the plot leaked, Jing had him killed.

sentences.zh: 是月，世祖遣巴州刺史王珣等率衆下武昌助徐文盛。

translations.literal: That month Shizu sent Wang Xun of Bazhou and others with troops down to Wuchang to aid Xu Wensheng.
translations.idiomatic: That month Shizu sent Bazhou's Wang Xun and others with troops to Wuchang to aid Xu Wensheng.

sentences.zh: 任約以西臺益兵，告急於景。

translations.literal: Ren Yue urgently asked Jing for reinforcements from the Western Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yue sent urgent word to Jing asking the Western Headquarters for more troops.

sentences.zh: 三月，景自率衆二萬，西上援約。

translations.literal: In the third month Jing personally led twenty thousand men west to relieve Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Jing led twenty thousand men west himself to rescue Yue.

sentences.zh: 四月，景次西陽，徐文盛率水軍邀戰，大破之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Jing halted at Xiyang; Xu Wensheng led the river fleet to intercept him and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Jing camped at Xiyang; Xu Wensheng intercepted him on the water and routed his fleet.

sentences.zh: 景訪知郢州無備，兵少，又遣宋子仙率輕騎三百襲陷之，執刺史方諸、行事鮑泉，盡獲武昌軍人家口。

translations.literal: Learning that Ying province was undefended and lightly garrisoned, Jing sent Song Zixian with three hundred light cavalry to raid and take it, seizing Inspector Fang Zhu and acting administrator Bao Quan and capturing the families of the entire Wuchang army.
translations.idiomatic: Jing learned Yingzhou was undefended and sent Song Zixian with three hundred light horse to take it by surprise, seizing inspector Fang Zhu and acting administrator Bao Quan and all the families of the Wuchang army.

sentences.zh: 徐文盛等聞之，大潰，奔歸江陵，景乘勝西上。

translations.literal: When Xu Wensheng and the others heard of it they broke in rout and fled to Jiangling; Jing pressed west on the victory.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wensheng's troops heard and broke in panic, fleeing to Jiangling; Jing pressed west on momentum.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖遣領軍王僧辯率衆東下代徐文盛，軍次巴陵，會景至，僧辯因堅壁拒之。

translations.literal: Earlier Shizu had sent Army Commander Wang Sengbian east with troops to replace Xu Wensheng. The army halted at Baling; when Jing arrived, Sengbian fortified the walls and held him off.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu had already sent army commander Wang Sengbian east to replace Xu Wensheng. Sengbian halted at Baling; when Jing arrived he fortified and refused battle.

sentences.zh: 景設長圍，築土山，晝夜攻擊，不克。

translations.literal: Jing set a long siege, built earthen mounds, and attacked day and night without success.
translations.idiomatic: Jing laid a long siege, piled earthworks, and assaulted day and night without breaching the walls.

sentences.zh: 軍中疾疫，死傷太半。

translations.literal: Plague broke out in the army; more than half died or were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Plague swept the army; more than half were dead or wounded.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣平北將軍胡僧祐率兵二千人救巴陵，景聞，遣任約以精卒數千逆擊僧祐，僧祐與居士陸法和退據赤亭以待之，約至與戰，大破之，生擒約。

translations.literal: Shizu sent Pacification North General Hu Sengyou with two thousand troops to relieve Baling. When Jing heard, he sent Ren Yue with several thousand elite troops to intercept Sengyou. Sengyou and the layman Lu Fahe withdrew to Chiting to await him; when Yue arrived and gave battle, they inflicted a great defeat and took Yue alive.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu sent Pacification North General Hu Sengyou with two thousand men to relieve Baling. Jing sent Ren Yue with thousands of elite troops to cut him off. Sengyou and the layman Lu Fahe fell back to Chiting to wait; when Yue arrived they routed him and captured him alive.

sentences.zh: 景聞之，夜遁。

translations.literal: When Jing heard of it he fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Jing heard and fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 以丁和爲郢州刺史，留宋子仙、時靈護等助和守，以張化仁、閻洪慶守魯山城，景還京師。

translations.literal: He made Ding He Inspector of Ying province, left Song Zixian, Shi Linghu, and others to aid He in the defense, put Zhang Huaren and Yan Hongqing in charge of Lushan city, and Jing returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Ding He inspector of Yingzhou, left Song Zixian and Shi Linghu to help him hold the city, garrisoned Zhang Huaren and Yan Hongqing at Lushan, and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯乃率衆東下，次漢口，攻魯山及郢城，皆陷之。

translations.literal: Wang Sengbian then led troops east, halted at Hankou, and attacked Lushan and Ying city—both fell.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengbian marched east to Hankou and took Lushan and Ying city.

sentences.zh: 自是衆軍所至皆捷。

translations.literal: From then on the armies met victory wherever they went.
translations.idiomatic: After that the loyal armies won wherever they marched.

sentences.zh: 景乃廢太宗，幽於永福省。

translations.literal: Jing then deposed Taizong and imprisoned him in Yongfu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Jing deposed Taizong and confined him in Yongfu Province.

sentences.zh: 作詔草成，逼太宗寫之，至「先皇念神器之重，思社稷之固」，歔欷嗚咽，不能自止。

translations.literal: The draft edict was prepared and Taizong was forced to copy it; when he came to "The late emperor thought on the weight of the imperial regalia and the firmness of the altars of state," he sobbed and wept and could not stop.
translations.idiomatic: The abdication edict was drafted and Taizong was forced to write it out; at "The late emperor pondered the weight of the throne and the realm's security" he wept until he could not continue.

sentences.zh: 是日，景迎豫章王棟卽皇帝位，升太極前殿，大赦天下，改元爲天正元年。

translations.literal: That day Jing brought Prince Dong of Yuzhang to the throne, ascended the Hall before Taiji, declared a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Tianzheng, year one.
translations.idiomatic: That day Jing set Prince Dong of Yuzhang on the throne, ascended the Hall before Taiji, declared amnesty, and renamed the era Tianzheng.

sentences.zh: 有回風自永福省吹其文物，皆倒折，見者莫不驚駭。

translations.literal: A whirlwind blew from Yongfu Province and knocked down the ritual vessels; all who saw it were struck with terror.
translations.idiomatic: A gust from Yongfu Province blew over the ritual vessels; every witness was horrified.

sentences.zh: 初，景旣平京邑，便有篡奪之志，以四方須定，且未自立；

translations.literal: At first, once Jing had pacified the capital, he already harbored intent to usurp; because the four directions had yet to be settled, he had not yet set himself up.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment Jing took the capital he meant to seize the throne—but the realm was still unsettled, so he held back.

sentences.zh: 旣巴陵失律，江、郢喪師，猛將外殲，雄心內沮，便欲偽僭大號，遂其姦心。

translations.literal: Once Baling was lost, Jiang and Ying lost their armies, fierce generals were destroyed without, and his bold heart was discouraged within—then he wished to usurp the great title and satisfy his treacherous heart.
translations.idiomatic: After Baling fell, Jiang and Ying lost their armies, his best generals were gone, and his ambition turned inward—he meant to take the throne himself and satisfy his treachery.

sentences.zh: 其謀臣王偉云「自古移鼎，必須廢立」，故景從之。

translations.literal: His counsellor Wang Wei said, "Since ancient times to shift the tripod one must depose and install"; so Jing followed him.
translations.idiomatic: His adviser Wang Wei said, "Since antiquity, whoever moved the sacred vessel had first to depose one ruler and install another"—and Jing did as he said.

sentences.zh: 其太尉郭元建聞之，自秦郡馳還，諫景曰：「四方之師所以不至者，政爲二宮萬福；

translations.literal: His Grand Commandant Guo Yuanjian heard of it and galloped back from Qin commandery, remonstrating with Jing: "The reason armies from the four directions have not come is precisely because both palaces remain unharmed;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Guo Yuanjian heard and rode back from Qin in haste, pleading with Jing: "The armies of the realm hold back only because both palaces still stand;

sentences.zh: 若遂行弑逆，結怨海內，事幾一去，雖悔無及。

translations.literal: if you now commit regicide and raise hatred throughout the realm, once the chance is gone regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: if you murder the emperor and turn the whole realm against you, the moment will pass—and no repentance will save you.

sentences.zh: 」王偉固執不從。

translations.literal: " Wang Wei stubbornly would not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Wei refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 景乃矯棟詔，追尊昭明太子爲昭明皇帝，豫章安王爲安皇帝，金華敬妃爲敬皇后，豫章國太妃王氏爲皇太后，妃張氏爲皇后；

translations.literal: Jing then forged an edict in Dong's name, posthumously honoring Crown Prince Zhaoming as Emperor Zhaoming, Prince An of Yuzhang as Emperor An, Consort Jing of Jinhua as Empress Jing, the Grand Consort of Yuzhang state Lady Wang as Empress Dowager, and Consort Zhang as Empress;
translations.idiomatic: Jing forged an edict in Dong's name posthumously elevating Crown Prince Zhaoming to Emperor Zhaoming, Prince An of Yuzhang to Emperor An, Consort Jing of Jinhua to Empress Jing, Yuzhang Grand Consort Lady Wang to Empress Dowager, and Consort Zhang to Empress;

sentences.zh: 以劉神茂爲司空，徐洪爲平南將軍，秦晃之、王曄、李賢明、徐永、徐珍國、宋長寶、尹思合併爲儀同三司。

translations.literal: and made Liu Shenmao Minister of Works, Xu Hong Pacification South General, Qin Huangzhi, Wang Ye, Li Xianming, Xu Yong, Xu Zhenguo, Song Changbao, and Yin Sihe Yitong commissioners with equal prestige to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: he made Liu Shenmao Minister of Works, Xu Hong Pacification South General, and Qin Huangzhi, Wang Ye, Li Xianming, Xu Yong, Xu Zhenguo, Song Changbao, and Yin Sihe all commissioners equal in prestige to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 景以哀太子妃賜郭元建，元建曰：「豈有皇太子妃而降爲人妾？

translations.literal: Jing gave the late crown prince's consort to Guo Yuanjian; Yuanjian said, "How can a crown prince's consort be reduced to another man's concubine?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing gave the late crown prince's wife to Guo Yuanjian; Yuanjian said, "What crown prince's wife becomes another man's concubine?"

sentences.zh: 」竟不與相見。

translations.literal: He ultimately refused even to see her.
translations.idiomatic: He would not even meet her.

sentences.zh: 十月壬寅夜，景遣其衛尉彭儁、王脩纂奉酒於太宗曰：「丞相以陛下處憂旣久，故令臣等奉進一觴。

translations.literal: On the night of renyin in the tenth month, Jing sent his Commandant of the Guard Peng Jun and Wang Xiuzuan to bring wine to Taizong, saying, "The Chancellor, seeing Your Majesty long in distress, has sent us to offer this cup."
translations.idiomatic: On the night of renyin in the tenth month Jing sent Guard Commandant Peng Jun and Wang Xiuzuan with wine for Taizong, saying, "The Chancellor sees you have suffered long and bids us offer this cup."

sentences.zh: 」太宗知其將弑，乃大酣飲酒，旣醉還寢，脩纂以帊盛土加於腹，因崩焉。

translations.literal: " Taizong knew they meant to kill him, drank heavily until drunk, and returned to sleep; Xiuzuan piled earth in a cloth on his belly, and so he died.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong knew murder was coming, drank himself senseless, and went to bed; Xiuzuan smothered him with a cloth sack of earth.

sentences.zh: 斂用法服，以薄棺密瘞於城北酒庫。

translations.literal: He was buried in court robes in a thin coffin, secretly interred at the wine storehouse north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: They clad him in court dress, placed him in a thin coffin, and secretly buried him at the northern wine storehouse.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗久見幽縶，朝士莫得接覲，慮禍將及，常不自安；

translations.literal: At first Taizong had long been confined; court officials could not visit him, and fearing disaster drew ever closer he was constantly uneasy;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had been confined so long that no courtier could see him; dreading what was coming, he lived in constant fear;

sentences.zh: 惟舍人殷不害後稍得入，太宗指所居殿謂之曰：「龐涓當死此下。

translations.literal: only Attendant Yin Buhai was later allowed entry. Taizong pointed at the hall where he dwelt and said to him, "It is here beneath this hall that Pang Juan ought to die."
translations.idiomatic: only attendant Yin Buhai was later admitted. Taizong pointed at his hall and said, "It is here that Pang Juan should die."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「吾昨夜夢吞土，卿試爲思之。

translations.literal: He also said, "Last night I dreamed I swallowed earth—try to interpret it."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "I dreamed I ate earth last night—what do you make of it?"

sentences.zh: 」不害曰：「昔重耳饋塊，卒反晉國。

translations.literal: Buhai said, "In the past Chong'er was given a clod of earth and in the end returned to rule Jin."
translations.idiomatic: Buhai said, "When Chong'er was given a clod of earth he returned to rule Jin."

sentences.zh: 陛下所夢，將符是乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's dream—will it match that?"
translations.idiomatic: Could your dream mean the same?"

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「儻幽冥有徵，冀斯言不妄耳。

translations.literal: Taizong said, "If the underworld gives a sign, I hope these words are not vain."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "If the dead send a sign, I hope this is true."

sentences.zh: 」至是見弑，實以土焉。

translations.literal: When he was murdered at last, it was indeed with earth.
translations.idiomatic: When he was killed, earth was indeed the means.

sentences.zh: 是月，景司空東道行臺劉神茂、儀同尹思合、劉歸義、王曄、雲麾將軍桑乾王元頵等據東陽歸順，仍遣元頵及別將李占、趙惠朗下據建德江口。

translations.literal: That month Jing's Minister of Works and Eastern Route Mobile Headquarters Liu Shenmao, Yitong Yin Sihe, Liu Guiyi, Wang Ye, Cloud Banner General Prince Yun of Sanggan, and others held Dongyang and surrendered; they still sent Yun and detached generals Li Zhan and Zhao Huilang south to hold Jiande River mouth.
translations.idiomatic: That month Liu Shenmao of Jing's eastern mobile headquarters, Yin Sihe, Liu Guiyi, Wang Ye, and Cloud Banner General Prince Yun of Sanggan held Dongyang and defected; Yun and detachments under Li Zhan and Zhao Huilang seized Jiande River mouth.

sentences.zh: 尹思合收景新安太守元義，奪其兵。

translations.literal: Yin Sihe seized Jing's Administrator of Xin'an Yuan Yi and stripped him of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Sihe seized Jing's Xin'an administrator Yuan Yi and took his army.

sentences.zh: 張彪攻永嘉，永嘉太守秦遠降彪。

translations.literal: Zhang Biao attacked Yongjia; Administrator Qin Yuan surrendered to Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Biao attacked Yongjia; administrator Qin Yuan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十一月，景以趙伯超爲東道行臺，鎮錢塘，遣儀同田遷、謝答仁等將兵東征神茂。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Jing made Zhao Bochao Eastern Route Mobile Headquarters, garrisoning Qiantang, and sent Yitong Tian Qian, Xie Daren, and others east with troops against Shenmao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Jing put Zhao Bochao in charge of the eastern mobile headquarters at Qiantang and sent Tian Qian, Xie Daren, and others east against Shenmao.

sentences.zh: 景矯蕭棟詔，自加九錫之禮，置丞相以下百官。

translations.literal: Jing forged an edict in Xiao Dong's name, granting himself the Nine Bestowments and appointing all offices from Chancellor downward.
translations.idiomatic: Jing forged an edict in Xiao Dong's name, giving himself the Nine Bestowments and filling every office down to Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 陳備物於庭，忽有野鳥翔于景上，赤足丹觜，形似山鵲，賊徒悉駭，競射之不能中。

translations.literal: The ritual objects were arrayed in the courtyard when suddenly a wild bird flew above Jing—red-footed, red-beaked, shaped like a mountain magpie—and the rebels were all terrified; they shot at it but could not hit it.
translations.idiomatic: As the ritual gear was set in the courtyard a wild bird flew over Jing—red feet, red beak, like a mountain magpie—and the rebels panicked, shooting wildly without a hit.

sentences.zh: 景以劉勸、戚霸、硃安王爲開府儀同三司，索九升爲護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Jing made Liu Quan, Qi Ba, and Zhu Anwang Yitong commissioners with equal prestige to the Three Dukes, and Suo Jiusheng Protector General.
translations.idiomatic: Jing made Liu Quan, Qi Ba, and Zhu Anwang commissioners equal to the Three Dukes, and Suo Jiusheng Protector General.

sentences.zh: 南兗州刺史侯子鑒獻白麞，建康獲白鼠以獻，蕭棟歸之于景。

translations.literal: Inspector of South Yanzhou Hou Zijian presented a white roe deer; a white rat was caught in Jiankang and presented—the items were returned to Jing through Xiao Dong.
translations.idiomatic: South Yanzhou inspector Hou Zijian offered a white roe deer; Jiankang caught a white rat as tribute—Xiao Dong passed both to Jing.

sentences.zh: 景以郭元建爲南兗州刺史，太尉、北行臺如故。

translations.literal: Jing made Guo Yuanjian Inspector of South Yanzhou, keeping his posts as Grand Commandant and Northern Route Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Jing made Guo Yuanjian inspector of South Yanzhou while keeping him Grand Commandant and northern mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 景又矯蕭棟詔，追崇其祖爲大將軍，考爲丞相。

translations.literal: Jing again forged an edict in Xiao Dong's name, posthumously honoring his grandfather as Grand General and his father as Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Jing forged another edict in Dong's name, posthumously making his grandfather Grand General and his father Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 自加冕，十有二旒，建天子旌旗，出警入蹕，乘金根車，駕六馬，備五時副車，置旄頭雲罕，樂儛八佾，鐘虡宮懸之樂，一如舊儀。

translations.literal: He added an imperial crown with twelve tassels, raised the imperial banners, went out and in with imperial escort, rode the golden-root chariot drawn by six horses with seasonal outriders, set yak-tail banners and the cloud canopy, arranged eight rows of dancers, and had the bell and stone palace music—all as in the old rites.
translations.idiomatic: He took a twelve-tassel crown, imperial banners, royal escort, the golden chariot with six horses and seasonal outriders, yak-tail standards and cloud canopy, eight rows of dancers, and full court music—everything by the old imperial rite.

sentences.zh: 景又矯蕭棟詔，禪位於己。

translations.literal: Jing again forged an edict in Xiao Dong's name, abdicating the throne to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing forged yet another edict in Dong's name, handing him the throne.

sentences.zh: 於是南郊，柴燎于天，升壇受禪文物，並依舊儀。

translations.literal: Thereupon at the Southern Suburban Altar he burned offerings to Heaven, ascended the altar, and received the abdication regalia—all by the old rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the southern altar he burned offerings to Heaven, mounted the ritual platform, and took the regalia of abdication by the old forms.

sentences.zh: 以轜車床載鼓吹，橐駝負犧牲，輦上置筌蹄、垂腳坐。

translations.literal: Drums and pipes rode on wagon beds; camels bore the sacrificial victims; the imperial carriage held footstools and dangling-leg seats.
translations.idiomatic: Wagon beds carried drums and pipes; camels bore the sacrifice; the carriage held foot-rests and dangling-leg seats.

sentences.zh: 景所帶劍水精標無故墮落，手自拾之。

translations.literal: The crystal finial on the sword Jing wore fell off for no reason; he picked it up himself.
translations.idiomatic: The crystal pommel on Jing's sword fell off without cause; he bent and picked it up himself.

sentences.zh: 將登壇，有兔自前而走，俄失所在；

translations.literal: Just before mounting the altar a rabbit ran out in front and vanished;
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to mount the altar a rabbit darted before him and vanished;

sentences.zh: 又白虹貫日。

translations.literal: a white rainbow also pierced the sun.
translations.idiomatic: a white rainbow cut across the sun.

sentences.zh: 景還升太極前殿，大赦，改元爲太始元年。

translations.literal: Jing then ascended the Hall before Taiji, declared a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Taishi, year one.
translations.idiomatic: Jing mounted the Hall before Taiji, declared amnesty, and renamed the era Taishi.

sentences.zh: 封蕭棟爲淮陰王，幽于監省。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Xiao Dong as Prince of Huaiyin and confined him in the prison province.
translations.idiomatic: He made Xiao Dong Prince of Huaiyin and locked him in the oversight compound.

sentences.zh: 偽有司奏改「警蹕」爲「永蹕」，避景名也。

translations.literal: The false authorities memorialized changing "imperial escort" to "eternal escort," avoiding Jing's name.
translations.idiomatic: The puppet court asked to rename the imperial escort "eternal escort" to avoid Jing's name.

sentences.zh: 改梁律爲漢律，改左民尚書爲殿中尚書，五兵尚書爲七兵尚書，直殿主帥爲直寢。

translations.literal: The Liang code was changed to the Han code; Left Director of the People was changed to Director of the Palace; Director of Five Arms was changed to Director of Seven Arms; Chief of Direct Palace Service was changed to Chief of Direct Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Liang law became Han law; Left Director of the People became Director of the Palace; Five Arms became Seven Arms; Direct Palace chiefs became Direct Quarters chiefs.

sentences.zh: 景三公之官動置十數，儀同尤多，或匹馬孤行，自執羈絆。

translations.literal: Jing appointed ten or more men to each of the Three Excellencies; Yitong posts were especially numerous—some rode a lone horse and held their own reins.
translations.idiomatic: Jing stuffed each of the Three Excellencies with a dozen appointees; Yitong posts proliferated—some men rode alone, reins in hand.

sentences.zh: 其左僕射王偉請立七廟，景曰：「何謂爲七廟？

translations.literal: His Left Vice Director Wang Wei asked to establish seven ancestral temples. Jing said, "What do you mean by seven temples?"
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Wang Wei asked to build seven ancestral temples. Jing said, "What are seven temples?"

sentences.zh: 」偉曰：「天子祭七世祖考，故置七廟。

translations.literal: Wei said, "A Son of Heaven sacrifices to seven generations of ancestors and forebears—that is why seven temples are set up."
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "A Son of Heaven sacrifices to seven generations—that is why one builds seven temples."

sentences.zh: 」幷請七世之諱，敕太常具祭祀之禮。

translations.literal: He also asked for the taboo names of seven generations and ordered the Director of Ceremonials to prepare the sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested seven generations of taboo names and ordered the Director of Ceremonials to prepare the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 景曰：「前世吾不復憶，惟阿爺名標。

translations.literal: Jing said, "Earlier generations I no longer remember—only Grandfather's name was Biao."
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "I remember no earlier generations—only that Grandpa was called Biao."

sentences.zh: 」衆聞咸竊笑之。

translations.literal: All who heard this laughed in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who heard laughed behind their hands.

sentences.zh: 景黨有知景祖名周者，自外悉是王偉制其名位，以漢司徒侯霸爲始祖，晉徵士侯瑾爲七世祖。

translations.literal: Among Jing's faction only one man knew that Jing's grandfather was named Zhou; all the rest were names and ranks Wang Wei invented, making Han Minister of Education Hou Ba the founding ancestor and Jin Recluse Hou Jin the seventh-generation forebear.
translations.idiomatic: Only one man in Jing's camp knew his grandfather was Zhou; every other name and title was Wang Wei's invention—Han Minister Hou Ba as founding ancestor, Jin recluse Hou Jin as seventh-generation forebear.

sentences.zh: 於是追尊其祖周爲大丞相，父標爲元皇帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he posthumously honored his grandfather Zhou as Grand Chancellor and his father Biao as Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: So he posthumously made Zhou Grand Chancellor and Biao Founding Emperor.

sentences.zh: 十二月，謝答仁、李慶等至建德，攻元頵、李占柵，大破之，執頵、占送景。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Xie Daren and Li Qing reached Jiande and attacked the palisades of Yun and Li Zhan, inflicting a great defeat; they seized Yun and Zhan and sent them to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Xie Daren and Li Qing reached Jiande, stormed the palisades of Yun and Li Zhan, captured them, and sent them to Jing.

sentences.zh: 景截其手足徇之，經日乃死。

translations.literal: Jing cut off their hands and feet and displayed them as a warning; after a full day they died.
translations.idiomatic: Jing cut off their limbs and displayed them as a warning; they died after a day.

sentences.zh: 景二年正月朔，臨軒朝會。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day in the second year of Jing's reign he held court at the imperial facade.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of Jing's second year he held imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 景自巴丘挫衂，軍兵略盡，恐齊人乘釁與西師掎角，乃遣郭元建率步軍趣小峴，侯子鑒率舟師向濡須，曜兵肥水，以示武威。

translations.literal: Since his defeat at Baling his army was nearly gone; fearing Qi would seize the chance and join the western armies in a pincer, he sent Guo Yuanjian with foot soldiers toward Xiaoxian and Hou Zijian with the river fleet toward Ruru, displaying troops at the Fei River to show martial might.
translations.idiomatic: Broken at Baling, his army nearly spent, he feared Qi would exploit the moment and link arms with the western host—so he sent Guo Yuanjian's infantry toward Xiaoxian and Hou Zijian's fleet toward Ruru, parading troops on the Fei to show strength.

sentences.zh: 子鑒至合肥，攻羅城，剋之。

translations.literal: Zijian reached Hefei and stormed the outer wall; he took it.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian reached Hefei, stormed the outer wall, and took it.

sentences.zh: 郭元建、侯子鑒俄聞王師旣近，燒合肥百姓邑居，引軍退，子鑒保姑孰，元建還廣陵。

translations.literal: Guo Yuanjian and Hou Zijian soon heard the royal armies were near; they burned the homes of the people of Hefei, withdrew their troops, Zijian holding Gudu, Yuanjian returning to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuanjian and Hou Zijian soon heard the loyal armies were closing in; they burned Hefei's settlements and retreated—Zijian to Gudu, Yuanjian to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 時謝答仁攻劉神茂，神茂別將王華、麗通並據外營降答仁。

translations.literal: At the time Xie Daren was attacking Liu Shenmao; Shenmao's detached generals Wang Hua and Li Tong both held outer camps and surrendered to Daren.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Daren was pressing Liu Shenmao; Shenmao's generals Wang Hua and Li Tong held the outer camps and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 劉歸義、尹思合等懼，各棄城走。

translations.literal: Liu Guiyi, Yin Sihe, and the others grew afraid and each abandoned his city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guiyi, Yin Sihe, and the rest fled their posts in fear.

sentences.zh: 神茂孤危，復降答仁。

translations.literal: Shenmao, isolated and endangered, surrendered to Daren again.
translations.idiomatic: Shenmao, isolated and desperate, surrendered to Daren.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯軍至蕪湖，蕪湖城主宵遁。

translations.literal: Wang Sengbian's army reached Wuhu; the Wuhu garrison commander fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengbian reached Wuhu; its commander fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 景遣史安和、宋長貴等率兵二千，助子鑒守姑孰，追田遷等還京師。

translations.literal: Jing sent Shi Anhe and Song Changgui with two thousand troops to help Zijian hold Gudu, and recalled Tian Qian and the others to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent Shi Anhe and Song Changgui with two thousand men to help Zijian hold Gudu and recalled Tian Qian and others to the capital.

sentences.zh: 是月，景黨郭長獻馬駒生角。

translations.literal: That month one of Jing's followers, Guo Chang, presented a colt born with horns.
translations.idiomatic: That month Jing's man Guo Chang offered a foal born with horns.

sentences.zh: 三月，景往姑孰，巡視壘柵，又誡子鑒曰：「西人善水戰，不可與爭鋒，往年任約敗績，良爲此也。

translations.literal: In the third month Jing went to Gudu to inspect the palisades and again admonished Zijian: "Westerners excel at river fighting—do not meet them on the water. Ren Yue's defeat in years past was precisely because of this.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Jing went to Gudu, inspected the defenses, and warned Zijian: "Westerners fight best on water—never meet them there. Ren Yue lost for exactly that reason.

sentences.zh: 若得馬步一交，必當可破，汝但堅壁以觀其變。

translations.literal: If you can clash once on horse and foot you are sure to break them—only hold the walls and watch for their lapse."
translations.idiomatic: One clash on land and you will break them—just hold your walls and wait."

sentences.zh: 」子鑒乃舍舟登岸，閉營不出。

translations.literal: " Zijian then abandoned his boats, came ashore, and closed camp without emerging.
translations.idiomatic: " Zijian left his boats, went ashore, shut camp, and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 僧辯等遂停軍十餘日，賊黨大喜，告景曰：「西師懼吾之強，必欲遁逸，不擊，將失之。

translations.literal: Sengbian and the others thereupon halted their army for more than ten days; the rebel faction rejoiced greatly and told Jing, "The western armies fear our strength—they mean to flee; if we do not strike we shall lose them."
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian halted for ten-odd days; the rebels rejoiced and told Jing, "The western host fears us and means to run—strike now or they escape."

sentences.zh: 」景復命子鑒爲水戰之備。

translations.literal: Jing again ordered Zijian to prepare for river battle.
translations.idiomatic: Jing ordered Zijian to ready the fleet again.

sentences.zh: 子鑒乃率步騎萬餘人渡洲，幷引水軍俱進，僧辯逆擊，大破之，子鑒僅以身免。

translations.literal: Zijian then led more than ten thousand horse and foot across the sandbar and advanced with the river fleet together; Sengbian met him in counterattack and inflicted a great defeat—Zijian barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian led ten thousand horse and foot across the ford, fleet and army together; Sengbian counterattacked and shattered him—Zijian escaped by a hair.

sentences.zh: 景聞子鑒敗，大懼涕下，覆面引衾以臥，良久方起，歎曰：「誤殺乃公！」

translations.literal: When Jing heard that Zijian was defeated he was greatly afraid and wept; he covered his face, pulled up the bedding, and lay down. After a long while he rose and sighed, "I have killed my old man!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jing heard Zijian was broken he wept in terror, hid his face under the covers, and lay a long while before rising with a sigh: "I killed my father-in-law!"

sentences.zh: 僧辯進軍次張公洲。

translations.literal: Sengbian advanced his army and encamped at Zhang Gong Isle.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian marched his army to Zhang Gong Isle.

sentences.zh: 景以盧暉略守石頭，紇奚斤守捍國城，悉逼百姓及軍士家累入臺城內。

translations.literal: Jing had Lu Huilue hold Stone Fort and Hexijin hold Defend-the-State city, and drove all commoners and soldiers' families into Terrace City.
translations.idiomatic: Jing put Lu Huilue in Stone Fort and Hexijin in Defend-the-State city, and forced every civilian and soldier's kin into Terrace City.

sentences.zh: 僧辯焚景水柵，入淮，至祥靈寺渚。

translations.literal: Sengbian burned Jing's river palisades, entered the Huai, and reached Xiangling Temple shoal.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian burned Jing's river barriers, crossed into the Huai, and reached Xiangling Temple shoal.

sentences.zh: 景大驚，乃緣淮立柵，自石頭至朱雀航。

translations.literal: Jing was greatly alarmed and built palisades along the Huai from Stone Fort to Vermilion Bird Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was terrified and ran palisades along the Huai from Stone Fort to Vermilion Bird Ford.

sentences.zh: 僧辯及諸將遂於石頭城西步上連營立柵，至於落星墩。

translations.literal: Sengbian and the other generals then on foot west of Stone Fort city linked camps and raised palisades as far as Falling Star Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian and his generals then linked camps on foot west of Stone Fort and raised palisades to Falling Star Mound.

sentences.zh: 景大恐，自率侯子鑒、于慶、史安和、王僧貴等，於石頭東北立柵拒守。

translations.literal: Jing was greatly afraid; he personally led Hou Zijian, Yu Qing, Shi Anhe, Wang Senggui, and others to build palisades northeast of Stone Fort and hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was badly shaken. He himself led Hou Zijian, Yu Qing, Shi Anhe, Wang Senggui, and others to raise palisades northeast of Stone Fort and stand firm.

sentences.zh: 使王偉、索超世、呂季略守臺城，宋長貴守延祚寺。

translations.literal: He sent Wang Wei, Suo Chaoshi, and Lü Jilue to hold Terrace City, and Song Changgui to hold Yanzuo Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Wei, Suo Chaoshi, and Lü Jilue to hold Terrace City and Song Changgui to hold Yanzuo Temple.

sentences.zh: 遣掘王僧辯父墓，剖棺焚屍。

translations.literal: He sent men to dig up Wang Sengbian's father's tomb, open the coffin, and burn the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: He had Wang Sengbian's father's tomb opened, the coffin broken, and the body burned.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯等進營於石頭城北，景列陣挑戰。

translations.literal: Wang Sengbian and the others advanced their camps north of Stone Fort city; Jing drew up battle lines and offered challenge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengbian and the others moved camp north of Stone Fort; Jing formed ranks and challenged them.

sentences.zh: 僧辯率衆軍奮擊，大破之，侯子鑒、史安和、王僧貴各棄柵走，盧暉略、紇奚斤並以城降。

translations.literal: Sengbian led the mass of troops in a fierce assault and routed them utterly. Hou Zijian, Shi Anhe, and Wang Senggui each abandoned their palisades and fled; Lu Huilue and Hexijin both surrendered their cities.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian led the whole army in a furious charge and broke them completely. Hou Zijian, Shi Anhe, and Wang Senggui fled their palisades; Lu Huilue and Hexijin surrendered both cities.

sentences.zh: 景旣退敗，不入宮，斂其散兵，屯于闕下，遂將逃竄。

translations.literal: Jing, already beaten in retreat, did not enter the palace; he gathered his scattered troops, encamped below the gate-towers, and was about to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Beaten back, Jing would not enter the palace. He gathered scattered troops below the gate-towers and prepared to run.

sentences.zh: 王偉攬轡諫曰：「自古豈有叛天子！

translations.literal: Wang Wei took the reins and remonstrated: "Since antiquity, has there ever been one who betrayed the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei seized the bridle and pleaded, "Since antiquity, who has ever betrayed the Son of Heaven!

sentences.zh: 今宮中衛士，尚足一戰，寧可便走，棄此欲何所之？

translations.literal: The palace guards alone are still enough for one battle—how can you flee at once? If you abandon this place, where can you go?
translations.idiomatic: The guards in the palace could still fight one battle. How can you flee now? If you leave this, where will you go?

sentences.zh: 」景曰：「我在北打賀拔勝，破葛榮，揚名河、朔，與高王一種人。

translations.literal: " Jing said: "In the north I fought He Ba Sheng, broke Ge Rong, and made my name on the Yellow River and north of the Great Wall—I am that sort of man, like Gao Wang.
translations.idiomatic: " Jing said, "In the north I fought He Ba Sheng, broke Ge Rong, and made my name on the Yellow River and beyond the frontier. I am a man of Gao Wang's kind.

sentences.zh: 今來南渡大江，取臺城如反掌，打邵陵王於北山，破柳仲禮於南岸，皆乃所親見。

translations.literal: Now coming south across the great river, I took Terrace City as easily as turning my hand; at North Hill I struck Prince Shao of Shaoling; on the south bank I broke Liu Zhongli—all with my own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Coming south across the great river I took Terrace City as easily as turning my hand. At North Hill I struck Prince Shao of Shaoling; on the south bank I broke Liu Zhongli. I saw it all myself.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，恐是天亡。

translations.literal: Today's affair, I fear, is Heaven's decree of ruin.
translations.idiomatic: What has happened today, I fear, is Heaven decreeing my end.

sentences.zh: 乃好守城，我當復一決耳。

translations.literal: So guard the city well—I shall make one more try."
translations.idiomatic: Hold the city well. I will make one more stand."

sentences.zh: 」仰觀石闕，逡巡歎息。

translations.literal: " He looked up at the stone gate-towers, hesitated, and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: He looked up at the stone gate-towers, hesitated, and sighed.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃以皮囊盛二子掛馬鞍，與其儀同田遷、范希榮等百餘騎東奔。

translations.literal: After a long while he put his two sons in leather sacks hung from the saddle and, with his Yitong Tian Qian, Fan Xirong, and more than a hundred horsemen, fled east.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he hung his two sons in leather sacks from his saddle and fled east with his Yitong Tian Qian, Fan Xirong, and more than a hundred riders.

sentences.zh: 王偉委臺城竄逸，侯子鑒等奔廣陵。

translations.literal: Wang Wei abandoned Terrace City and fled; Hou Zijian and the others fled to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei deserted Terrace City and fled; Hou Zijian and the others ran to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯遣侯瑱率軍追景。

translations.literal: Wang Sengbian sent Hou Tian to lead troops in pursuit of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengbian sent Hou Tian after Jing with an army.

sentences.zh: 景至晉陵，劫太守徐永東奔吳郡，進次嘉興，趙伯超據錢塘拒之。

translations.literal: Jing reached Jinling commandery, seized Prefect Xu Yong, and fled east to Wu commandery; advancing he halted at Jiaxing, where Zhao Bochao held Qiantang and resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing reached Jinling, seized Prefect Xu Yong, and fled east to Wu commandery. He halted at Jiaxing, where Zhao Bochao held Qiantang against him.

sentences.zh: 景退還吳郡，達松江，而侯瑱軍掩至，景衆未陣，皆舉幡乞降。

translations.literal: Jing fell back to Wu commandery and reached Song River, but Hou Tian's army came upon him by surprise; Jing's troops had not yet formed ranks and all raised banners begging to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jing retreated to Wu commandery and reached Song River, but Hou Tian's army fell on him before his men could form ranks. They all raised banners and begged to surrender.

sentences.zh: 景不能制，乃與腹心數十人單舸走，推墮二子于水，自滬瀆入海。

translations.literal: Jing could not control them; with several dozen trusted men in a single boat he fled alone, pushed his two sons into the water, and from Hudu outlet entered the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Jing could not hold them. With a few dozen trusted men in one boat he fled alone, threw his two sons into the water, and put to sea from Hudu outlet.

sentences.zh: 至壺豆洲，前太子舍人羊鯤殺之，送屍于王僧辯，傳首西臺，曝屍于建康市。

translations.literal: Reaching Hudou Isle, former Crown Prince Household Attendant Yang Kun killed him, sent the corpse to Wang Sengbian, forwarded the head to the Western Terrace, and exposed the body in Jiankang market.
translations.idiomatic: At Hudou Isle, former crown prince household attendant Yang Kun killed him, sent the body to Wang Sengbian, forwarded the head to the Western Terrace, and exposed the corpse in Jiankang market.

sentences.zh: 百姓爭取屠膾啖食，焚骨揚灰。

translations.literal: Commoners vied to butcher and slice it for food, burned the bones, and scattered the ash.
translations.idiomatic: The people fought to carve and eat his flesh, burned his bones, and scattered the ash.

sentences.zh: 曾罹其禍者，乃以灰和酒飲之。

translations.literal: Those who had once suffered his harm mixed the ash with wine and drank it.
translations.idiomatic: Those he had once harmed mixed the ash with wine and drank it down.

sentences.zh: 及景首至江陵，世祖命梟之於市，然後煮而漆之，付武庫。

translations.literal: When Jing's head reached Jiangling, Shizu ordered it displayed in the market, then boiled, lacquered, and sent to the armory.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing's head reached Jiangling, Shizu had it displayed in the market, then boiled, lacquered, and stored in the armory.

sentences.zh: 景長不滿七尺，而眉目疏秀。

translations.literal: Jing was less than seven feet tall, yet his brows and eyes were fine and handsome.
translations.idiomatic: Jing stood under seven feet, yet his brows and eyes were fine and handsome.

sentences.zh: 性猜忍，好殺戮。

translations.literal: By nature he was suspicious and cruel, fond of killing.
translations.idiomatic: He was suspicious and cruel by nature and loved killing.

sentences.zh: 刑人或先斬手足，割舌劓鼻，經日方死。

translations.literal: When punishing men he would first cut off hands and feet, slice out the tongue, and cut off the nose; only after a full day would they die.
translations.idiomatic: When he punished men he first cut off hands and feet, sliced out the tongue, and cut off the nose. They would not die until a full day had passed.

sentences.zh: 曾於石頭立大舂碓，有犯法者，皆搗殺之，其慘虐如此。

translations.literal: Once at Stone Fort he set up a great pounding mortar; whoever broke the law was pounded to death—his cruelty and savagery were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Stone Fort he erected a great pounding mortar. Every lawbreaker was pounded to death. His cruelty was like that.

sentences.zh: 自篡立後，時著白紗帽，而尚披青袍，或以牙梳插髻。

translations.literal: After usurping the throne he often wore a white gauze cap yet still draped a green robe, or stuck an ivory comb in his topknot.
translations.idiomatic: After seizing the throne he often wore a white gauze cap over a green robe, or stuck an ivory comb in his hair.

sentences.zh: 床上常設胡床及筌蹄，著靴垂腳坐。

translations.literal: On his bed he always kept a camp stool and a folding seat; wearing boots he sat with his legs hanging down.
translations.idiomatic: His bed always held a camp stool and a folding seat. Booted, he sat with his legs dangling.

sentences.zh: 或匹馬遊戲於宮內，及華林園彈射烏鳥。

translations.literal: Sometimes he rode alone sporting inside the palace, and at Hualin Garden shot at birds.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he sported alone on horseback inside the palace, or shot birds in Hualin Garden.

sentences.zh: 謀臣王偉不許輕出，於是鬱怏，更成失志。

translations.literal: His counselor Wang Wei would not allow him to go out lightly; he grew sullen and lost heart altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Counselor Wang Wei would not let him go out lightly. He grew sullen and lost heart.

sentences.zh: 所居殿常有鵂鶹鳥鳴，景惡之，每使人窮山野討捕焉。

translations.literal: Owls often cried in the hall where he lived; Jing hated it and constantly sent men to scour mountain and wild to hunt them down.
translations.idiomatic: Owls often cried in the hall where he lived. Jing hated it and constantly sent men to scour hills and wilds to catch them.

sentences.zh: 普通中，童謠曰：「青絲白馬壽陽來。

translations.literal: During the Putong era, a children's rhyme ran: "Green silk, white horse—Shouyang comes.
translations.idiomatic: In the Putong era a children's rhyme ran, "Green silk, white horse—Shouyang comes.

sentences.zh: 」後景果乘白馬，兵皆青衣。

translations.literal: " Later Jing indeed rode a white horse, and his soldiers all wore green.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Jing did ride a white horse, and his soldiers all wore green.

sentences.zh: 所乘馬，每戰將勝，輒躑躅嘶鳴，意氣駿逸，其奔衂，必低頭不前。

translations.literal: The horse he rode, whenever battle was about to go his way, would paw and neigh, spirited and swift; when he fled, it always hung its head and would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: His horse, whenever victory was near, would paw and neigh, fierce and swift. When he fled, it always hung its head and refused to go on.

sentences.zh: 初，中大同中，高祖嘗夜夢中原牧守皆以地來降，舉朝稱慶，寤甚悅之。

translations.literal: At first, in the Zhongdatong era, Gaozu once dreamed by night that governors of the central plains all came offering their lands in surrender; the whole court called it auspicious, and waking he was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Zhongdatong era, Gaozu dreamed one night that every governor of the central plains came offering land in surrender. The whole court called it auspicious, and he woke very pleased.

sentences.zh: 旦見中書舍人朱异說所夢，异曰：「此豈宇內方一，天道前見其徵乎？

translations.literal: At dawn he told Palace Secretariat Attendant Zhu Yi of the dream. Yi said: "Can this not mean the realm is becoming one under Heaven—that Heaven foreshows its sign?
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he told palace secretariat attendant Zhu Yi of the dream. Yi said, "Does this not mean the realm is becoming one—that Heaven shows its sign in advance?

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「吾爲人少夢，昨夜感此，良足慰懷。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "I rarely dream. Last night I felt this—it truly comforts the heart.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu said, "I rarely dream. Last night this came to me, and it truly comforts the heart.

sentences.zh: 」及太清二年，景果歸附，高祖欣然自悅，謂與神通，乃議納之，而意猶未決。

translations.literal: " In the second year of Taiqing, Jing indeed came to submit. Gaozu was glad of himself, thought it supernatural, debated receiving him, yet his mind was still unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: " In Taiqing year two Jing did come to submit. Gaozu was delighted, took it for a sign, and debated taking him in, but his mind was still unsettled.

sentences.zh: 曾夜出視事，至武德閣，獨言：「我家國猶若金甌，無一傷缺，今便受地，詎是事宜，脫致紛紜，非可悔也。

translations.literal: Once he went out at night to conduct affairs, reaching Wude Pavilion, and spoke alone: "My state is still like a golden bowl without a single chip—if we now accept territory, how can that be right? If disorder follows, there will be no undoing it.
translations.idiomatic: Once at night he went out to conduct affairs, reached Wude Pavilion, and said alone, "My realm is still a golden bowl without a chip. To accept territory now—how can that be right? If trouble follows, it cannot be undone.

sentences.zh: 」朱异接聲而對曰：「聖明御宇，上應蒼玄，北土遺黎，誰不慕仰？

translations.literal: " Zhu Yi answered in immediate reply: "The sage illumines the realm, above matching the azure dark; the remnant folk of the north—who does not look up in longing?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu Yi answered at once, "The sage rules the realm, matching Heaven above. Who among the remnant folk of the north does not look up in longing?

sentences.zh: 爲無機會，未達其心。

translations.literal: Without opportunity, their hearts could not be known.
translations.idiomatic: Without opportunity, their hearts could not be known.

sentences.zh: 今侯景據河南十餘州，分魏土之半，輸誠送款，遠歸聖朝，豈非天誘其衷，人獎其計？

translations.literal: Now Hou Jing holds more than ten provinces south of the Yellow River, half of Wei territory, renders sincerity and sends pledges, and comes from afar to the holy court—is this not Heaven guiding his inmost heart, men applauding his plan?
translations.idiomatic: Now Hou Jing holds more than ten provinces south of the Yellow River, half of Wei's land, renders loyalty and sends pledges, and comes from afar to the holy court. Is this not Heaven guiding his heart and men applauding his plan?

sentences.zh: 原心審事，殊有可嘉。

translations.literal: Reading his intent and weighing the matter, there is much to praise.
translations.idiomatic: Reading his intent and weighing the matter, there is much to praise.

sentences.zh: 今若拒而不容，恐絕後來之望，此誠易見，願陛下無疑。

translations.literal: If you now refuse and do not accept him, I fear later arrivals will lose hope. This is easy to see—your Majesty need not doubt.
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse him now, I fear later comers will lose hope. That is easy to see. Your Majesty need not doubt.

sentences.zh: 」高祖深納異言，又信前夢，乃定議納景。

translations.literal: " Gaozu deeply took up Yi's words, trusted the earlier dream as well, and decided to receive Jing.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu took Yi's words to heart, trusted the earlier dream as well, and decided to receive Jing.

sentences.zh: 及貞陽覆敗，邊鎮恇擾，高祖固已憂之，曰：「吾今段如此，勿作晉家事乎？」

translations.literal: When Zhenyang was overthrown in defeat and border garrisons panicked, Gaozu was already worried, saying: "I am now like this—are we not doing Jin's business?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenyang fell and the border garrisons panicked, Gaozu was already worried. He said, "I am like this now—are we not repeating Jin's fate?"

sentences.zh: 先是，丹陽陶弘景隱於華陽山，博學多識，嘗爲詩曰：「夷甫任散誕，平叔坐談空。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tao Hongjing of Danyang, living in seclusion on Mount Hua, learned and widely knowing, once composed a poem: "Yi Fu lived in idle dissipation; Ping Shu sat discoursing on emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tao Hongjing of Danyang, living in seclusion on Mount Hua, learned and widely read, once wrote a poem: "Yi Fu lived in idle dissipation; Ping Shu sat discoursing on emptiness.

sentences.zh: 不意昭陽殿，化作單于宮。

translations.literal: Who would have thought Zhaoyang Hall would become a Xiongnu palace.
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought Zhaoyang Hall would become a Xiongnu palace.

sentences.zh: 」大同末，人士競談玄理，不習武事；

translations.literal: " At the end of Datong, gentlemen rivaled one another in discussing arcane principle and did not practice military affairs;
translations.idiomatic: " At the end of Datong, gentlemen rivaled one another in discussing arcane principle and did not practice military affairs;

sentences.zh: 至是，景果居昭陽殿。

translations.literal: now Jing indeed occupied Zhaoyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Now Jing did occupy Zhaoyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 天監中，有釋寶志曰：「掘尾狗子自發狂，當死未死齧人傷，須臾之間自滅亡，起自汝陰死三湘。

translations.literal: During the Tianjian era, the monk Baozhi said: "The tail-digging dog goes mad by itself; when due to die yet not dead it bites and wounds men; in a moment it perishes of itself—rising from Ruyin it dies in the Three Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianjian era the monk Baozhi said, "The tail-digging dog goes mad by itself. When it should die but does not, it bites and wounds men. In a moment it perishes—rising from Ruyin, dying in the Three Xiang.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「山家小兒果攘臂，太極殿前作虎視。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The mountain man's child indeed flings up his sleeves, at the front of Taiji Hall making a tiger's stare.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "The mountain man's child flings up his sleeves and at the front of Taiji Hall stares like a tiger.

sentences.zh: 」掘尾狗子、山家小兒，皆猴狀。

translations.literal: " "Tail-digging dog" and "mountain man's child" both suggest a monkey's form.
translations.idiomatic: " "Tail-digging dog" and "mountain man's child" both suggest a monkey's shape.

sentences.zh: 景遂覆陷都邑，毒害皇室。

translations.literal: Jing then overthrew and seized the capital, poisoning the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Jing then overthrew the capital and poisoned the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 大同中，太醫令朱躭嘗直禁省，無何，夜夢犬羊各一在御坐，覺而惡之，告人曰：「犬羊者，非佳物也。

translations.literal: During Datong, Court Physician Zhu Zhan once attended the forbidden precinct. Before long, by night he dreamed a dog and a sheep each on the imperial seat; waking, he hated it and told others: "Dog and sheep—neither is an auspicious thing.
translations.idiomatic: During Datong, court physician Zhu Zhan attended the forbidden precinct. One night he dreamed a dog and a sheep each on the imperial seat. Waking, he hated it and told others, "Dog and sheep are no good omen.

sentences.zh: 今據御坐，將有變乎？

translations.literal: Now occupying the imperial seat—will there be upheaval?
translations.idiomatic: Now on the imperial seat—will there be upheaval?

sentences.zh: 」旣而天子蒙塵，景登正殿焉。

translations.literal: " Before long the Son of Heaven suffered exile in the dust, and Jing ascended the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long the Son of Heaven suffered exile in the dust, and Jing ascended the main hall.

sentences.zh: 及景將敗，有僧通道人者，意性若狂，飲酒噉肉，不異凡等，世間遊行已數十載，姓名鄉里，人莫能知。

translations.literal: When Jing was about to fall, there was a monk called Tong whose mind seemed half mad; he drank wine and ate meat no differently from ordinary men. He had wandered the world for several decades—name, home, and village, none could know.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was about to fall, there was a monk called Tong whose mind seemed half mad. He drank wine and ate meat like any ordinary man. He had wandered the world for decades, and no one knew his name or home.

sentences.zh: 初言隱伏，久乃方驗，人並呼爲闍梨，景甚信敬之。

translations.literal: At first his words were hidden; only after long delay were they verified. All called him acarya, and Jing trusted and honored him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: At first his words were obscure; only long afterward were they verified. All called him acarya, and Jing trusted and honored him deeply.

sentences.zh: 景嘗於後堂與其徒共射，時僧通在坐，奪景弓射景陽山，大呼云「得奴已」。

translations.literal: Jing once in the rear hall shot with his followers; Monk Tong was present, seized Jing's bow, and shot at Jingyang Hill, shouting, "Got the slave!"
translations.idiomatic: Jing once shot with his followers in the rear hall. Monk Tong was there, seized Jing's bow, and shot at Jingyang Hill, shouting, "Got the slave!"

sentences.zh: 景後又宴集其黨，又召僧通。

translations.literal: Later Jing again feasted his faction and summoned Monk Tong once more.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jing feasted his faction again and summoned Monk Tong once more.

sentences.zh: 僧通取肉揾鹽以進景，問曰：「好不？

translations.literal: Monk Tong took meat dipped in salt and presented it to Jing, asking: "Good?
translations.idiomatic: Monk Tong took meat dipped in salt and offered it to Jing, asking, "Good?

sentences.zh: 」景答：「所恨太咸。

translations.literal: " Jing answered: "My only regret is it is too salty.
translations.idiomatic: " Jing answered, "My only regret is it is too salty.

sentences.zh: 」僧通曰：「不鹹則爛臭。

translations.literal: " Monk Tong said: "Without salt it rots and stinks.
translations.idiomatic: " Monk Tong said, "Without salt it rots and stinks.

sentences.zh: 」果以鹽封其屍。

translations.literal: " Indeed his corpse was sealed with salt.
translations.idiomatic: " Indeed his corpse was sealed with salt.

sentences.zh: 王偉，陳留人。

translations.literal: Wang Wei was a man of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei came from Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 少有才學，景之表、啓、書、檄，皆其所制。

translations.literal: In youth he had talent in letters; Jing's memorials, reports, letters, and proclamations were all composed by him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had literary talent. Jing's memorials, reports, letters, and proclamations were all his work.

sentences.zh: 景旣得志，規摹篡奪，皆偉之謀。

translations.literal: Once Jing had achieved his ambition, the planning and pattern of usurpation were all Wei's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jing had his way, every plan for usurpation was Wei's counsel.

sentences.zh: 及囚送江陵，烹於市，百姓有遭其毒者，並割炙食之。

translations.literal: When he was bound and sent to Jiangling, he was boiled in the market; commoners who had suffered his poison all sliced and roasted his flesh to eat.
translations.idiomatic: When he was bound and sent to Jiangling, he was boiled in the market. Commoners who had suffered his poison sliced and roasted his flesh to eat.

translations.literal: Commentary section marker in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: Marker denoting the historian's commentary section in the source text.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫道不恒夷，運無常泰，斯則窮通有數，盛衰相襲，時屯陽九，蓋在茲焉。

translations.literal: The historian says: The Way is not always level; fortune is not always secure—thus success and failure have measure, prosperity and decline succeed one another; the age stalls in yang's ninth calamity—this lies here.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The Way is not always smooth; fortune is not always secure. Rise and fall have their measure, prosperity and decline follow in turn. The age stalls in yang's ninth calamity—and that is here.

sentences.zh: 若乃侯景小豎，叛換本國，識不周身，勇非出類，而王偉爲其謀主，成此姦慝。

translations.literal: As for the petty wretch Hou Jing—rebellious and disloyal to his own state, insight not reaching his person, courage not exceeding the norm—yet Wang Wei was his chief strategist and accomplished this wicked treachery.
translations.idiomatic: As for the petty wretch Hou Jing—rebellious to his own state, insight not reaching his person, courage nothing out of the ordinary—Wang Wei was his chief strategist and made this wicked treachery possible.

sentences.zh: 驅率醜徒，陵江直濟，長戟強弩，淪覆宮闕，禍纏宸極，毒遍黎元，肆其恣睢之心，成其篡盜之禍。

translations.literal: Driving ugly followers, crossing the river directly eastward, long halberds and strong crossbows, overthrowing palace and tower, disaster entwining the supreme throne, poison spread through the common folk, indulging his arbitrary heart, completing his usurping treachery.
translations.idiomatic: He drove ugly followers straight across the river, long halberds and strong crossbows overturning palace and tower, disaster coiling around the throne, poison spreading through the people, indulging his will to the full, completing his usurping crime.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 國之將亡，必降妖孽。

translations.literal: When a state is about to perish, monsters and freaks descend.
translations.idiomatic: When a state is about to perish, monsters and freaks descend.

sentences.zh: 雖曰人事，抑乃天時。

translations.literal: Though called human affairs, yet it is Heaven's timing.
translations.idiomatic: Though men call it human affairs, it is Heaven's timing.

sentences.zh: 昔夷羿亂夏，犬戎厄周，漢則莽、卓流災，晉則敦、玄構禍，方之羯賊，有逾其酷，悲夫！

translations.literal: In old times Yi of Xia brought chaos to Xia, the Quan Rong threatened Zhou; under Han, Wang Mang and Dong Zhuo spread disaster; under Jin, Wang Dun and Huan Xuan engineered calamity—compared with the Jie bandit, this exceeded their cruelty. Alas!
translations.idiomatic: In old times Yi of Xia brought chaos to Xia and the Quan Rong threatened Zhou. Under Han, Wang Mang and Dong Zhuo spread disaster; under Jin, Wang Dun and Huan Xuan engineered calamity. Compared with the Jie bandit, this was crueller still. Alas!
